sound-direction picked C

What is being decided

Brief: sound direction

Question being decided

Which sonic character should the game's synthesised audio have? The customer asked for "nice sound and graphics" and "generate what you need" (addendum in ../../00-brief.md); the proxy answer to Q5 (../../circles/circle-01.md) chose procedural sound effects plus a generative ambient loop per zone with volume sliders (../../30-spec/08-audio.md). Nothing may be a recorded file or a third-party sample (NFR-L01): every sound is built at runtime with Web Audio. The choice fixes the synthesis toolbox, the mixing rules, the CPU budget and the look-and-feel promise of the audio, so it is cheaper to decide before slice S3.

Reviewers cannot listen, so each board has a measurement mode (below) and the decision should still be made by ear.

Requirements involved

  • R-080 sound effects for core actions (attack, hit, death, pickup, UI click, level up, potion; QF-08-1 asks about miss, monster attacks and stairs, which all boards cover)
  • R-081 generative ambient per zone (lobby, open-plan floors, basement)
  • R-082 master, effects and ambient sliders plus mute (all three boards have them, wired to kit.setVolume and kit.setMuted)
  • NFR-L01 no third-party assets: no audio files, no samples, no fetches
  • NFR performance (CPU-cheap voices; see "Budget")
  • QF-08-4 "nice sound" bar: this topic is the listening gate, with the numbers below as a safety net

What all three variants share

  • One file per variant (A.html, B.html, C.html), inline CSS and JS, opened from disk, in the C2 visual style (dark indigo panels, gold trim, teal buttons, cyan highlights).
  • The same 27 sound buttons: hero swing (stapler-mace), hit flesh, hit paper, miss; hurt and death for zombie intern, printer imp and middle manager; hero hurt, low-health heartbeat (one beat pair; the game repeats it), potion (coffee slurp); gold coins, item pickup, rare sparkle, unique sparkle, level-up fanfare; Stapler Throw, Reply-All burst, Coffee Break heal, Mute; UI click, open drawer, equip, stairs, elevator ding.
  • Three ambient loops, one at a time: open-plan floors (fluorescent hum, distant printer, HVAC), basement (server fans, drips, low drones), lobby (muffled elevator-music-like pad, safe and warm). They are continuous generative beds (sustained oscillators and noise plus seeded random events), so there is no loop seam by construction (AC-R-081-3).
  • Master, effects and ambient sliders, a mute switch, and a live waveform and spectrum view. Browsers need a gesture, so the first button press starts audio.
  • A liftable createSoundKit(ctx, destination[, {seed}]) section (marked in each file), pure Web Audio and no DOM: kit.play(id, when), kit.startAmbient(zone, when[, {duration}]), kit.setVolume(bus, 0..1), kit.setMuted(bool). Chain: voice -> effects or ambient bus -> master -> compressor (20:1, -4 dB threshold) -> soft ceiling at 0.97 -> destination. Every sound has a calibrated trim.
  • Noise is seeded and generated once per context, so renders are repeatable (AC-R-080-2 style).

Budget (same rules for all)

Short SFX at most 1 s, at most about 12 Web Audio nodes per SFX, no clipping, peaks between -6 and -1 dBFS, ambient RMS between -30 and -20 dBFS, RMS spread across SFX at most 12 dB.

How to view and measure

  • Open A.html, B.html or C.html and press buttons.
  • ?measure=1 renders every SFX (1.7 s window) and 10 s of every ambient through an OfflineAudioContext (44.1 kHz stereo, all volumes at 1.0) and writes window.__report, then sets window.__ready. Per sound: duration, peak dBFS, RMS dBFS, crest factor, spectral centroid (2048-point FFT, Hann), clipping count, and for SFX the node count and render time. The report also carries a method string and a summary with the pass checks. The saved runs are measure-A.json, measure-B.json, measure-C.json (Playwright, Chromium).
  • Duration is measured to the last sample above -50 dBFS, so it includes any reverb tail. Peak and clipping cover the whole render; SFX RMS and centroid cover the active window; ambient RMS and centroid cover seconds 1 to 10.
  • Per-sound trims were set by a calibration pass (target RMS about -16 to -17 dBFS, peak limited to -5.2..-2.2 dBFS) and are stored in the kit; the numbers therefore say the mix is consistent, not that the sounds are pleasant.
Notes per variant

Notes: sound direction

All numbers come from the saved measure-*.json (offline render, Chromium, 2026-10-13). Measurements show level, length, brightness and cost; they cannot judge taste, so the pick must be made by ear.

Measurement summary

A Gothic officeB Retro chiptuneC Foley-synth
SFX peak range (target -6..-1)-2.8 to -2.2-5.2 to -2.1-5.2 to -2.2
SFX RMS range, spread (target spread at most 12 dB)-25.8 to -17.0, 8.8 dB-16.0 to -11.0, 5.0 dB-24.5 to -16.2, 8.3 dB
Ambient RMS (target -30..-20)-25.0 all three-25.0 all three-25.0 all three
Clipping samples (SFX / ambient)0 / 00 / 00 / 0
Longest SFX incl. tail (target at most 1 s)0.999 s0.906 s0.963 s
Most nodes in one SFX (target about 12)121112
Slowest offline render, SFX / 10 s ambient71 ms / 201 ms20 ms / 101 ms41 ms / 202 ms
All checks passyesyesyes

Ambient RMS sits at exactly -25 because the trims were calibrated to it. B is the loudest on average (square waves have a low crest factor, 5.7 to 13.6 dB against 14.2 to 23.6 dB for A and 11 to 22 dB for C), so at equal slider positions B will feel louder than A and C even though the peaks match.

A Gothic office

  • Character: dark and heavy. Sub-bass thumps, saw-through-formant growls for the monsters, minor-key bells and a D minor drone under every floor, all pushed through a feedback-delay room (four parallel combs, RT60 about 0.4 s). Closest to the moody genre classic: impacts feel big and the basement is oppressive; the lobby pad is the only warm place.
  • Fit with C2: C2 is a stylised, saturated vector look in indigo and teal with gold trim; the sound is darker and more serious than the picture, so the two pull in different directions (funny office, grim audio). That contrast can read as dry humour, or as a mismatch.
  • Risks: reverb tails make the SFX run right up to the 1 s limit (0.999 s, only 1 ms spare), so any change that lengthens a sound needs a re-measure; heavy low end is lost on laptop speakers, so thumps may sound thin; constant reverb in busy fights can smear. Five sounds sit at the 12-node ceiling.
  • CPU: shared room is 18 nodes always on; SFX 7 to 12 nodes, one ambient bed roughly 15 to 40 live nodes (estimated from the code). Slowest offline render 71 ms for one SFX including setup; 201 ms for 10 s of ambient.
  • Effort: M (voice and room tuning, tails per sound).

B Retro chiptune

  • Character: punchy, dry, playful. Pulse waves at 12.5, 25 and 50 percent duty, triangle bass and a stepped noise channel, with 6-to-10 step decays like a console sound chip. Fanfares are arpeggios, deaths are falling pitch slides; ambient beds are quiet triangle arpeggios and noise hiss.
  • Fit with C2: the cheerful, outlined, saturated look suits it, and the office-gone-wrong comedy comes through (coin blips, "pew" skills). It undersells the moody lighting (the dark vignette and flickering fluorescent) and the genre classic's heavy feel; ambient reads as game-music rather than atmosphere.
  • Risks: it commits the whole game to a retro-pixel sound identity while the art is smooth vector; square waves are tiring at length and loud for their peak (RMS about 6 dB above the others at equal peak); brightness is high (centroids 1.0 to 10.8 kHz) so it can sound harsh on headphones; ambient stays "musical" instead of spooky.
  • CPU: cheapest. SFX 3 to 11 nodes (most 5 to 7), no room, 10 s ambient renders in about 100 ms. Safest for low-end laptops and for many simultaneous voices in a crowded fight.
  • Effort: S to M (the toolbox is small and the sounds are short note tables).

C Foley-synth

  • Character: realistic-ish and tactile. Filtered-noise whooshes and slaps, FM clicks and ticks (stapler, UI, equip), inharmonic FM chimes for coins and sparkles, formant voices for monsters, a small room from four short feedback delays (RT60 under 0.3 s) and tonal ambient beds (mains hum with beating, fan noise with a blade tone, drips, soft electric-piano pad in the lobby).
  • Fit with C2: sits in between. It supports the office setting (paper, staplers, coffee, plastic clicks) and the comedy of everyday objects turned into weapons, and it keeps the dark-room mood of the C2 lighting without pushing it to gothic. Closest to a real "office as dungeon" soundscape.
  • Risks: hardest to make sound convincing and the most likely to sound "cheap synth" next to real recordings; many quiet sounds (hit paper, stapler, equip) are transient-heavy, so their RMS is low and they may feel weak next to growls; eight sounds at the 12-node ceiling (FM voices cost four nodes each). Needs listening time to tune.
  • CPU: moderate. SFX 5 to 12 nodes (FM voices use four nodes each); same 18-node room as A; offline render 41 ms worst SFX and 202 ms for 10 s of ambient.
  • Effort: M to L (the most tuning, and the sound design is the part the customer will judge).

Cross-cutting notes

  • Loudness consistency is achieved by a per-sound trim table baked into each kit; adding a sound means one calibration run.
  • All three kits are lifted unchanged into the game by copying the marked section; the game then calls kit.play(id) from its cue events (the cue ids attack, hit, death, pickup, uiClick, levelUp, potion of AC-R-080-3 map to swing, hitFlesh, deathZombie and the other death ids, coin, uiClick, levelUp, potion).
  • A hybrid is possible (for example C's foley for impacts and UI, A's drones and room for the basement), but it costs effort and a decision is cheaper now.
Decision

Decision: sound direction

Status: provisional default (PROXY), final pick by the real customer by ear

Picked (provisional default, PROXY, confidence low to medium): C Foley-synth. All three kits still ship, selectable in Options (audio.kit).

Notes from the human (optional): listen on both headphones and laptop speakers, with an ambient running, and say if a hybrid is wanted.

Orchestrator note (2026-10-13)

Taste needs ears (learning L-14). The game ships all three kits behind one interface, selectable in Options (audio.kit). The customer-proxy sets the provisional default. The real customer is asked to listen to A.html, B.html and C.html (headphones and laptop speakers, with an ambient running) and pick the default.

Proxy decision (2026-10-13)

PROXY (confidence low to medium): default kit is C Foley-synth. The proxy cannot listen; this rests on the customer's words, the frozen C2 style, the notes and measurements, and a read of each kit's synthesis code. A is the close second; B is last.

Reasons

  1. "Stay close to the original" (moody genre classic) rules out B as default: chiptune pulse waves and arpeggio ambients read as game music, not atmosphere (notes.md), and B commits an outlined smooth-vector game to a retro-pixel identity. B is also about 6 dB louder at equal sliders and bright (centroids up to 10.8 kHz), tiring on headphones.
  2. C keeps the dark-room mood without going gothic: noise whooshes and slaps, FM clicks, a short room (RT60 under 0.3 s), tonal ambients (mains hum with beating, fan blade tone, drips). That matches the dark-graded C2 look and its slightly playful office humour (everyday objects turned weapons), where A's grim sub-bass and D minor drones pull against the picture.
  3. Robust on a likely listening setup: the customer plays on a laptop. A's weight sits in sub-bass thumps that laptop speakers lose (notes.md), so it may sound thin exactly where it should impress. C's content is mid and high, with transient-heavy sounds that survive small speakers.
  4. Headroom: C's longest SFX is 0.963 s with a short room, so fights stay readable; A runs to 0.999 s with long reverb tails that smear busy fights and leave 1 ms spare. All checks pass for all three, so the numbers do not separate them except on tails and cost.
  5. Cost and effort are similar to A (moderate CPU, M to L tuning). Risk accepted: C is the most likely to sound "cheap synth"; its quiet sounds (hit paper, stapler, equip) need a listening pass.

What to keep from the others

  • From A: the basement ambient (server drones, oppression) and the heavier monster growls as the first candidates for a hybrid if the customer finds C too light. A hybrid is not planned now; the Options switch covers a full change.
  • From B: its sparse, dry punch for UI blips is not needed; keep only its discipline on voice count and CPU.

Switch conditions (for the real customer): if "moody" outranks "readable" when listening, pick A (note that this is the same trade as the art pick). Pick B only if the customer wants a deliberate retro feel, which conflicts with "stay close to the original".

Answers to the prototyper's open questions

  • Separate cues vs merged: separate. Miss, monster attack (hurt/death per monster) and stairs keep their own ids (QF-08-1 as should, already in all kits, 27 sounds). Merging would cost little in code but lose readable combat feedback, and the per-sound trims already exist. If the budget forces cuts, merge the three monsters' hurt sounds first, not miss or stairs.
  • Title-screen ambient (QF-08-2): yes, soft. Play the lobby bed (the safe, warm one) at the ambient slider's default, started by the first gesture, fading out when a zone ambient starts. No music track. Consistent with the earlier proxy answer to QF-08-2. Default volumes stay master 0.6, effects 0.8, ambient 0.5 (QF-08-3, low confidence; B would need lower values).

ESCALATE: none. The final kit pick is the real customer's, by ear.

To pick: tell Claude "pick sound-direction variant X because …", or edit variants/sound-direction/decision.md.

QF-11-9 Skill panel key S/K vs other keys

If a conflict appears with a later keyboard-movement option, K stays and S yields. Basis: spec-questions-01.md QF-01-3, QF-01-4.

spec-questions-01

Spec questions 01: answers to "Questions for the facilitator"

Date: 2026-10-13. Answerer: customer-proxy, under the delegation record in 00-brief.md. Source: the "Questions for the facilitator" sections of 30-spec/01 to 30-spec/10. All answers are PROXY and provisional until the real customer reviews them (proxy-log.md). Tie-breaker used where the customer's words are silent: "stay close to the original" for mechanics (brief, verbatim), read as the genre classic's conventions, never its names or assets. Answers do not change any earlier customer or proxy answer (circle-01 Q2-Q7); where one touches an earlier answer it says so.

Answer format: PROXY (confidence) / basis. "ESCALATE" = needs the real customer.

01 Core loop and controls

QF-01-1 Town stairs: floor 1 or deepest reached floor?

PROXY (high): The town stairs lead down to the deepest reached floor, via an elevator in the Lobby. This is the genre's waypoint idea, re-expressed in office terms. A first-time player has "deepest reached = 1". config.townStairsTarget = 'deepest'. Basis: R-004 ("come back to the deepest reached floor"); genre convention (waypoint / return to depth); circle-01 Q7 (short sessions).

QF-01-2 Click on an unreachable tile (wall)?

PROXY (medium): The player walks to the nearest reachable tile to the click, as the genre classic did. noPath is raised only when no tile closer than the current one is reachable. Basis: genre convention (brief: stay close to the original; customer's words silent).

QF-01-3 Skill panel key: S, K or both?

PROXY (medium): Both bound by default (S and K open the skill panel). Basis: spec proposal; costs nothing; customer silent.

QF-01-4 Collision of skill hotkeys 1-4 and belt potions 1-4

PROXY (high): Resolved as the genre classic did. Belt potions on keys 1-4. Skills on the mouse: left button = move/attack, right button = the currently selected skill. A skill selector assigns four skills to hotkeys F1-F4 (default; rebindable); pressing F1-F4 selects the skill that the right mouse button then uses. The game calls preventDefault for F1-F4 so the browser's own function keys do not fire. R-005's "hotkeys for skills (1-4)" is read as "four skill hotkeys", not the number row. Basis: brief "stay close to the original" (mechanics); R-005 "skills on mouse buttons"; R-056 (belt 1-4); no conflict with circle-01 answers. Consequence: AC-R-015-3 uses F1-F4.

QF-01-5 R-006 "meaningful in 20-40 minutes"

PROXY (medium): Accept as a release-gate measurement, not an AC: the playtest bot reaches the boss in 20-40 minutes of simulated time (tick / tickHz) on seed 1, after a balance pass. Basis: circle-01 Q7 (answer A, 20-40 min run); the measurement is the proxy's way to make Q7 testable.

QF-01-6 Rebinding collision

PROXY (medium): Reject with a notice (ui.notice), options.keys unchanged; the player must free the key first. Basis: spec proposal; safest for accessibility (NFR-A01); the genre classic is not clear on this and the customer is silent.

02 Combat

QF-02-1 Hit chance formula and clamp

PROXY (medium): Owned by the architect (ADR). Genre-style guidance: chance depends on attacker rating against defender defence and level, clamped to a floor and ceiling (recommended 5% to 95%, as in the genre). Values live in config. The spec asserts monotonicity and bounds only. Basis: genre convention; customer silent.

QF-02-2 Respawn with full health and mana?

PROXY (high): Yes, the player respawns in town with full health and mana, no gold loss. Basis: circle-01 Q7 answer A ("moderately forgiving, death returns to town with no gold loss").

QF-02-3 Dying with an item on the cursor

PROXY (medium): The item returns to the inventory; if the inventory is full it drops at the death tile on the floor (retrievable per QF-04-6). It is never destroyed. Basis: spec proposal; Q7 forgiving.

QF-02-4 Natural regeneration

PROXY (low): Genre feel: no natural health regeneration on floors; slow natural mana regeneration, rate in config and tunable by playtest. Full restore of health on the healer (QF-04-2). Both resources are refilled on respawn. Basis: genre convention (customer silent); to be reviewed after playtest.

QF-02-5 "Feel" criteria (animation, readability)

PROXY (high): Accept screenshot review by the independent visual reviewer as the gate. Basis: circle-01 Q2 (art quality via independent visual review).

03 Monsters and AI

QF-03-1 Final monster names

PROXY (medium) for working names; ESCALATE for final names. ACs test working names. All names must be original and pass the IP denylist (QF-10-2). Final names, as part of the product's naming and brand, are for the real customer. Basis: R-030 "open to the user"; IP/branding is not delegated.

QF-03-2 Which archetypes flee, at what health?

PROXY (medium): The small/weak melee archetypes of the swarm kind flee below 25% health, regroup, and return after a delay (a genre convention). Ranged and caster types and bosses never flee. Exact threshold and archetype mapping in config, set by the spec-writer within this rule. Basis: genre convention.

QF-03-3 Leash and losing interest

PROXY (medium): Monsters lose interest when the player is farther than twice their aggro radius for a set time (config), then walk back to their origin and idle. Basis: genre convention; R-032 needs no break in behaviour.

QF-03-4 "Better drops" for champions

PROXY (medium): Accept the proposal: a champion's drops are at least magic rarity (guaranteed); the mean-rarity AC stays. Basis: spec proposal.

QF-03-5 Safe radius around the entry stair

PROXY (high): Add as a requirement: no monster spawns within a safe radius of the entry stair (radius in config, suggested 8 tiles). Basis: genre convention and fairness (Q7 "forgiving").

QF-03-6 Archetype to behaviour mapping, availability by zone

PROXY (low): Delegated to the spec-writer and architect within these limits: 6 to 8 archetypes; each of the 3 behaviours used by at least two archetypes; zone 1 (floors 1-4) has about half of them, zone 2 (floors 5-8) adds the rest and keeps some of zone 1 at higher level. Not a customer-facing decision. Basis: R-031; customer silent.

04 World and floors

QF-04-1 Spawning hostiles in town via cheat

PROXY (high): Cheats reject it, keeping "no hostiles in town" an invariant (AC-R-040-5). Basis: spec proposal; R-040.

QF-04-2 Healer cost and mana

PROXY (medium): Free, restores health only; mana comes from potions and regeneration. Basis: R-041 text ("restores health"); genre convention (free healer).

QF-04-3 Potion seller stock by player level

PROXY (medium): Unlimited stock; potion strength tiers unlock by player level (for example minor, normal, greater, with the thresholds in config). Values owned as in QF-05-7. Basis: genre convention.

QF-04-4 Zone boundary and room-kind mapping

PROXY (medium): Accept the spec's proposal as in AC-R-101-2. Floors 1-4 are zone 1, floors 5-8 zone 2; the boss arena has its own tileset. Basis: R-043, R-101; circle-01 Q3.

QF-04-5 Boss on floor 8 or a ninth arena

PROXY (high): The boss gets its own final area, as in the genre classic: a boss arena reached from floor 8 by a stair. The 8 floors and 2 zones of circle-01 Q3 are unchanged; the arena is the ninth location and is not counted among the 8. config.bossDepth = 9 (arena). R-045's wording "boss on the last floor" is to be amended to "in the final area after floor 8". Basis: circle-01 Q3 (8 floors, 1 end boss with 2 phases), genre convention; no conflict with the earlier answer.

QF-04-6 Ground items on a re-entered floor

PROXY (medium): Within a running session, layout, cleared monsters and ground items persist while the player moves between town and floors (as in the genre classic; forgiving per Q7). Across save and reload nothing mid-floor is restored (circle-01 Q4, option A). AC-R-044-2 changes from "lost" to "still there (same session)". Basis: genre convention; circle-01 Q4 and Q7.

QF-04-7 "Guaranteed good loot" minimum

PROXY (medium): The boss drops at least 3 items, each rare or better. Values config.boss.guaranteedDrops = 3, config.boss.minRarity = rare. Basis: genre convention; R-045.

QF-04-8 Where the player stands after "keep playing"

PROXY (medium): In town. The boss stays dead; the elevator target remains the deepest reached floor. Basis: genre convention (return to hub); R-004.

QF-04-9 Boss reset on death

PROXY (medium): If the player dies or leaves the arena before the boss is dead, the boss resets to full health and phase 1. Basis: genre convention; fairness.

QF-04-10 Lobby sub-areas

PROXY (high): Accept reception and breakroom as working sub-area names (generic words, not IP). Basis: spec proposal.

QF-04-11 Visual identity of town and tilesets

PROXY (high): Decided by the art-direction variant pick; accepted by independent visual review. Basis: circle-01 Q2.

05 Items and loot

QF-05-1 Container kinds

PROXY (medium): Two kinds per floor: breakable "supply crates" (gold, potions) and openable "filing cabinets" (items, better chance). Count per floor in config (suggested 4 to 10, by room size). Basis: R-050; genre convention (barrels and chests, re-expressed).

QF-05-2 Unique item dropping twice

PROXY (low): A unique drops at most once per game; a roll that would repeat a taken unique falls back to a rare of the same base. Basis: genre convention; flag for review since the spec proposed "may drop again".

QF-05-3 "Same stat group" for affix exclusion

PROXY (medium): The group is the affix's primary stat family (for example all tiers of +strength are one group, all +fire resist another). The architect lists the groups in config; an item never has two affixes of the same group. Basis: R-051; genre convention.

QF-05-4 Two-handed weapons

PROXY (medium): Yes, a few. A two-handed weapon occupies the weapon and off-hand slots; equipping one returns the off-hand item to the inventory, and is refused (with a notice) when the inventory has no room. Basis: genre convention.

QF-05-5 Potion at full health

PROXY (low): As the genre classic did, the potion is consumed (and wasted). Behind config.consumePotionAtFull so it is a one-line change if playtest shows accidental waste. Basis: genre convention; flagged because Q7 asks for "forgiving", so the real customer may prefer "refused".

QF-05-6 Selling equipped items

PROXY (high): Only inventory items can be sold; unequip first. Basis: spec proposal; genre convention.

QF-05-7 Balance table owner (drop chances, rarity weights, prices, potion values)

PROXY (high): The architect and implementer own it. All balance values live in a single config module, tuned by the playtest bots (QF-01-5). The customer sets only the feel targets already given (20-40 minutes, forgiving). Basis: customer's earlier answers delegate mechanics to "stay close to the original"; Q7.

QF-05-8 Item label and icon readability

PROXY (high): Visual review item, not an AC. Basis: circle-01 Q2.

06 Character and progression

QF-06-1 Class selection screen with one class

PROXY (medium): No selection step; the character-creation screen shows the single class and asks for a character name only. Final class name: working name now, final naming is ESCALATE with the other names (QF-03-1). Basis: circle-01 Q3 (1 class).

QF-06-2 XP at level cap

PROXY (medium): XP keeps counting for display up to config.xpPastCap; level, attribute points and skill points no longer change. Basis: genre convention.

QF-06-3 XP for non-player kills

PROXY (medium): List, no prerequisites, for the four actives in the MVP. A tree is for later with more classes. Basis: circle-01 Q3 (1 class).

QF-06-8 Starting attributes, gold, gear, base values, per-level gains

PROXY (medium): config values owned as in QF-05-7. Guidance: one starting weapon, two health potions, small starting gold. Basis: genre convention.

Real brand and company names are also covered by the denylist in QF-10-2. Basis: R-103; customer silent. This is a content-quality rule, not an IP decision.

QF-07-5 Colour-blind delta E threshold

PROXY (medium): Accept the spec's proposal. Basis: NFR-A03; technical value, reviewable later.

QF-08-1 Sounds for miss, monster attack, stairs

PROXY (medium): Yes, add all three as "should" cues. Basis: circle-01 Q5 answer A ("nice sound").

QF-08-2 Title screen audio

PROXY (medium): A soft generative title ambient, started after the first user gesture (browser rule), with the same mute and volume controls. Basis: Q5 answer A.

This is a gate outside the automated suite. The real customer's own ear is the final judge on return. Basis: addendum "nice sound" (agreed customer statement).

10 Tech and testability

QF-10-1 Performance targets

PROXY (medium): Accept a CI reference measurement (headless Chromium, software rendering) as a relative regression check: the 95th-percentile frame time of 33.3 ms and the 4 ms sim-step budget are limits for that runner, compared with the stored baseline, not absolute guarantees. The goal "60 fps on a mid-range laptop" is stated as the target, checked by manual release checks. NFR-P03 to P05 stay "should", unspecified. Basis: NFR-P01-P05 (assumed); circle-01 readiness item 6; customer silent.

QF-10-2 Who supplies the denylists

PROXY (medium) that the mechanism is within the delegation; IP closeness itself remains ESCALATED (circle-01 Q1). A denylist of the original's trademarks is only the enforcement of the already-applied safe default A (strict originality). Proposal: the orchestrator maintains one file docs/product/ip-denylist.txt, a list of terms that must not appear in the product, code, assets or docs, with two sections (original's names and trademarks; real brands, companies and people). This replaces the two files named in the spec (denylist-original-terms.txt, denylist-real-brands.txt); the spec-writer updates the references. The spec-writer and the proxy do not author the trademark list; the orchestrator does. Marked: implementation of safe default A. Until the file exists the denylist ACs are not meaningful. Basis: circle-01 Q1 (safe default A in force); proxy definition "Never decide: legal/IP".

QF-10-3 "Fast" simulation: 10,000 ticks in 10 s

PROXY (medium): Accept as a relative regression bound on the CI runner. Basis: spec proposal; QF-10-1.

QF-10-4 Browser and OS matrix

PROXY (medium): CI verifies the three Playwright engines (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). The OS matrix and real Safari are manual release checks, listed in the release checklist for the user; not blocking for slice acceptance. Basis: R-110 (browser); customer silent.

QF-10-5 ?test=1 flag

PROXY (medium): Accept as a proposal; the architect confirms in the ADR. Condition: cheats and the test API exist only with the flag. Basis: NFR-S01.

Circle 3: quest journal, main quest and side quests (round R7-0)

Date: 2026-10-14. Facilitator: requirements-facilitator. Trigger: sixth briefing of the real customer (../00-brief.md, verbatim, 2026-10-14, status agreed): "hey i missing a place to look at the quest and the next step to solve for them can you put that into the next round after all is done?" Scheduled as R7-0 in ../50-plan.md. Answerer: the real customer or, under the delegation record, customer-proxy. Quest names and story text are brand/IP questions and are not delegated (see Escalations).

Starting point (OBSERVED in the repo)

  • The only goal is implicit: three story beats in src/core/content/story.js (start memo, boss, victory; R-104). No journal, no quest state.
  • Town NPCs in src/core/content/npcs.js: vendor, healer, potion seller, stash keeper. They trade, heal or store; none gives a task.
  • 8 floors (config.maxDepth), then the boss arena; save version is 3 (config.saveVersion); five save slots (R-220); panel keys I, C, S/K, M (src/input/keymap.js, J is free).
  • The customer's words fix only: a place to look at quests, and the next step for each. Everything else below is the orchestrator's reading of "stay close to the original" (NPC quests, a quest log, quest areas) and is a draft.

Readiness (area N, R-240..R-256)

Threshold 16/20, no item at 0 (harness/02-lifecycle.md). Scored for area N only.

Blocking question open: none for readiness. Q2 (final titles and story text) is a brand escalation that does not block work on working titles.

Questions (ordered by impact)

Q1 How many side quests, of what kind, from whom, for what reward?

  • Why it matters: biggest content driver (text, balance, tests, bot paths) and the part of "stay close to the original" that is a guess. The original's first act had about 6 NPC quests.
  • Options:
    • A. 3 side quests: smallest, one per NPC kind; fast, feels thin next to a journal.
    • B. 6 side quests: vendor 2, healer 2, potion seller 1, stash keeper 1, spread over the 8 floors (about one per floor pair). Kinds: kill N of a kind (for example interns, printers, auditors) or in a zone; find a quest item on a floor; reach a floor; defeat a named elite; one "use the stash" tutorial-style task. Rewards: gold and experience scaled to the floor, plus for three of them one item of fixed rarity from the normal generator, or potions; no skill or attribute points; no uniques.
    • C. 9 side quests: adds a second tier of tasks per zone and a chain (two linked steps); about 50% more text and tests.
  • Proposed default: B (6; no new NPCs; see R-245..R-247). Working titles and text are written by the agents and checked against the denylists.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy for count, kinds, givers and rewards; the final quest titles and dialogue text escalate (Q2 note below).
  • Affects: R-245, R-246, R-247, R-249, R-255, balance (R-230).

Answers

PROXY (confidence medium): A, 3 side quests, not the proposed 6. One per giver kind that matters for pacing: (1) vendor, a kill task on floors 1-2 (kill N of a basic monster kind), reward gold, experience and a stack of potions; (2) healer, find a quest item on floor 3 or 4 (item lives in a quest pouch, not the bag), reward one armour piece of at least magic rarity from the normal generator, scaled to floor 4; (3) potion seller, defeat a named elite on floor 4, reward one weapon of at least magic rarity plus potions. Quests 2 and 3 are the pacing tools: the gear lands before floor 5 (R6-acceptance: floors 1-4 painless, floor 5 a wall for an ungeared hero). No skill or attribute points, no uniques. Quests are data (R-240), so going to 6 later is content only. Cost reasoning: 3 quests need 3 texts, 3 reward tables, 3 bot paths; 6 doubles that in a round that also carries AI fixes (R7-1), the floor-entry stutter (R7-2) and polish. The customer asked for a journal and next steps, and did not answer whether they want side quests, so the smallest set that still shows the feature and helps pacing is the right bet. Basis: sixth briefing ("a place to look at the quest and the next step"), no answer on side quests; R6-acceptance pace finding; "stay close to the original" (NPC quests) satisfied in kind. Drop first if R7 is tight: (1) side quest 1 (kill task, cheapest to lose, no pacing role), (2) the map marker part of Q4, (3) NPC overhead markers shapes. Never drop: journal, main quest steps, the two gear quests. Working titles (original, scanned against both denylists by the proxy, FINAL ESCALATED): "Intern Overflow" (kill), "The Missing Badge" (find), "Toner Tyrant" (elite).

Q2 How does the memo become explicit main quest steps?

  • Why it matters: the customer's first need: today the player has no stated goal after the intro. Also fixes the story beats the journal repeats, which are text the customer may want to see.
  • Options:
    • A. One main quest "Why the lights went out" (working title) with 6 steps, each with a next-step line: 1 Read the memo and go to the lift (Lobby); 2 Reach floor 1 and find the first dark floor's cause (reach depth); 3 Reach floor 4 (zone change, mid-run milestone); 4 Reach floor 8 and find the way to the Executive Suite (boss unlock); 5 Defeat the Regional Director; 6 Return and read the verdict (victory screen). Steps follow existing events (depth reached, boss unlocked, boss defeated), so no new world content is needed.
    • B. As A but 4 steps (start, floor 4, floor 8, boss).
    • C. A plus story clues (found memos on floors) as collectible steps: more story, needs new item and placement work (later).
  • Proposed default: A. Step titles and next-step lines are original text. C is "could" for a later round.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy for the step structure; the quest title, step wording and any new story text ESCALATE to the real customer (brand/IP, as R-233); working text proceeds meanwhile.
  • Affects: R-241, R-242, R-104, R-255.

Answers

PROXY (confidence high for structure, text escalated): A, six main steps as proposed, driven by existing events only. One change: step 3's next-step line (reach floor 4) also tells the player that deeper floors hit harder and that the quest givers in the Lobby pay in gear (a nudge to the pacing quests). Structure only; no new world content. Working text (original, written by the proxy, FINAL ESCALATED): title "Why the Lights Went Out". Steps and next-step lines: 1 "Read the memo" / "Take the lift down." 2 "Find the dark floor" / "Reach floor 1 and look for what cut the power." 3 "Go deeper" / "Reach floor 4. Visit the Lobby first: the staff may pay in gear." 4 "Open the executive floor" / "Reach floor 8 and find the way up to the Executive Suite." 5 "Face the Regional Director" / "Defeat the Regional Director." 6 "File the report" / "Read the verdict." Side quest texts follow the same style (one title, one next-step line, short hand-in line); the implementer writes them in this style and the proxy scans them. Basis: sixth briefing; R-104; Q2 option A. The customer's own approved naming pattern (class names) is the precedent for escalating final wording.

Q3 Quest-specific areas or levels, or reuse of generated floors?

  • Why it matters: a new level costs generator work, art, balance and test time and risks the floor-generation budget (and the R7-2 stutter work in the same round). The original had quest-specific areas.
  • Options:
    • A. Reuse: quests use the Lobby and the 8 floors; a quest item or a named elite is placed in a generated room through the existing generator hooks; layouts stay valid for every seed.
    • B. A: plus one small hand-made special room (a fixed "records room" or "server closet") that appears on one floor for one quest.
    • C. Separate quest levels (full maps, entered from a floor).
  • Proposed default: A. B is a later round (could); C is out of scope.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy.
  • Affects: R-250, R-042, floor generation budget (R7-2).

Answers

PROXY (confidence high): A, reuse generated floors. Quest item and named elite are placed by the existing generator hooks, valid on every seed. No special room, no quest levels. Basis: default; R7 already carries a floor-entry stutter fix, and the customer asked only for a journal and next steps.

Q4 What does "next step" mean: text, map marker, arrow?

  • Why it matters: this is the customer's literal ask; the form decides the HUD and the map work.
  • Options:
    • A. Text only in the journal.
    • B. Text in the journal, plus a one-line tracker on the HUD for one pinned quest (default: the main quest), plus a marker on the full map (M) for targets the player already knows (stairs, NPC). No in-world arrow.
    • C. B plus a screen-edge arrow towards the target (needs known target positions; spoils exploration on generated floors).
  • Proposed default: B. Next-step text states where and what ("Take the lift to floor 3"); on unexplored floors the marker only shows what is known, so the game does not reveal the map. C is could.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy.
  • Affects: R-242, R-248, HUD layout (phone width).

Answers

PROXY (confidence high): B: journal text with next step, one-line HUD tracker for one pinned quest (default main quest), map (M) marker only for already-known targets. No in-world arrow. The next-step line is the customer's literal ask, so it must read as a concrete instruction ("Reach floor 4"), not a status. The map marker is the first thing cut if R7 is tight (the tracker and journal text already answer the ask). Basis: "the next step to solve for them"; default.

Q5 Where does the journal live, on desktop and on phone?

  • Why it matters: the customer asked for "a place to look"; discoverability decides whether the feature is felt.
  • Options:
    • A. Key only (default J, remappable, listed in Options with the other panel keys).
    • B. Key J, a HUD button (with a badge when something new happened) and a pause-menu entry. Desktop: side panel like the character sheet; phone width: full-screen panel opened by the HUD button.
    • C. B plus a title-screen view of quests per slot (read-only). Not needed: the slot card summary (Q6) covers it.
  • Proposed default: B. Panel opens and closes without extra pause beyond other panels; Escape closes it; keyboard-operable.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy.
  • Affects: R-243, R-244, R-254, key table (src/input/keymap.js), Options key list.

Answers

PROXY (confidence high): B: key J (remappable, listed in Options), a HUD button with a badge when something is new, and a pause-menu entry. Desktop side panel like the character sheet, full screen on phone width. No pause while open (same as the inventory panel decision), Escape closes, keyboard-operable. Basis: "a place to look at the quest" means discoverable by mouse, not only a key; inventory-panel decisions in the proxy log.

Q6 Quest state in saves, slot cards, old saves, several characters

  • Why it matters: touches every save path and the 5 slots; a wrong migration silently resets progress.
  • Options:
    • A. Save version 4 stores quest state per character slot. v3 saves migrate: main step derived from deepest depth, boss unlocked and boss defeated; side quests start available (none active or completed, no retroactive rewards). Slot card adds the current main step title and "N/6" side quests done. A new character in another slot starts at the first main step; slots never share quest state.
    • B. As A, but a v3 save is migrated by giving all side quests whose targets were already passed as completed with rewards (more generous, risk of reward exploits and hard to test).
    • C. Quest state is global (shared by all slots). Conflicts with R-220 and per-character stash (circle 2 Q4/Q6).
  • Proposed default: A. Needs an ADR stub (schema, migration fixtures) from the architect; a v4 save in old code is rejected as "newer" (existing rule).
  • Answerer: customer-proxy.
  • Affects: R-251, R-252, R-253, R-220..R-227, NFR-D05, NFR-D06.

Answers

PROXY (confidence high): A: save version 4, quest state per character slot, v3 migrates (main step from deepest depth, boss unlocked/defeated; side quests available, no retroactive rewards). Slot card adds the main step title and "N/3 side quests done" (count follows the final number of side quests). Quest state never shared across slots. Quest items live in a quest pouch so a full bag never blocks a pickup; two quests asking for the same kill both count it. Architect writes the ADR stub with migration fixtures. Basis: R-220 (5 slots, per character), proxy log circle-02 Q6.

Q7 Failing or abandoning quests; sound and visual cues

  • Why it matters: fail states multiply edge cases; the cues decide whether players notice the journal at all.
  • Options (fail/abandon):
    • A. No quest can fail; death, leaving a floor or quitting changes nothing; side quests cannot be abandoned but can be left unpinned. Quest items are bound to the quest and never lost.
    • B. Side quests can be abandoned and re-accepted later (progress reset).
    • C. Timed or failable quests. Not recommended (original has few; costs testing).
  • Options (cues):
    • D. Toast with quest title and new next step on accept, step done and complete; a short procedural chime from the global audio kit (honours mute and volume); badge on the journal button until opened; "available" and "hand-in ready" markers over NPCs with different shapes (not colour only); reduced motion: no animation, toast still shown.
    • E. Toast and badge only, no sound or NPC markers.
  • Proposed default: A and D. B is could.
  • Answerer: customer-proxy.
  • Affects: R-249, R-253, R-254, NFR-A03, NFR-A05.

Answers

PROXY (confidence high for A, medium for D details): A and D. No quest can fail or be abandoned; death, leaving a floor and quitting change nothing; quest items are bound and never lost. Cues: toast with title and new next step on accept, step done and complete; short procedural chime from the global audio kit (honours mute and volume); badge on the journal button; NPC markers "quest available" and "hand-in ready" with different shapes (not colour only); reduced motion: no animation, toast still shown. If tight, the NPC markers go before the chime and badge. Basis: customer wants "nice sound" (addendum) and a visible place for quests; defaults.

Escalations to the real customer

  • Added with the answers (2026-10-14): (1) side quest count: the proxy chose 3 and the customer never said whether they want side quests, so confirm or ask for more; (2) working titles "Why the Lights Went Out", "Intern Overflow", "The Missing Badge", "Toner Tyrant" and the six main step lines in Q2; (3) whether quests should hand out gear (pacing, floor 5 wall) or only gold and experience.
  • Quest titles, step wording, NPC dialogue and any new story text (brand/IP, R-255): working titles and text proceed; the customer confirms or renames, as for class names (R-233). Names and text stay original; both denylists (../ip-denylist.txt, ../ip-denylist-brands.txt) apply and a scan test runs over all quest strings. No quest may echo the original's quests, places or plot.
  • Q1 and Q2 count and structure are answered by the proxy but are the customer's call if they care: the briefing was silent on them.
  • Everything else (Q3..Q7) may be answered by customer-proxy; each is cheap to change because quests are data (R-240).

Proposed out of scope for this round (draft)

Quest-specific levels or full maps (Q3 C), timed, failable or escort quests, quest chains beyond two steps, dialogue trees with choices, branching outcomes, new NPCs or a notice board, daily or repeatable quests, rewards that grant skill or attribute points, unique quest-only items, voice, an in-world quest arrow (could), story collectibles (Q2 C, could), achievements, sharing quests across slots, localisation.

Next

After answers: set area N statuses, ADR stub for the v4 quest schema and migration (architect), spec ACs for R-240..R-256 (spec-writer), then the R7-0 order in ../50-plan.md (CORE quest state machine, events, save; then UI and WORLD). Expected readiness once defaults are accepted: about 14-15/20 (items 1, 2, 4, 10 rise to 2; items 3, 6, 7, 9 reach 2 only with ACs in Spec). The quest text stays a brand escalation.

7NFR: accessibility, i18n, browsers1NFR-A07 drafted: keyboard path, no colour-only state, reduced motion. Not agreed; tree panel on phone width still to be checked in review.
8Compliance and data residency1No personal data; names are local text. IP: class and skill names must be original, final class names are escalated (R-233). Q1 of circle 1 is still open.
9Acceptance criteria for every must1Each must in area M carries a "Testable as" line, so every must is testable. Formal AC ids come in the Spec phase (the spec files for character, skills, UI and save need new ACs). Not 2 until then.
10Out-of-scope list agreed1Proposed out of scope (below); nothing agreed.
Total11No item at 0. Below 16, so not ready.

Blocking question open: none for readiness; Q1 (class concepts) gates the spec, and the final names are a brand escalation.

Proposed out of scope for this round (draft)

Fourth class or multiple characters visible in one world; attribute respec; skill synergies as must (R-208 stays could); cloud saves or accounts; class-locked items; party play; cosmetic customisation (hair, colour) on the selection screen; hardcore or ladder modes; copy-slot (could in R-221).

Questions (ordered by impact)

Q1 Which three classes, and what happens to the existing Clerk?

  • Why it matters: decides content volume (3 trees, 3 rigs, 3 sets of animations and sounds), the name risk (brand check) and the migration of existing saves. The genre trio is melee/heavy, ranged/agile, caster. Names must be original (R-233); no name or branch may echo the original's classes or skill names.
  • Options:
    • A. Facilities Manager (melee, heavy, tough: keys, trolleys, floor buffers, fire doors), Sales Rep (ranged, agile: throws business cards, pens, staplers; dodge, speed, crits), IT Wizard (caster: scripts, firewalls, reboots, summons a helpdesk ticket bot).
    • B. As A, but the caster is a Compliance Officer (audits, debuffs, rule-based area effects, damage over time).
    • C. Another concept the customer names.
  • Working skill-branch sketch for A (all names provisional and original):
    • Facilities Manager, branches Heavy Lifting (Dolly Charge, Floor Buffer Sweep, Pallet Slam), Safety Officer (Hard Hat, Fire Drill, Lockout), Maintenance (Duct Tape, Master Key, Mop Up).
    • Sales Rep, branches Cold Calling (Stapler Throw, Pen Volley, Business Card Fan), Networking (Quick Exit, Smooth Talk, Handshake), Closing (Upsell, Hard Close, Commission).
    • IT Wizard, branches Scripting (Hotfix, Fork Bomb, Cron Job), Network Admin (Firewall, Reboot, Lockout Policy), Helpdesk (Ticket Bot, Restore Backup, Have You Tried Turning It Off).
  • Existing Clerk: the working class "Clerk" (all attributes 10, Stapler Throw, Reply-All, Coffee Break, Mute, Dress Code, Hustle) is retired as a class. Proposed: its skills are redistributed into the new trees (Stapler Throw to Sales Rep, Reply-All and Mute to IT Wizard or Sales Rep, Dress Code and Coffee Break to Facilities Manager, Hustle to Sales Rep), and old saves migrate to the Facilities Manager with skill points refunded (R-225).
  • Proposed default: A with the Clerk handling above. Final names ESCALATE for the brand check; they stay working names until the customer confirms.
  • Affects: R-200, R-201, R-203, R-225, R-232, R-233.

Q2 How is a skill tree built?

  • Why it matters: the biggest design lever; it defines the skill panel, data format, tests and balance.
  • Options:
    • A. 3 branches (tabs) per class, about 10 skills per class (3 + 3 + 4), 3 tiers per branch, 1 skill point per level (R-013, 29 points at the level cap of 30), max skill level 5 (single level for capstones and some passives), prerequisites: a character level per tier (for example tiers at levels 1, 8, 16) plus one earlier skill in the branch; synergies optional (could). A character cannot max everything, so it chooses a build.
    • B. As A but 2 points per level so a player can fill about half of the tree.
    • C. Flat list per class (no prerequisites), as in the earlier proxy answer QF-06-7.
  • Proposed default: A. Basic attack is free and not part of the 10.
  • Affects: R-202..R-208, R-014 (replaced), R-013 (points).

Q3 Respec rules

  • Why it matters: with three classes and 20-40 minute runs, players want to try builds; free respec also lowers the test cost for bots.
  • Options:
    • A. Skill points: unlimited and free in town; attributes are not respecced (LATER).
    • B. Skill points respec for gold, rising with level, in town.
    • C. One free respec at level 10, none after; or no respec at all (genre purist).
    • D. Delete and recreate the character is the only way (no feature).
  • Proposed default: A.
  • Affects: R-209, R-207, R-018.

Q4 What do classes share: items, attributes, stash?

  • Why it matters: controls loot design (class-locked items multiply the item tables) and balance.
  • Options:
    • A. All items usable by all classes (level and attribute requirements only); classes differ in starting attributes, growth, basic attack and tree; a few class-tagged affixes ("+1 level to Sales Rep skills") roll only for that class. The four attributes (Grit, Agility, Stamina, Focus) stay the same for all.
    • B. Class-restricted weapon types and armour (genre-like).
    • C. Fully class-locked unique items on top of A.
  • Proposed default: A. Stash is per character slot (see Q6).
  • Affects: R-201, R-231, R-053/R-054, item tables in 05-items-and-loot.md.

Q5 Character creation and the selection screen

  • Why it matters: the customer asked explicitly for "visually appealing"; it is judged by eye, so the content and the review route must be fixed. It is also the first screen of the game.
  • Options (content):
    • A. Three class cards in a carousel in the lobby scene; the selected class shows a large animated character from the same rig (idle loop, attack demo on hover or click), class name, role tag, a 2-3 line original blurb, starting stat bars (health, mana, strength-like and so on), the three branch names with icons, a name field with "suggest a name" button, Begin and Back.
    • B. As A plus a skill demo reel (the first active of each branch plays on a dummy).
    • C. Static portraits only (cheapest, weaker).
  • Name entry: 1-16 characters, letters, digits, space, hyphen, apostrophe, trimmed, stored as plain text; same name allowed in several slots.
  • Review route: 2-3 layout variants, independent visual review at desktop and phone width, as for art direction and the inventory panel; the real customer may overrule on screen.
  • Proposed default: A with the review route above; reduced motion shows a static pose.
  • Affects: R-210..R-214, R-232, NFR-P06, NFR-A07.

Q6 Save slots: placement, rules and migration

  • Why it matters: touches every save path; destructive actions are the main risk. The customer fixed the number (5) and the Options entry; the rest is open.
  • Options:
    • Placement: Options menu section "Save slots" (agreed) on title and pause; plus the title's New game and Continue using the same list (proposed).
    • Rules: overwrite and delete need confirmation that names the character; rename edits the character name; stash is per character (default) or shared across slots; options are global; autosave writes only to the active slot; Continue opens the last used slot.
    • Slot card: slot number, name, class, level, depth, play time, last played (R-222).
    • Migration: the old single save goes to slot 1 with the old key kept as backup; skills refunded (Q1).
    • Export/import per slot (R-226).
  • Proposed default: all of the above as written, stash per character, 400 KB per-slot cap (NFR-D05). In-game load/overwrite from the pause menu asks for confirmation.
  • Affects: R-215, R-220..R-227, R-090..R-092 (adapted), NFR-D05, NFR-D06.

Q7 Per-class balance targets and how they are checked

  • Why it matters: three classes with different power curves can break the 20-40 minute target (R-006, Q7 circle 1); without targets the bots cannot judge it.
  • Options:
    • A. Each class reaches the end boss in 20-40 minutes by the bot and by a normal player; parity band: median clear time and deaths of each class within 25% of the three-class median; no dominant skill in a tree; numbers in one config module; checked by release-gate bot runs per class with fixed seeds (one bot policy per class).
    • B. Same targets, but only as a soft report with no gate.
    • C. No numeric parity (tune by feel).
  • Proposed default: A, with B as the fallback if bot policies for casters prove unreliable.
  • Affects: R-230, R-234, bot/policy.js.

Answers

Answered by PROXY, 2026-10-14 (provisional until the real customer reviews; overrule any line in ../proxy-log.md).

Q1 Classes and the Clerk

PROXY (confidence medium): Option A (Facilities Manager, Sales Rep, IT Wizard as working names), Clerk retired as a class with skills redistributed as proposed and old saves migrated to the Facilities Manager with skill points refunded. Basis: "3 player classes with skill trees" (Third briefing) and "stay close to the original" (brief); the melee/ranged/caster trio is the genre's later convention, so it fits closeness in mechanics (brief G2: close in mechanics, original names). The customer named no concepts, so the office concepts are the default. ESCALATE: needs the real customer for the final class names (brand, R-233, QF-06-1); the three names above stay working names and work proceeds on them. Names and branch names must stay original; no echo of the original's classes or skills.

Q2 Skill tree structure

PROXY (confidence high): Option A: 3 branches per class, about 10 skills (3 + 3 + 4), 3 tiers (levels about 1, 8, 16), 1 point per level (29 points at cap 30), max skill level 5 (capstones single), one earlier skill in the branch plus a level gate; synergies stay could; basic attack free. Basis: "skill trees" (Third briefing) means branching with prerequisites, which replaces the flat list of QF-06-7 (the customer's later words override the earlier proxy answer); genre convention for point scarcity and build choice (customer words silent on numbers).

Q3 Respec

PROXY (confidence low): Option A: skill points respec free and unlimited in town; attributes not respecced. Basis: no customer words on respec; default taken because it keeps bot testing and 20-40 minute runs cheap. Tension noted: "stay close to the original" could point to C/D (no or limited respec, genre purist), so this is cheap to flip: the real customer may switch to B or C by changing one config value.

Q4 Shared items, attributes, stash

PROXY (confidence medium): Option A: all items usable by all classes (level and attribute requirements only), classes differ in start values, growth, basic attack and tree, a few class-tagged affixes, same four attributes, stash per character slot. Basis: default; the customer's words are silent, and A avoids multiplying item tables for three classes in three rounds. Genre closeness (B, restricted weapon types) is not demanded by the customer.

Q5 Character creation and selection screen

PROXY (confidence medium): Option A (three class cards in a carousel in the lobby scene, large animated character from the same rig, idle loop and attack demo, role tag, original blurb, stat bars, three branch names with icons, name field with suggest button, Begin and Back), name rules as proposed, reduced motion shows a static pose. Review route: 2-3 layout variants, independent visual review at desktop and phone width, as for art direction. Basis: "visually appealing character selection screen" (Third briefing), "generate what you need ... nice graphics" (Addendum, agreed). Option B (skill demo reel) accepted as a could if the renderer budget allows (NFR-P06). Final look is judged by eye, so the real customer may overrule on screen.

Q6 Save slots

PROXY (confidence high): all of the proposed default: 5 slots, section "Save slots" in the Options menu (customer's words, agreed) plus the same list on title New game/Continue and in the pause menu; overwrite and delete confirmation naming the character; rename; options global; stash per character; autosave to the active slot; Continue opens the last used slot; slot card with number, name, class, level, depth, play time, last played; old single save migrates to slot 1 with the old key kept as backup and skills refunded; export/import per slot; 400 KB per-slot cap (NFR-D05). Basis: "a save with 5 slots to the options menu" (Third briefing, agreed), which overrides circle 1 Q4 "one slot"; the remaining rules are the safe defaults for destructive actions.

Q7 Balance targets

PROXY (confidence medium): Option A: each class reaches the end boss in 20-40 minutes by bot and normal player, parity band within 25% of the three-class median for clear time and deaths, no dominant skill, numbers in one config module, release-gate bot runs per class with fixed seeds; B (soft report) as fallback if the caster bot policy proves unreliable. Basis: circle 1 Q7 (20-40 minute run, unchanged by the customer) and "keep improving the games and the tool as before" (Third briefing).

Escalations

  • Final class names and the game title (brand, R-233, QF-06-1, QF-07-3): ESCALATE: needs the real customer. Working names proceed.
  • Circle 1 Q1 (IP closeness) remains escalated; strict originality stays in force.

Next

After answers: update area M statuses, add ADR stubs if the answers change storage (stash scope) or tree schema, and ask the spec-writer to add ACs for the new requirements (character, skills, HUD, save files). Expected readiness after defaults are accepted: about 14-15/20 (items 1, 2, 4 and 10 rise to 2; items 3, 6, 7, 9 reach 2 only with ACs in Spec). A short circle 3 on edge cases is likely, and the class names stay a brand escalation.

What changed in this circle

Nothing answered yet. Created 20-requirements.md (79 requirements: 68 MVP, 11 later; 3 agreed from the user's own words: R-001, R-002 intent, R-003) and 40-nfr.md.

Questions (ordered by impact)

Q1 ESCALATE - real customer: how close may names and visuals go to the original?

  • Why it matters: decides title, naming, art, audio and marketing for the whole project, and whether the result can ever be shown publicly. The brief says "tribute" and "stay close to the original" (G2: partly contradicted). The harness rule forbids copying names, art, text and music. This is a legal/IP decision and is not delegated to customer-proxy.
  • Options:
    • A. Strict: mechanics and genre conventions only; every name, look, sound and text original; title does not allude to the original; no screenshots or comparisons to it in public text.
    • B. As A, but the project description may call it "inspired by a classic isometric action-RPG" (without naming it).
    • C. Closer allusions: homage names, lookalike layout or UI. Needs a legal review first. Not recommended.
  • Proposed default (safe): A. Working title "Office Crawler" stays internal only. Public naming and release are not decided here (also not delegated).
  • Affects: R-102, NFR-L01-L05, R-070 (HUD look).

Q2 What should it look like: perspective, art style, tone?

  • Why it matters: the biggest cost and architecture driver. All assets are made by agents, so the style must be producible in code or from generated shapes, with consistent quality.
  • Options:
    • (a) Perspective: true isometric 2:1 diamond tiles with depth sorting (matches the genre; harder: sorting, picking, occlusion); or top-down 2D (simpler, less "close to the original"); or top-down with a skewed 3/4 look.
    • (b) Art: pixel-art sprites generated by scripts from palettes and templates; or flat vector/geometric shapes drawn in code (canvas paths, simple animated figures); or hybrid (geometric characters, tile textures from a generator).
    • (c) Tone: dark-comedy satire (default); cosy comic; grim-serious office horror.
  • Proposed default: isometric 2:1 projection, vector/geometric shapes drawn in code on canvas (no external art files, fully original, easy to colour-blind-test), dark-comedy tone, stylised non-gory violence.
  • Affects: R-112, R-103, R-100, R-101, NFR-A03, NFR-P01.

Q3 What is the MVP scope: classes, depth, boss, level cap?

  • Why it matters: sets the size of the plan and the number of slices; the genre classic has several classes and dozens of levels, which is far beyond a first playable.
  • Options:
    • Classes: 1 (melee) / 2 (melee + caster) / 3.
    • Depth: 4 floors / 8 floors / 12 floors, then boss.
    • Boss: 1 end boss with 2 phases / none (MVP ends at depth) / boss every 4 floors.
    • Level cap: 20 / 30 / 50.
    • Gear depth: all slots incl. durability / reduced slots, no durability.
  • Proposed default: 1 class, 8 floors in 2 zones, 1 end boss with 2 phases, level cap 30, full slot list as in R-053, no durability, no identify. Further classes later.
  • Affects: R-010, R-013, R-014, R-043, R-045, R-053, R-054.

Q4 How much saving, and where?

  • Why it matters: save/load touches every data structure; mid-floor saving is much more work than saving in town.
  • Options:
    • A. Autosave to browser local storage at town, floor change, exit; resume in town or at floor entry; one character slot; manual export/import file.
    • B. Same plus exact mid-floor state restore.
    • C. No saving at all (single sitting).
    • D. Several character slots.
  • Proposed default: A. B and D later.
  • Affects: R-090-R-093, NFR-D01-D04.

Q5 Audio: how much, and how is it made?

  • Why it matters: no third-party samples (NFR-L01), so sound must be generated by agents; this is real effort.
  • Options:
    • A. Procedural sound effects (Web Audio synthesis), simple generative ambient loop per zone, volume sliders.
    • B. Sound effects only, no music.
    • C. Silent MVP, audio later.
    • D. Licensed or CC0 audio files with recorded licences.
  • Proposed default: B in MVP (procedural effects; music as "could" via A later). D only with licences recorded.
  • Affects: R-080-R-083, NFR-P02.

Q6 Monetisation, hosting and publication?

  • Why it matters: decides whether accounts, payment, analytics or legal text are needed; and who may see the result. Publishing publicly is not delegated.
  • Options:
    • A. None: free, no ads, no accounts, private/static preview only; public release decided later by the user.
    • B. Free public web page, no monetisation.
    • C. Any paid, ad or tracked model.
  • Proposed default: A.
  • Affects: NFR-D01, NFR-O02, NFR-L03, release planning.

Q7 Target session length and difficulty feel?

  • Why it matters: drives floor size, monster density, experience curve, loot rate and the save design.
  • Options:
    • A. Short: full run to the boss in 20-40 min, moderately forgiving, death returns to town with no gold loss.
    • B. Medium: 1-2 hours, moderate death penalty (lose some gold).
    • C. Long: many hours, replay at higher difficulty.
  • Proposed default: A. Replay difficulty later.
  • Affects: R-006, R-023, R-031, R-043, R-048.

Answers

Answered 2026-10-13 by customer-proxy under the delegation record in 00-brief.md. All PROXY answers are provisional until the real customer reviews them (proxy-log.md).

Q1

ESCALATE: needs the real customer; safe default A stays in force provisionally. Basis: legal/IP question, excluded from the delegation ("Not delegated" in 00-brief.md; "Never decide" in the proxy definition). The brief's "tribute" and "stay close to the original" (G2) are not read as permission to use names or assets.

Q2

PROXY (confidence medium): Perspective: isometric 2:1 with depth sorting, because the genre feel is what the customer asked to stay close to. Tone: dark-comedy satire of office life with stylised, non-gory violence. ART STYLE: not picked here; it is decided by the art-direction variant pick (docs/product/variants/art-direction/), which runs through independent visual review. Constraint carried into that pick: graphics must look good and be generated entirely by the team in code, with no third-party assets. Basis: "stay close to the original" and "a tribute but in an office environment" (verbatim brief); addendum "nice ... grafics ... generate what you need"; genre convention for tone (1-2 are silent on tone, so this part rests on genre/domain convention).

Q3

PROXY (confidence medium): Take the default: 1 class, 8 floors in 2 zones, 1 end boss with 2 phases, level cap 30, full slot list as in R-053, no durability, no identify. Further classes later. Basis: "stay close to the original" is applied to mechanics and feel only (never names/assets), and the default keeps the core loop (town, descend, fight, loot, boss). Nothing in the customer's words asks for more breadth in a first playable.

Q4

PROXY (confidence medium): Take the default A: autosave to browser local storage at town, floor change and exit; one character slot; manual export/import file. B and D later. Basis: the customer's words are silent on saving; default chosen on genre convention and lowest risk. No personal data leaves the browser.

Q5

PROXY (confidence medium): Choose A instead of the proposed default B: procedural sound effects (Web Audio synthesis) plus a simple generative ambient loop per zone, with volume sliders (master, effects, ambient) and mute. Real music composition stays "could". Reason: the proposed default B (effects only, no music) was written before the addendum; the customer then said "we want to have nice sound", and "generate what you need". Effects only would under-deliver on "nice sound", while A stays inside NFR-L01 (everything synthesised by the team, nothing third-party) and costs only effort, not money. D (licensed or CC0 files) is not chosen: the customer said the team generates everything. Basis: addendum, verbatim: "we want to have kuce soubd anf grafics as well generate what you need" (agreed customer statement). This is a refinement of a proxy proposal, not a change to a customer answer, so no conflict.

Q6

PROXY (confidence high): Take the default A: free, no ads, no accounts, private/static preview only; any public release is decided later by the user. Basis: the brief mentions no monetisation or publication; publishing is not delegated, so this answer only keeps things private and does not publish anything.

Q7

PROXY (confidence medium): Take the default A: a full run to the boss in 20-40 minutes, moderately forgiving, death returns to town with no gold loss. Replay difficulty later. Basis: the customer's note "dont play to much" suggests short sessions for testing; otherwise genre convention for a first playable (the customer's words are silent on length).

Escalations

  • Q1 (IP: how close names and visuals may go): ESCALATE: needs the real customer; safe default A stays in force provisionally.

Full requirements document

Requirements (working draft, circle 1)

Date: 2026-10-13. Owner: requirements-facilitator.

Conventions

  • Status: only the user's explicit words (00-brief.md, verbatim) are agreed. Everything else is draft.
  • Provenance: OBSERVED = seen in evidence; INFERRED = derived from the brief or from known genre conventions; ASSUMED = my guess, needs an answer. Greenfield: there is no as-is model. "Genre knowledge" is recorded as INFERRED (from the brief's "stay close to the original"), not OBSERVED.
  • Scope: MVP = first playable slice set; LATER = after MVP. Priority is must / should / could within that scope.
  • Naming rule (claim G2): the original's names, art, text, music and story are never used. Refer to it only as "the original".
  • Acceptance criteria are not written yet (Spec phase). Items marked "AC: pending" need them before leaving Circles.

Summary

108 requirements: 97 MVP, 11 later (79 from circle 1 plus 29 in area M added 2026-10-14; R-010, R-014, R-017, R-018, R-074, R-092 and R-093 are superseded or promoted by area M, see its header). The count is above the 35-60 target because each HUD panel, slot type and testability hook is listed separately; the Spec phase may merge them.

A. Core loop and controls

R-001 Playable game in a desktop browser

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief (user, verbatim: "browser clone")
  • Status: agreed | Provenance: OBSERVED (brief)
  • Notes: details in K.

R-002 Hack-and-slash action-RPG in the spirit of the original

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief (user: "famous hack and slay", "stay close to the original")
  • Status: agreed (intent); detail items below are draft | Provenance: OBSERVED (brief)
  • Notes: "close" applies to mechanics and feel only (claim G2).

R-003 Office environment setting

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief (user: "in an office environment")
  • Status: agreed | Provenance: OBSERVED (brief)
  • Notes: see J.

R-004 Core loop: town, descend, fight, loot, return, upgrade, descend deeper

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief restatement; genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: the player can return to town (via stairs or a portal item) and come back to the deepest reached floor.

R-005 Mouse-driven controls

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief ("stay close"); genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: left click on ground = move; click on monster = attack; click on item = pick up; click on NPC/object = interact; right click = use the selected secondary skill. Hold button = continuous move/attack. Hotkeys for skills (1-4), potions (belt keys), panels (C, I, S/K, M/Tab), Esc = pause.

R-006 Run length: a session is meaningful in 20-40 minutes

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: ASSUMED (see circle-01 Q7)
  • Status: draft | Provenance: ASSUMED

R-007 Gamepad and touch support

  • Priority: could | Scope: LATER
  • Source: ASSUMED
  • Status: draft | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: desktop mouse and keyboard only for MVP (see K, NFR).

B. Character

R-010 Selectable character class

  • SUPERSEDED 2026-10-14 by R-200..R-215 (3 classes, customer's third briefing).
  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre; circle-01 Q3
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: MVP default: 1 playable class (melee). Two more classes (ranged, caster) LATER. Class names are original, office-flavoured (working: "Intern-turned-Enforcer" style, final names open).

R-011 Four primary attributes

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: strength-like (damage, equipment requirement), dexterity-like (hit chance, defence), vitality-like (health), energy-like (mana). Original names: e.g. Grit, Agility, Stamina, Focus (working).

R-012 Derived stats

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: max health, max mana, damage range, defence (armour), chance to be hit, resistances (see R-026).

R-013 Experience and levelling

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: kills give experience; each level raises base health/mana, grants 5 attribute points to spend and 1 skill point. MVP level cap: 30 (draft number, see circle-01 Q3). Level-up restores health and mana.

R-014 Skills: learn and upgrade with skill points

  • SUPERSEDED in structure 2026-10-14 by R-202..R-205 (per-class trees).
  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: MVP: 1 basic attack + 4 active skills + 2 passives for the one class, each with levels 1..N. Skill choice from a small tree or list. Mana cost, cooldown or none (open, spec).

R-015 Skill bar with assignable skills

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: primary (left-click) skill and secondary (right-click) skill, plus hotkey slots.

R-016 Attribute point allocation UI with requirements preview

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

R-017 Multiple classes with distinct skill sets

  • PROMOTED to MVP 2026-10-14: see R-200..R-208.
  • Priority: should | Scope: LATER
  • Source: genre; circle-01 Q3
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

R-018 Respec (reset skill/attribute points)

  • PARTLY PROMOTED 2026-10-14: skill respec is R-209; attribute respec stays LATER.
  • Priority: could | Scope: LATER
  • Source: ASSUMED
  • Status: draft | Provenance: ASSUMED

R-022 Ranged and spell projectiles

R-023 Health and mana; death and respawn

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

  • Notes: MVP: 6-8 archetypes in 3 behaviours: melee swarmers, ranged attackers, tough "elites". Working names: Temp Worker, Middle Manager, Auditor, Printer Jam, Consultant, Rogue Vending Machine. Final names open to the user.

R-031 Monster stats scale with depth

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP

  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

E. World

R-040 Town hub (the Lobby)

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief restatement ("safe town hub")
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

R-042 Procedurally generated dungeon levels

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief restatement ("randomly generated dungeon levels")
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: every new game (and each new floor visit) has a different layout; room-and-corridor on a tile grid; each floor has an entry stair and an exit stair; reachable by construction (validated).

R-043 Depth progression

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: brief restatement ("going deeper")
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: MVP default: 8 floors in 2 themed zones (Floors 1-4 "Open Plan Floors", Floors 5-8 "Basement/Server Room"), then boss. Open: Q3.

R-044 Floor persistence within a session

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: ASSUMED
  • Status: draft | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: default: each floor is regenerated on re-entry from its seed (same layout), cleared monsters stay cleared within the run.

R-045 End boss on the last floor

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre; circle-01 Q3
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: single end boss (working: "The Regional Director"), multi-phase attack patterns, guaranteed good loot, victory screen, then "keep playing" mode.

R-046 Waypoint / quick-return item

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP

  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: slots: head, body, hands, feet, belt, weapon (main), off-hand (shield or second item), two rings, amulet. MVP can start with a subset (head, body, weapon, off-hand, ring x2, amulet) if spec shows cost; decision in Spec.

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP

  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre

M. Classes, skill trees and save slots (added 2026-10-14, circle 2)

Source of this area: the third briefing in 00-brief.md (user, 2026-10-14, verbatim: "I want to have 3 player classes with skill trees. Also, make a visually appealing character selection screen. Add a save with 5 slots to the options menu"). Status agreed is used only where those words cover the item; everything else is draft with a proposed default in circles/circle-02.md. Genre convention used for the drafts (INFERRED): three classes in a melee/heavy, ranged/agile and caster split; each class has its own tree of three branches (tabs); about ten skills per class; prerequisites and level gates; one skill point per level; a character-creation step with name and class.

Supersedes (customer words win; no open conflict, the brief already records the override):

  • R-010 ("MVP default: 1 playable class") and circle-01 Q3 "1 class" (PROXY): now 3 classes (R-200).
  • R-017 (multiple classes, LATER): promoted to MVP via R-200..R-208.
  • R-014 ("1 basic attack + 4 active skills + 2 passives", "list" per QF-06-7 "list, no prerequisites"): replaced by per-class trees with prerequisites (R-202..R-205). The existing clerk content (Strike, Stapler Throw, Reply-All, Coffee Break, Mute, Dress Code, Hustle) is a design input, not a final class (see R-225).
  • R-018 (respec, LATER): promoted, see R-209.
  • R-092 ("single character slot") and circle-01 Q4 "one save slot" (PROXY): now 5 slots (R-220). R-093 (multiple slots, LATER): promoted and merged into R-220..R-227.
  • R-074 (skill panel): becomes the skill-tree panel (R-206). QF-06-1 ("no class screen for one class") and QF-09-4 ("delete character keeps options") stay valid in spirit; see R-221.
  • Open tension (not a conflict): R-013 gives 1 skill point per level and a level cap of 30, i.e. 29 points, while a class has about 10 skills with several levels each. The tree is therefore a "choose a build" tree, not "learn everything". Confirmed as default in Q2.

Every skill has a name, original text and levels 1..N that scale (AC-R-014-5 pattern). Skill names are original and office-flavoured; the existing 6 skills are reused or renamed into the trees.

R-205 Skill points, levels and spending rules

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP

No negative points, no spending without a point, points cannot be spent on another class's skill. Points are never lost on level-up while unspent.
  • Testable as: unit test of point accounting over levels 1-30: spent plus unspent equals levels gained; max level enforced.

  • Source: circle-02 Q1 and Q6; NFR-D03
  • Status: draft | Provenance: INFERRED

The legacy class maps to one of the new classes (default: the melee/heavy class, circle-02 Q1) and the learned legacy skills are refunded as free skill points rather than guessed into the new tree. Attributes, items, stash, gold, depth and boss flag are preserved. If slot 1 already holds a new-format save, the old save goes to the first empty slot, else stays as backup with a notice.
