  • Source: sixth briefing; R-104; circle-03 Q2
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: the memo goal ("find out why the floors went dark") becomes one main quest of about six steps from the start of a run to the end boss and victory, each with a one-line next-step text. It starts active in a new game. Step texts are original.
  • Testable as: bot run to the boss: every main step completes in order and the journal shows the matching next step at each point.

R-242 Next step per active quest

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: sixth briefing ("the next step to solve for them")
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: every active quest shows exactly one concrete next step as text, derived from state, never stale (for example "Take the lift to floor 3", "Talk to the facilities desk"). Optional hint of where (floor, NPC). Completed quests show no next step.
  • Testable as: unit test: for every quest and every state the next-step text key exists and matches the current step; E2E: journal text changes after the step is done.

R-243 Quest journal panel

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: sixth briefing ("a place to look at the quest")
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: a panel listing active quests (main first, then side quests) with title, giver, next step and progress, plus a completed list. Opens with a key (default J, remappable in Options like the other panel keys), a HUD button and a pause-menu entry; closes with Escape or the same key. Does not pause the game more than other panels do.
  • Testable as: E2E: the key, the HUD button and the pause entry each open it; Escape closes it; remapped key works.

R-244 Journal on phone width and keyboard

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: sixth briefing; NFR-A04, NFR-A07
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: on phone width the journal is a full-screen panel reached by the HUD button (touch target size as other buttons); desktop shows it as a side panel like the character sheet. Keyboard-operable, no colour-only state, reduced motion respected, long text wraps.
  • Testable as: E2E at phone and desktop width: no horizontal scroll, button reachable, all quests readable; keyboard-only open, scroll and close.

R-245 Side quests: number and givers

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: orchestrator interpretation of "stay close to the original"; circle-03 Q1
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: default 6 side quests, given by the existing town NPCs (vendor 2, healer 2, potion seller 1, stash keeper 1) in src/core/content/npcs.js; no new NPCs. A quest is offered in the NPC dialogue, accepted or declined, and handed in by talking to the same NPC again.
  • Testable as: E2E: each of the 6 quests can be accepted, advanced and handed in with the right NPC; count equals the configured number.

R-246 Quest kinds and objectives

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre; circle-03 Q1
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: objective types: kill N monsters of a kind or in a zone, find a quest item on a floor (drops once, in a generated room, never lost: it is not in the normal item pool and not sold), reach a floor, defeat a named elite, use a floor feature or the stash. No timed quests, no escort.
  • Testable as: unit tests per objective type; quest item spawns exactly once per quest and per run and is deterministic per seed.

R-247 Quest rewards

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre; circle-03 Q1
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: gold and experience scaled to the floor, plus for some quests one item of a fixed rarity rolled by the normal item generator, or a few potions; one reward (a stash capacity step) is allowed if the stash supports it. No skill points, no attribute points, no unique-only items. Reward is shown in the journal before accepting and is granted once on hand-in.
  • Testable as: unit test: reward granted once; inventory-full hand-in keeps the quest open or drops to the floor per spec (no loss).

R-248 Tracker line and map marker

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: sixth briefing; circle-03 Q4
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: HUD shows one tracked quest's next step as a short line (default: the main quest; the player may pin another); the full map (M) marks the known target (stairs, NPC) of the tracked quest. No in-world arrow in MVP (could).
  • Testable as: E2E: tracker line equals the journal's next step for the pinned quest; marker appears on the map only for known targets.

R-249 NPC quest indicators and dialogue

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: genre; circle-03 Q1
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: an NPC with an available quest shows a marker over the figure, one with a hand-in ready a different marker (shape differs, not colour only, NFR-A03); quest dialogue is short original text; existing vendor, healer and stash functions keep working unchanged.
  • Testable as: E2E: marker states in the Lobby; trading and healing still work with an open quest.

R-250 Quest areas reuse generated floors

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: circle-03 Q3
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: no new quest-only levels or maps in this round; quests use the existing Lobby and the 8 floors plus the boss arena. Quest content may place a quest item or a named elite in a generated floor through the existing generator hooks without changing layout validity (R-042) or the floor-generation budget.
  • Testable as: generator test: every seed still passes validity with quest content placed; floor generation time within budget.

R-251 Quest state in saves, migration v3 to v4

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: sixth briefing; R-090; circle-03 Q5
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: save version 4 adds quest state per character slot. Migration of a v3 save: main quest step derived from existing fields (deepest depth, boss unlocked, boss defeated); side quests start as available, none active, none completed (no retroactive rewards). A v4 save loaded by older code is rejected as "newer" (existing rule). Checksum and corrupt-slot behaviour unchanged (R-227).
  • Testable as: unit tests: v3 fixtures at several progress points migrate to the right step; round trip of v4; E2E: load an old save, open the journal.

R-252 Quest summary on the slot card

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: circle-03 Q5; R-222
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: the slot card (R-222) adds the main quest's current step title and the count of completed side quests (for example "3/6"). A slot with no quest data shows nothing extra.
  • Testable as: E2E: slot card text after progress; migrated old slot shows its derived step.

R-253 Quests cannot fail; no abandon in MVP; per character

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: circle-03 Q7
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: death, leaving a floor or quitting never fails a quest; an unfinished quest item stays with the character; objectives are re-reachable. Active side quests cannot be abandoned, but may be left unpinned. Each character slot has its own quest state; a new character starts at the first main step. Respeccing, deleting or overwriting a slot affect only that slot.
  • Testable as: E2E: die with an active quest, reload, quest and progress intact; two slots hold different quest states.

R-254 Sound and visual cues for quest updates

  • Priority: should | Scope: MVP
  • Source: circle-03 Q7
  • Status: specified | Provenance: ASSUMED
  • Notes: on accept, step done and complete: a short toast with the quest title and new next step, a short chime from the procedural audio kit (global, no files; honours mute and volume), and a badge on the journal button until the journal is opened. Reduced motion: no animation, toast still shown.
  • Testable as: unit test: events raise the cue; E2E: toast text, badge clears on opening; audio test: cue is silent when muted.

R-255 Original quest names and text

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: claim G2; R-102; NFR-L01, NFR-L05; circle-03 escalation
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: quest titles, step texts, dialogue and reward names are original, contain no real brand, company or person, and pass the scans against ip-denylist.txt and ip-denylist-brands.txt. No quest title or plot may echo the original's. Final quest titles and story text go to the real customer for confirmation (ESCALATE, as R-233); working titles proceed.
  • Testable as: legal test scans all quest strings against both denylists.

R-256 Testability and bot support for quests

  • Priority: must | Scope: MVP
  • Source: R-121, R-123; ADR-0003
  • Status: specified | Provenance: INFERRED
  • Notes: in test mode the hook exposes quest state, can set a quest step, and cheats can complete a quest; the headless bot completes the main quest from events without special casing and is not slowed below the R-006 run target by quest items. Replay hashes are re-pinned once when quest state enters the state (as in R4).
  • Testable as: hook E2E and unit tests; bot run per class reaches the boss with all main steps completed.
Non-functional requirements

Non-functional requirements (working draft, circle 1)

Date: 2026-10-13. All items are draft. No NFR comes from the user's words; provenance is shown per item. Values marked ASSUMED need an answer or confirmation.

Performance

NFR-P01 Frame rate

  • Target: 60 fps on a mid-range laptop (integrated graphics, 4 cores, 8 GB RAM) with up to 50 active monsters on screen; never below 30 fps in the same scene.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-P02 Load time

  • Target: playable within 5 s on a broadband connection from a cold cache; total download at most 10 MB (stretch: 3 MB).
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-P03 Floor generation time

  • Target: a new floor generates in under 500 ms on the reference laptop.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-P04 Input latency

  • Target: click-to-visible-reaction under 100 ms at 60 fps.
  • Provenance: INFERRED (genre feel) | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-P05 Memory

  • Target: under 500 MB of browser memory after a one-hour session (no unbounded growth from items, particles or floors).
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

Browsers and platforms

NFR-B01 Supported browsers

  • Latest two stable versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux). Only standard web APIs; no plug-ins.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED (brief says "browser") | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-B02 Screen size

  • Playable from 1280x720 up to 4K; the view scales; minimum window width 1024 px. Mobile and tablet are out of scope for MVP.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-B03 No install, no account, no server needed to play

  • Provenance: INFERRED from brief ("browser") | Priority: must | Status: draft

Offline

NFR-O01 Works offline after first load

  • The game runs without network once loaded (all assets local, no CDN at run time). Saves are local. A service worker for installable offline use is "could".
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-O02 No telemetry or network calls during play

  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

Accessibility

NFR-A01 Remappable keys

  • All keyboard bindings can be changed in options and persist in the save/options. Mouse buttons stay as defaults in MVP.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED (not the user's words) | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-A02 Pause

  • The game can be paused at any time outside menus with Esc; simulation and audio stop; panels may be opened while paused. No time-limited input anywhere.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-A03 Colour-blind-safe loot and UI

  • Rarity is never shown by colour alone: each rarity also has a distinct label prefix/icon/border pattern. Palette checked for deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia. Health vs mana distinguished by shape/fill too.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-A04 Text size and contrast

  • UI text at least 14 px at 1080p with a size option; contrast ratio at least 4.5:1 for body text.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-A05 Reduced motion / flashing

  • Option to reduce screen shake and flash effects; no content flashing more than 3 times per second.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-A06 Language

  • English only in MVP; all text kept in one string table so translation is possible later (i18n "could").
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

Legal and IP guardrails

NFR-L01 No third-party names, assets or text

  • No names, characters, artwork, sprites, sounds, music, logos, level layouts copied from the original or any other third-party game or brand. No asset downloaded from the internet unless its licence is recorded and it is CC0 or equivalent; MVP default is that all assets are generated by agents in code.
  • Provenance: INFERRED (claim G2, harness rule 06) | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-L02 Mechanics are free to follow the genre

  • Genre mechanics (click-to-move, loot rarity tiers, inventory grid, potion belt, procedural levels) are ideas and systems, not protected expression; used as general genre conventions. This is an engineering position, not legal advice; see circle-01 Q1.
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-L03 Title, store/marketing text and trade dress

  • The title and any public description must not include the original's name, nor imply endorsement. No lookalike logo, font or colour trade dress of the original. Public release is not delegated (see brief).
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-L04 Dependencies

  • Any library used has a permissive licence (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC); licence list shipped with the build.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-L05 No real brands, companies or people in game text

  • Satire stays generic.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

Save data and retention

NFR-D01 Data stored

  • Only the game save and options, in browser local storage on the player's machine. No personal data, no accounts, no cookies, no analytics. GDPR/personal-data scope: none by design.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-D02 Retention

  • Save stays until the player deletes it (in-game "delete character" or clearing browser data). No expiry. Browsers may evict storage, so export/import (R-092) exists.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-D03 Save format versioning

  • Saves carry a version number; a newer game version migrates older saves or refuses with a clear message; a corrupt save never crashes the game (offers a fresh start and keeps the bad file for export).
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-D04 Save integrity

  • Players may edit their own save; no anti-cheat in MVP.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: could | Status: draft

Security baseline

NFR-S01 Static content only

  • No server code, no user-supplied content executed; test-mode hooks (R-121, R-123) are off in normal play unless a documented flag is set. Content-Security-Policy where hosting allows.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

Reliability and quality

NFR-Q01 Determinism

  • Given a seed and an input sequence, the simulation produces identical state on every supported browser (see R-120). Rendering is excluded.
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-Q02 No crash on invalid state

  • Errors are caught at the game loop; the game shows an error screen with a way to export the save.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

Classes, skill trees and save slots (added 2026-10-14, circle 2)

All draft; none comes from the user's words except the existence of 5 slots.

NFR-D05 Five-slot storage budget

  • Five slots plus options plus one legacy backup fit in browser local storage (commonly about 5 MB per origin). The per-slot soft cap of QF-09-1 (1 MB) cannot hold for all five; proposed: per-slot soft cap 400 KB, total under 2.5 MB, measured with a worst-case character (full inventory, stash, level 30). A failing write for one slot never damages another (R-227). Writes are coalesced (R-224).
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-D06 Save version bump and migration

  • The slot format has its own version; the v1 single-slot save migrates into slot 1 (R-225) without data loss on preserved fields; migration is idempotent and tested with a synthetic fixture (QF-09-5). Extends NFR-D03.
  • Provenance: INFERRED | Priority: must | Status: draft

NFR-P06 Selection screen performance

  • The animated class-selection screen holds 60 fps on the reference laptop (NFR-P01) and does not leak memory when switching classes 200 times.
  • Provenance: ASSUMED | Priority: should | Status: draft

NFR-A07 Selection screen and tree accessibility

  • Class selection, name entry, slot list and skill tree are fully keyboard-operable, never rely on colour alone (NFR-A03), honour reduced motion (NFR-A05) and meet NFR-A04 contrast and text size.
  • Provenance: INFERRED (extends NFR-A01..A05) | Priority: must | Status: draft

after retro R6, patch-level wording, 2026-10-14

  • tools/metrics-report.mjs: one readable docs/metrics/REPORT.md per project (overview per round, agent table per round, your messages), regenerated with the portals. Reason: only rounds 1–3 had readable metric pages (user, 2026-10-14).

  • implementer.md: bench = 5 runs with median, min, p99 and load (L-034); validation tightening greps seeded fixtures into e2e_red (L-038); new events list every consumer table (L-039).
  • test-engineer.md: legal fixtures come from real play, the save writer or the same validator; hostile fixtures name the rule they break (L-038).
  • harness-retro.md: reconcile human-log against 00-brief, verify candidate learnings against files (L-037, L-012).
  • Playbook: bench row now 5 quiet runs with median/min/p99; human-log written before acting; 5 new rows (metric additions name their first finding L-035, stop re-reporting agents L-032, fixtures vs validation L-038, contract consumer tables L-039, probes from structure L-036); prompt template items 6 and 7 (no git at all, hand back once).

Reading notes. (1) R3 totals are unknowable: metrics-iter2-3.md stops at the S3 core ("so far"), so S3 WORLD, S3 UI, both final reviews, both FINAL-FIX runs and the POLISH agent have no token or minute data. (2) The source table's stated subtotal of 293 agent minutes does not match its own rows (273.0); the JSON uses the rows. (3) Visual score has not reached "ship" (32) in any in-game review: 30, 29, 31. Experiment E3 targets 32 by round G. (4) humanMin was never timed, so the human-time claim in 11-operating-model.md cannot be checked from these rounds.

Learning register state: 20 files; verified 8, applied 8, reopened 1 (L-016), open 3 new (L-018 to L-020). See harness/learnings/INDEX.md.

Three most valuable practices so far

  1. Independent code review. Blocking findings per round were 1, 3, 3, and every one was missed by the implementers' own suites (120, 360, 415 tests): mouse-up while paused (S1-code-review.md B1), unimplemented map and Emergency Exit plus an ungated stash (S2-code-review.md blocking 1 and 3), progress lost on quit-to-title (S3-code-review.md B1). Cost per review: 108k, 167k tokens, 2.4 to 7.5 min. Highest defect yield per token of any step (L-008; E1 will test the adversarial add-on).
  2. Pure deterministic core first, with a bot playing it (L-011). The bot found the orbiting AI bug in R1 and runs that were too short in R2 (8.6 min against a 20-40 min target, fixed to 23 min in CORE-FIX), and reached 20/20 boss wins in R3, before or independent of any sprite. Replay hashes matched across Node and Chromium (S1-code-review.md passed checks).
  3. Machine-checked rules instead of prose (L-017, L-006). After lint-rules.test.js and layering.test.js, the S2 and S3 reviews report no clock, Math.random or wall-clock findings, where R1's review had found 4 more after the prose rule. Also the resumable progress file (L-015) let FINAL-FIX continue from a green WIP commit (427 tests) after the container restart, though no second restart has tested it.

Three least effective practices so far

  1. Behavioural rules written into one agent file. L-016 was added to spec-writer.md only; the same failure ("not done" / "missing" without checking the repo) reappeared in the POLISH implementer within hours (SESSION-NOTES.md r4, final-visual-review.md). Same root cause as L-007: agents already in flight never see new rules, and nothing re-sends them. Change: apply cross-role checking rules to the shared prompt template in 12-orchestration-playbook.md, and have the orchestrator list in-flight agents when a rule is added. Status: L-016 reopened, L-007 flagged.
  2. A long AC list as the coverage mechanism. 341 ACs cost 140k tokens and 8.2 min (R1), yet S1 acceptance still found 7 ACs without evidence, and two slices shipped with unowned ACs (map and Emergency Exit in S2, story frame R-104 in S3), found only at the end-of-slice review. The cap (L-003) reduces volume but not the missing owner. Change: AC-to-package matrix before launch (L-019, proposed for post-mortem since it touches the plan gate).
  3. Polish-after-review without a regression check. In-game visual scores were 30, 29, 31 across three review-and-polish cycles; floater, plate and label overlap is a named defect in all three (L-018), each time fixed by prose fix lists and each time back with new content. Change: an automated overlap layout test and a named checklist line for the visual reviewer (L-018, proposed).

Measurement gaps to close before the post-mortem

  • Metrics were copied by hand from agent reports; R3 is incomplete and one subtotal is off by 20 min. From round 4, harness-retro should collect tokens and minutes at each agent hand-back.
  • docs/product/STATE.md still reads "Phase: Circles. Circle 1 open" (head of file, checked 2026-10-14) although R3 is done: the state file is not part of any step's exit criteria.
  • Proxy acceptance has records for S1 only; S2, S3 and human sign-off have none, so "gates passed without rework" cannot be scored.
  • humanMessages is only attributable for the original brief; the standing instructions in SESSION-NOTES.md are undated. Record user messages with a round tag in 00-brief.md from now on.
  • Escaped defects are undefined; propose: defects found by a later stage than the one that should have caught them, counted from round 4.

Architecture decisions

ADR-0001-stack.md

ADR-0001 Stack

Date: 2026-10-13. Status: proposed (architect; gate authority delegated to the customer proxy, see ../proxy-log.md). Inputs: ../00-brief.md, ../20-requirements.md (R-110..R-113), ../40-nfr.md, ../circles/circle-01.md (Q2, Q3, Q5 PROXY answers), ../30-spec/10-tech-and-testability.md, stack pack harness/stack-packs/static-web/.

Context

A single-player, real-time isometric action-RPG for desktop browsers. No server, no accounts, no network at play time (NFR-B03, NFR-O02). All art and sound are generated in code (NFR-L01, Q2/Q5 PROXY answers). One self-contained build that also runs from file:// (R-111, AC-R-111-1). Simulation must be deterministic and runnable in Node (R-113, R-120, R-122). Every dependency must be MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0/ISC (NFR-L04).

Options considered

#OptionForAgainst
1static-web pack, plain JS ES modules, Canvas 2D, esbuild to one dist/index.htmlPack already provides build, seeded RNG, test hook, preview workflow. Node-testable pure modules. One dev dependency. Canvas 2D is enough for an isometric 2D game at 50 monsters.No engine conveniences; we write loop, sprites, UI ourselves (accepted, cost is planned).
2Game engine (Phaser, PixiJS, Godot web export)Scene graph, sprite batching, asset pipeline.Runtime licence/size review (Godot export is large and needs wasm/files, breaks file:// single file); engines assume loaded art assets, our art is generated; couples simulation to the engine loop, hurting Node tests and determinism. Rejected.
3WebGL / WebGPU rendererFaster at very large sprite counts.Context-loss handling, shader work, headless-test pain (software GL in CI), WebKit differences. Not needed for the stated load (NFR-P01: 50 monsters). Rejected for MVP; the render module boundary (ADR-0002) keeps a later swap possible.
4UI framework (React, Svelte) for HUD/panelsQuick declarative UI.Adds runtime dependency and build complexity; inventory drag/drop with grid items is simpler against our own hit-region model on the canvas; pack says "no framework unless an ADR says otherwise". Rejected.
5TypeScriptType safety.Needs a typecheck step the pack does not have; JSDoc @typedef on state shapes gives most of the value. Deferred; can be added later because esbuild strips TS.

Decision

  1. Stack pack: static-web (harness/stack-packs/static-web/, commands npm ci, npm test, npm run build, npm run e2e). No adapter needed beyond the extensions below.
  2. Language: plain modern JavaScript, ES modules, target es2022. Types are documented with JSDoc typedefs in src/core/types.js (no build step).
  3. Rendering: one HTML5 <canvas> using the 2D context for the world, HUD and in-game panels. Menus, title, game over, error and options screens are DOM overlays (real <button>s with roles and text from the string table) so tests and screen readers can find them (AC-R-001-2, AC-R-023-2, AC-NFR-Q02-1).
  4. Build: esbuild (already in the skeleton, 0.25.10, MIT) bundles src/main.js and CSS into one dist/index.html, IIFE, minified. build.mjs additionally: injects a CSP meta tag (default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; media-src blob:; connect-src 'none', AC-NFR-S01-2), embeds the licence list (THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES) in the HTML as a <script type="text/plain" id="licenses"> block, because the build must stay one file (AC-NFR-L04-1 reads it from there and from package-lock.json).
  5. No frameworks, no runtime dependencies. Runtime dependency count is zero; THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES states that.
  6. Dev dependencies and licences (checked 2026-10-13 from the lockfile in the skeleton; re-verify at install):
    • esbuild 0.25.10 - MIT (https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/main/LICENSE.md, 2026-10-13).
    • playwright (e2e only, not in the skeleton package.json; the smoke test imports it) - Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/LICENSE, 2026-10-13). Pin an exact version when added; allowed by NFR-L04.
    • Unit tests use the built-in node:test and node:assert runner (no dependency).
  7. Test layers: Unit in test/*.test.js (Node, no DOM); E2E in e2e/*.mjs (Playwright, Chromium + Firefox + WebKit, against dist/index.html, both over http and file://). Fixtures in test/fixtures/.
  8. Style swap: the rendering style is selected behind a Style interface (ADR-0002 section 7, ADR-0004). The art-direction pick (variants A painterly, B pixel, C vector) is a configuration choice, not a stack decision. All three can be built; the build embeds only the chosen style once picked (--style= flag in build.mjs, default until the pick: the vector style, the cheapest to produce procedurally).
  9. Hosting/preview: static hosting only (pack preview workflow). No public release is implied (Q6 PROXY answer).

Consequences

  • Zero runtime dependency risk; licence list is trivial.
  • We own the game loop, input, audio, UI and sprite generation. This is the main cost and is planned as explicit work packages (../50-plan.md).
  • The single-file constraint means no fetch of neighbouring files and no worker script files; any Web Worker must be created from a Blob URL (CSP then needs worker-src blob:; decision deferred, not planned for MVP).
  • Cheats and the test hook ship in the production bundle and are gated at runtime by ?test=1 only (ADR-0003). This is acceptable for a single-player offline game with no server; it is stated here because NFR-S01 says "off in normal play" and the spec tests exactly that.
  • Size budget: the bundle without art files should be well under 1 MB (ceiling 10 MB, AC-R-111-2). Generated art adds load-time CPU, not bytes (ADR-0004 gives the time budget).
  • Playwright's browser downloads are blocked or limited in some environments; E2E stays runnable with whatever engines are installed, the CI reference runner installs all three (spec QF-10-4 stays open).
ADR-0002-architecture.md

ADR-0002 Architecture

Date: 2026-10-13. Status: proposed. Depends on ADR-0001. Test surface names follow ../30-spec/10-tech-and-testability.md ("Test contract"); where this ADR renames or fixes an open point, it says so in section 11.

Context

Requirements that drive the structure: fixed-timestep simulation separate from rendering (R-113), same seed + same inputs = same state, identical across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and Node (R-120, AC-NFR-Q01-2), a Node-only unit surface with no window/document/AudioContext (AC-R-113-2), 50 active monsters at 60 fps (NFR-P01), floor generation under 500 ms (NFR-P03), and a rendering style that is not yet chosen (art variants A painterly, B pixel, C vector). The game is large, so the module boundaries must let several implementer runs work in parallel without touching each other's files.

Decision overview

Three layers with a one-way dependency rule:

 shell (browser only)         render/ input/ audio/ ui/ save/ testhook/ main.js
        |  reads state, sends input commands, subscribes to events
        v
 core (pure, deterministic)   src/core/**   no DOM, no Date, no Math.random, no Web APIs
        ^
 content (data only)          src/core/content/**   registries + config + strings
  • core imports only core and content. A unit test (test/layering.test.js) greps import specifiers and forbidden globals in src/core/** and fails the build on violation (AC-R-113-2 in spirit).
  • render, input, audio, ui, save may import core; core never imports them.
  • Rendering style lives only under src/render/styles/<id>/ and is reached through one interface (section 7).

1. Game state, step and the loop

  • State is one plain JSON-serialisable object (no functions, classes, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, cycles, undefined, NaN): AC-R-121-2. Shape = the spec snapshot (tick, seed, scene, paused, depth, player, monsters, projectiles, groundItems, containers, floor, inventory, equipment, belt, stash, vendors, events, floaters, ui, options, config ...). getState() is structuredClone of it (plus conversions listed below); it is the same object the renderer reads, so there is no second model.
  • Derived caches (walkability grid as Uint8Array, spatial hash, path scratch buffers) live in a non-serialised context object ctx kept in a WeakMap<state, ctx> inside core/ctx.js. They are rebuilt from state on demand (ensureCtx(state)), so structuredCloned or loaded states work.
  • floor.tiles is a plain number[] of length w*h (row-major) so it round-trips JSON.
  • API (all in src/core/index.js):
    • newGame(seed, opts) -> state (opts.class, default the one MVP class).
    • applyInput(state, input) -> void: applies one input command immediately (sets intent: target, path, panel toggle, ...). Does not advance time. Appends to state.events (for example noPath).
    • step(state, inputs = []) -> state: clears state.events, applies inputs in order, then runs exactly one simulation tick, tick += 1. It mutates state in place and returns the same reference (a deep copy per tick for 50 monsters plus a 3,600-cell floor would waste the 4 ms per tick budget, AC-NFR-P01-2). Tests that need the pre-step state call cloneState(state) first. The spec text "returning a new state" is amended accordingly (section 11).
    • snapshot(state) -> object, hashState(state) -> string, cloneState(state).
    • generateFloor(seed, depth), findPath(grid, from, to, opts), rollItem(rng, ctx), createRng(seed), registries content.*, config.
  • When paused (state.paused), step does nothing but process UI-only inputs (open panels, move items, unpause); tick and all entity state stay untouched (AC-NFR-A02-1, AC-NFR-A02-3, AC-R-020-3).
  • Fixed timestep: config.tickHz = 60. The loop accumulator is a pure function in src/core/clock.js: advance(acc, dtMs, tickHz) -> { acc, ticks } using integer-friendly arithmetic: acc += dtMs * tickHz; ticks = floor(acc / 1000); acc -= ticks * 1000. Any chunking of the same total elapsed time yields the same tick count (AC-R-113-1). The browser loop caps catch-up at config.maxCatchupTicks (5) per frame and drops the rest (tab was in background), which lives in src/main.js, not in the pure function.
  • Interpolated rendering: each moving entity stores prev (value at the start of the tick) and current position. The renderer draws at alpha = acc / (1000 / tickHz). Render never writes to state.
  • Order of systems in one tick (fixed, listed in core/step.js; entities within a system iterate in array order which is creation order, i.e. id order, AC-R-020-2):
    1. clearEvents, apply inputs
    2. playerIntent (resolve click target to move/attack/pickup/interact; hold repeat)
    3. monsterAI (notice, chase, attack, flee; pack wake)
    4. movement (player, then monsters; tile-to-tile)
    5. combat (swing timers, hit resolution)
    6. projectiles
    7. status (stagger, regen, cooldowns, buffs)
    8. loot (drops, pickups, gold)
    9. cleanup (remove dead after config.deathTicks, floater timers)
    10. scene (death, victory, floor change, autosave request flag)
  • Errors: the browser loop wraps step in try/catch. On a throw it sets scene = 'error', keeps the last good serialised save, and shows the error screen with an "export save" action (AC-NFR-Q02-1). cheat.throwInTick() sets a flag that makes the next tick throw.

2. Determinism rules (hard rules, enforced by tests)

  1. All randomness comes from createRng. State holds named streams, each a {s} integer (mulberry32 state): rng.world, rng.combat, rng.loot, rng.ai. Separate streams keep floor generation, loot and combat from perturbing each other. Per-floor generation uses a derived seed floorSeed = hash32(seed, depth), so a floor regenerates identically on re-entry (R-044). createRng gains getState()/setState() (the skeleton closure has none); the 5-value golden test (AC-R-120-4) fixes the mulberry32 sequence.
  2. No Date, performance, Math.random, setTimeout or requestAnimationFrame inside core.
  3. No transcendental math in core: no Math.sin/cos/atan2/pow/exp/log/hypot (results may differ in the last bit between engines). Only + - * /, Math.sqrt, floor/ceil/round/min/max/abs. Directions use an 8-way integer table; projectile direction is normalised with sqrt. test/layering.test.js greps for the forbidden calls.
  4. Movement and timing are integer ticks wherever possible. Actors are tile-based: an actor stands on an integer tile and moves to a neighbour over config.moveTicksPerTile ticks (diagonals round(moveTicksPerTile * 1.4142)), with moveT as an integer counter. pos (float) is derived for rendering/spec (pos = tile + (next - tile) * moveT / total). Projectiles are the only continuous bodies.
  5. State hash: hashState(state) = FNV-1a 32-bit (two lanes for 64 bits) over a canonical JSON string with sorted keys, excluding ui.tooltip, ui.hud layout caches and perf. Golden hash in test/fixtures/run-a.hash.
  6. Iteration order is always array order or sorted by id; never Object.keys order of dynamically-keyed maps without sorting.

3. Entity model

Plain objects in typed arrays-of-objects on state (monsters, projectiles, groundItems, containers, npcs, props), ids from state.nextId ("m12"). No ECS framework, no classes. "Systems" are functions (state, ctx) => void in src/core/systems/*.js. A monster is data (type, tile, hp, ai, target, cooldowns, packId, mods[]); its behaviour is looked up from content.monsters[type] (stats, behaviour id, attack kind). Adding a monster type is a data change plus (optionally) a behaviour in systems/ai/behaviours.js.

4. Isometric projection

2:1 diamond tiles, tile footprint 64 x 32 logical px (config.render.tileW = 64, tileH = 32). In src/render/iso.js (pure, no DOM, Node-testable, used by input, render, tests):

tileToScreen(tx, ty, cam) = { x: (tx - ty) * tileW/2 - cam.x, y: (tx + ty) * tileH/2 - cam.y }   // tile centre; ty,tx may be fractional
screenToTile(sx, sy, cam) : u = (sx + cam.x) / (tileW/2), v = (sy + cam.y) / (tileH/2);
                            tx = (u + v) / 2, ty = (v - u) / 2     // fractional; floor() for the tile

Camera cam follows the interpolated player position and clamps at floor bounds. render/view.js owns the logical-to-device scale: the canvas fills the viewport (canvas.width = innerWidth * dpr), logical height targets 720 with an integer-or-half-step scale chosen from viewport size (1280x720 to 3840x2160, AC-R-112-3). screenToTile(tileToScreen(t)) == t is a unit test (AC-R-112-3 round trip). Picking priority (monster sprite bounds, then ground item label, then NPC/prop, then tile) is in input/pick.js, using sprite bounds from the active style's atlas so a click on a tall sprite works.

Depth sorting: painter's order by (tx + ty) of the entity's foot tile, ties by ty, then id. Floor tiles are drawn first from a cached chunk layer (16x16-tile offscreen chunks, built lazily, invalidated on floor change); walls, props, entities and projectiles go into one sorted draw list per frame, culled to the viewport. Occlusion fade: walls within 2 tiles in front of the player are drawn at reduced alpha (render-only).

5. Pathfinding, collisions, line of sight

  • A\* on the tile grid in core/path.js: 8-neighbour, no corner cutting (both orthogonal neighbours must be walkable), integer costs 10/14, octile heuristic, binary min-heap, deterministic tie-break (f, h, index). Signature findPath(grid, from, to, {maxNodes, blocked}) -> tile[] | null. Unreachable goals return null after exhausting the open set (under 50 ms on 100x100, AC-R-005-9); monsters pass maxNodes: config.ai.maxPathNodes and re-path at most every config.ai.repathTicks ticks.
  • Occupancy: one tile holds at most one actor; a Int16Array occupancy map in ctx is updated on tile entry/exit. Props and walls are static blockers in the same grid.
  • Spatial hash: uniform grid, bucket = 8x8 tiles, rebuilt at the start of each tick in id order (cheap at a few hundred entities). Used for notice radius, AoE, projectile hit tests, click picking and "nearest monster". core/spatial.js.
  • Line of sight: integer Bresenham between tile centres (core/los.js) used by AI notice and ranged attacks; the same function marks tiles explored (bit array stored as a string of 0/1 per row to stay JSON-friendly) within config.sightRadius.
  • Click on an unreachable tile (QF-01-2, decision): walk to the nearest reachable tile within radius config.clickSnapRadius (3); if none, stay and emit noPath. Switchable by config.

6. Procedural floor generation (core/gen/)

generateFloor(seed, depth) -> floor (pure, no render knowledge):

  1. Grid config.floorSize (default 56x56). Theme from depth (open-plan floors 1-4, basement 5-8; lobby is the hand-authored town, core/town.js).
  2. Rooms + corridors: place N non-overlapping rectangular rooms by rejection sampling (attempt cap), assign a room kind from the theme's kind table (cubicle-maze, meeting-room, copy-room, storage, server-room, break-room), join rooms in order of a minimum spanning tree over centre distances plus a few extra edges for loops, carve L-shaped corridors (width 1-2), add doors where corridors cross walls.
  3. Validation: flood fill from entry; every room, stair and prop that must be reachable is checked; on failure retry with the next sub-seed up to config.maxGenAttempts, then fall back to a known-good fixed layout (never throws).
  4. Stairs: entry in the room farthest from exit by path length (BFS), exit likewise; the safe radius config.safeRadius around entry has no monsters.
  5. Props (office-themed decoration): per room kind from content.props (desks, cubicle walls, copiers, plants, filing cabinets, vending machines, server racks, boxes). Each prop has blocks: bool; blocking props never disconnect the floor (validated again after placement).
  6. Population: a difficulty budget by depth fills monster packs and singles from content.monsters filtered by theme and depth, champions per config.championChance, containers (S2), all via rng.world.
  7. Output is plain data: {depth, seed, theme, w, h, tiles[], rooms[{kind,x,y,w,h}], entry, exit, props[], spawns[], explored[]}. Tile codes (0 void, 1 floor, 2 wall, 3 door, 4 stairs-up, 5 stairs-down) are constants in core/tiles.js. The renderer derives wall orientation from neighbours; the generator never decides pixels.

7. Style isolation (art direction not yet chosen)

Everything that decides how the game looks is behind one interface, so swapping variant A/B/C is a build/config change plus one folder:

// src/render/style.js  (JSDoc contract)
// Style = {
//   id: 'painterly' | 'pixel' | 'vector',
//   logicalTile: {w:64, h:32},          // must stay 64x32 (geometry is not style)
//   palette: {...},                      // incl. colour-blind-safe rarity encodings (NFR-A03)
//   build(progress): Promise<Atlas>      // draws every sprite into offscreen canvases, yielding between batches
// }
// Atlas.get(key) -> { img, sx, sy, sw, sh, ox, oy }   // ox,oy = anchor offset to the foot point
// Atlas.frames(key) -> number

Sprite keys are semantic, never file names or style details: tile:<theme>:<kind>:<variant>, wall:<theme>:<mask>, prop:<id>, mon:<type>:<anim>:<dir>:<frame>, plr:<class>:<anim>:<dir>:<frame> (anims: idle, walk, attack, hit, death; 8 directions, 5 stored + mirrored), proj:<id>:<frame>, item:<base> (inventory icon), fx:<id>:<frame>, ui:<id>, npc:<id>. The renderer (render/world.js, render/hud.js, render/fx.js) knows keys and geometry only. Shared, style-neutral helpers live in render/draw/ (seeded noise, polygon/outline helpers, rig.js = skeleton poses per animation frame so body animation is written once and each style only decides how to paint limbs and torso). Styles live in render/styles/{painterly,pixel,vector}/. Selection: config.render.style, overridable with ?style= in test mode (art review harness), and build.mjs --style= to embed only one.

Nothing in core knows the style. The only coupling is content ids (monster types, item bases, prop ids): a style must provide a sprite for every id in the registries. Canvas is not available in Node (no dependency is added for it), so completeness is checked in E2E (e2e/atlas.mjs): every registry id resolves to an atlas entry in the chosen style. A Node test checks that the registry ids and the sprite-key builders (render/keys.js, pure) agree.

8. Input

src/input/ converts DOM events to input commands (plain objects) and never touches state directly: {t:'mouse', tile, screen, button, down}, {t:'key', code, phase:'down'|'up'|'press'}, {t:'uiClick', region, button}, {t:'uiDrag', ...}, {t:'pause'}. HUD hit-regions come from ui/layout.js (pure function layout(state, viewport) -> regions[]), so UI picking is unit-testable. Key bindings: options.keys (action -> KeyboardEvent.code), defaults in config.defaultKeys; input/keymap.js maps code -> action; core receives actions, not raw codes, for game keys (rebinding is invisible to core, AC-NFR-A01). Mouse buttons are fixed (NFR-A01).

Held-button repeat lives in core (state.input.mouse = {down, button, tile}) so it is deterministic and works under step(n) (AC-R-005-6).

9. Event bus for audio and FX hooks

Core emits data, not callbacks: state.events (this tick's list: {type:'hit', source, target, value}, kill, miss, levelup, pickup, noMana, noPath, inventoryFull, stairs, bossPhase, ...). A rolling state.eventLog (last 256 events, non-contract, for bots and debugging) is kept too. After every tick the shell passes state.events to src/bus.js, a ~30-line synchronous pub/sub (on(type, fn), emit). Subscribers: audio cues (audio/cues.js maps event type -> SFX id and volume), render FX (particles, hit flashes, screen shake request), UI notices. Because core never calls subscribers, it stays deterministic and testable; audio/FX cannot break the simulation. In step(n) batches the shell dispatches events for every tick (audio may be muted in test mode).

Floaters (damage numbers), ui.notice and ui.fx.shake are state because the spec snapshots them (AC-R-025-1, AC-R-025-3); particles and camera easing are render-only.

10. Source layout

See ../50-plan.md section "Source tree". Summary: src/core/ (state, systems, gen, path, content), src/render/ (iso, view, world, hud, fx, styles), src/input/, src/audio/ (pure sample synthesis + WebAudio engine), src/ui/ (layout, panels, DOM screens, string table access), src/save/, src/testhook/, src/main.js, test/, e2e/, bot/.

11. Decisions on open points from the spec (spec files to be updated mechanically)

PointDecision
step(state, inputs) "returns a new state"Mutates in place, returns the same reference. cloneState for copies. Equality assertions (AC-R-113-1 "deep-equal") are unaffected.
QF-10-5 test flag?test=1 confirmed (ADR-0003).
QF-02-1 hit chancehitChance = clamp(2 * A/(A+D) * La/(La+Ld), config.hitChanceMin, config.hitChanceMax); A = attack rating (base + agility x config.ar.perAgility + gear), D = defence, L = level; defaults 0.05..0.95. Monotonic as required by AC-R-021-3.
QF-01-2 click on wallnearest reachable tile within 3, else noPath.
QF-01-4 skill keys vs potion keysPotions 1..4; skills on Q W E R. (Proposal accepted for architecture; spec/UI to confirm.)
QF-01-6 rebind collisionReject with ui.notice (spec proposal).
QF-04-5 boss depthconfig.bossDepth = 8, boss arena is floor 8's exit room.
QF-04-6 ground items on re-entryFloor regenerates from seed, cleared monsters stay cleared (stored in state.floors[depth].cleared), ground items do not persist.
QF-01-1 town stairs targetconfig.townStairsTarget = 'deepest'.
QF-10-1 perf referenceAccepted as proposed; E2E perf checks are advisory on non-reference runners.

Consequences

  • Core runs at thousands of ticks per second in Node, so the bot can play whole runs headlessly (ADR-0003).
  • The determinism rules cost some convenience (no trig in core, tile-based movement); they buy cross-engine hash equality, which is a stated acceptance criterion.
  • UI drawn on canvas means we write a small hit-region system and tooltips ourselves; in return drag/drop of grid items and the pause-with-panels case are simple state transformations that are testable in Node.
  • Three styles can coexist in the repo during art review without touching core.
  • Risk: sprite generation time on load (ADR-0004 gives a budget and a progress screen).
ADR-0003-test-hook.md

ADR-0003 Test hook (window.__app) and the scripted bot player

Date: 2026-10-13. Status: proposed. Depends on ADR-0002. Implements R-120..R-123, NFR-S01, AC-NFR-Q01. The member names are those of ../30-spec/10-tech-and-testability.md ("Test contract"); the short aliases requested by the harness (clickTile, clickScreen, setSeed, pause) are added as thin wrappers so nothing in the spec has to be renamed.

Context

Agents (the Playwright suite and the customer-proxy "bot player") must be able to read the whole game state, send the same inputs a human can, and advance time deterministically. The hook must be absent in normal play (AC-R-123-1, AC-NFR-S01-1), must not change simulation results, and must work from file://.

Decision

Activation

  • ?test=1 enables the hook. Parsed once at boot in src/testhook/index.js from location.search. Without it window.__app is never assigned (undefined).
  • Optional parameters (only read when test=1): seed=<int> (initial seed shown on title; newGame still needed to start, AC-R-120-1), style=<id> (art review), realtime=1 (see below), mute=1.
  • Manual clock by default in test mode. With ?test=1 the requestAnimationFrame loop still renders but does not advance the simulation; ticks happen only through step(n). This makes step(n) exact (AC-R-121-3), makes runs independent of frame rate (AC-R-113-3) and removes flakiness. ?test=1&realtime=1 runs the normal accumulator loop as well (for a human or bot watching, and for the frame-time perf check perf()); in that mode step(n) adds n ticks on top and tests that need exactness must not use it.
  • After each __app call that changes state, the hook requests one render so screenshots are current.

API (all synchronous, return JSON-serialisable values)

MemberBehaviour
describe()Array of {name, kind:'fn'|'obj', doc} for every member below; test asserts each listed function exists (AC-R-121-1).
getState()snapshot(state): a structuredClone of core state with derived fields filled (player.pos, tile, floor minus nothing). JSON round-trip safe (AC-R-121-2). getState().hash is hashState.
newGame({seed, class})Create a run (title -> floor in S1, town from S2). Returns the snapshot.
setSeed(n)Alias for newGame({seed:n, class: current class}); also stores n as the seed shown at the title.
step(n)Run exactly n ticks via core step (stops early only if scene becomes error), dispatch events to the bus after every tick, render once, return the snapshot. While paused, ticks do not advance (AC-NFR-A02-1).
click({tile:{x,y}} | {screen:{x,y}}, {button=0, hold=false})Builds the same input command a DOM event would (screen goes through screenToTile with the current camera and UI hit-regions, exactly like a real mouse event), then applyInput immediately (no tick). So player.target/path are updated before the next step (AC-R-005-2). hold:true leaves the button down until the next click/key release call or mouseUp().
clickTile(x, y, opts?)click({tile:{x,y}}, opts).
clickScreen(x, y, opts?)click({screen:{x,y}}, opts). Coordinates are CSS pixels of the canvas.
mouseMove(screen|tile), mouseUp()Move the held cursor (AC-R-005-6) / release the button.
key(code, phase='press')Same as a keyboard event with KeyboardEvent.code semantics ('KeyI', 'Digit1', 'Escape', 'Tab'), passed through the key map so rebinding works.
pause()Toggles pause exactly like key('Escape') and returns paused.
cmd.moveTo(tile), cmd.attack(monsterId), cmd.use(itemId)Agent commands (R-121). Validate arguments, then issue the same input a click would. Return {ok:true} or {ok:false, error:'<non-empty text>'} and never throw or change state on failure (AC-R-121-7). More commands may be added (cmd.pickup(id), cmd.descend(), cmd.skill(id, tile)); they must be listed in describe().
cheat.spawnItem(spec), spawnMonster(type,tile), setLevel(n), setHp(n), giveGold(n), teleportFloor(depth), throwInTick()Debug cheats (R-123). They write through core functions in src/core/cheats.js (so they are Node-testable) and go through the same validation: no hostile spawn in town (QF-04-1), occupied tile rejected.
save.write(), save.read(), save.export(), save.import(text)Bridge to src/save/ (S3).
audio.getState(){ctxState, master, sfx, ambient, muted, effectiveGain, cueLog[]} read from the real GainNodes (S3).
perf(){frameMs[], simMsPerTick, samples} from the render loop and step timing.

All state changes go through applyInput/step, never by assigning to state fields from the hook, except the cheats (documented, test mode only).

How Playwright tests use it

// e2e/helpers.mjs
export async function open(browser, {seed = 1, style} = {}) {
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  const errors = [];
  page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push(e.message));
  page.on('console', m => m.type() === 'error' && errors.push(m.text()));
  await page.goto(pathToFileURL(resolve('dist/index.html')).href + `?test=1&seed=${seed}`);
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__app?.getState().scene === 'title');
  const app = (fn, ...args) => page.evaluate(([f, a]) => f.split('.').reduce((o, k) => o[k], window.__app)(...a), [fn, args]);
  return { page, app, errors };
}
// test
const { app } = await open(browser, { seed: 7 });
await app('newGame', { seed: 7 });
const s0 = await app('step', 120);
assert.equal(s0.tick, 120);
await app('clickTile', 12, 9);
const s1 = await app('step', 200);

Rules for tests: assert on getState() fields, not on pixels, except the checks that name pixels (AC-R-112-2 colour count, art review screenshots by the independent reviewer); never use waitForTimeout for game time (use step); compare runs with getState().hash; run each engine with the same file.

Scripted bot player ("customer proxy plays")

Two executors share one pure policy:

  • bot/policy.js: decide(snapshot, memory) -> command | null, where a command is {type:'moveTo'|'attack'|'pickup'|'use'|'descend'|'equip'|'spendPoints'|'wait', ...}. Pure, no I/O, written against the documented snapshot only (so it is a faithful test of what the contract exposes). Heuristics: heal below a HP fraction using belt potions, attack the nearest living monster in sight, pick up items/gold, equip upgrades by a simple score, spend attribute/skill points by a fixed build, head for the exit when the floor is cleared or explored, return to town to sell when the inventory is full, stop at victory or death.
  • bot/run-headless.mjs (Node): imports src/core directly, loops decide -> applyInput -> step(state) for up to N ticks, no browser. Thousands of ticks per second; used for balance (R-006 run length via tick / tickHz, QF-01-5), regressions, soak tests and for generating the golden run-a fixture. Writes a JSON report (bot/out/*.json: seed, ticks, deepest depth, deaths, items found, time in each state, uncaught errors).
  • bot/run-browser.mjs (Playwright): drives window.__app through the same decide, takes a screenshot every K ticks to bot/out/shots/ for the visual reviewer and records page errors. It proves that what the headless bot can do is also possible through the real page.

The bot only uses cmd.*, click*, key, step, getState (and optionally cheat.* to jump to a scenario, flagged in the report). Findings go to the harness learnings log; the bot is a harness test subject (project brief) and is never shipped (bot/ is outside src/).

Determinism cross-check

test/fixtures/run-a.json is a list of {tick, inputs[]} entries recorded once from the bot. test/replay.test.js (Node) replays it and compares hashState to run-a.hash; e2e/replay.mjs does the same through __app in each engine (AC-R-120-2, AC-R-122-1, AC-NFR-Q01-1/2).

Consequences

  • The hook is a thin adapter over core functions; there is no logic in it to get wrong. Two exceptions: coordinates conversion (clickScreen) and event dispatch, both covered by E2E.
  • Cheats ship in the bundle behind the flag. If this is judged unacceptable at release, a build flag can strip src/testhook/cheats for a "release" build while the spec's "production build" tests run on the normal build (npm run build -- --no-testhook); not planned for MVP.
  • Manual clock in test mode means a human opening ?test=1 sees a frozen game until realtime=1 is added. Documented in the README of the hook.
  • Slice order: S1 ships describe, getState, newGame, step, click*, key, pause, cmd.moveTo/attack, cheat.spawnMonster, setSeed, perf; cmd.use, other cheats arrive with S2; save.*, audio.getState, cheat.throwInTick with S3.
ADR-0004-assets.md

ADR-0004 Assets: everything generated in code

Date: 2026-10-13. Status: proposed. Implements NFR-L01, AC-NFR-L01-2/-3, R-111, R-080/R-081 and the Q2/Q5 PROXY answers. Interacts with the open art-direction pick (variants A painterly, B pixel, C vector).

Context

The game must ship as one HTML file with no image, audio or font files and no third-party assets (NFR-L01; AC-R-111-1 opens it from file://; AC-NFR-L01-3 checks that no asset requests occur). Art is produced by agents as code. The visual style is still to be chosen, so the generation pipeline must not bake one style in.

Decision

Graphics

  1. No image files, no font files, no <img>. Every sprite, tile, icon and UI element is drawn at load into offscreen canvases (OffscreenCanvas where available, else document.createElement('canvas'); both feature-detected) by the active Style (ADR-0002 section 7).
  2. Atlas: the style's build(progress) draws sprites into pages of at most 2048x2048 px, keeps a map key -> {page, sx, sy, sw, sh, ox, oy} and returns the Atlas. The renderer only calls atlas.get(key). Keys are semantic (mon:temp-worker:walk:SE:3), defined in render/keys.js.
  3. Animation economy: characters are drawn from a shared skeleton rig (render/draw/rig.js) per animation frame; 5 stored directions, 3 mirrored; frame counts: idle 4, walk 8, attack 6, hit 2, death 6. Tiles have 2-4 variants chosen by a position hash (render-only). Walls are drawn per neighbour mask.
  4. Seeded generation, separate stream: art uses its own RNG (createRng(artSeed), artSeed constant per style), not the game RNG, and is never part of the state hash. Same style + same engine = same pixels (screenshots comparable within an engine).
  5. Load budget: atlas build target at most 1.5 s on the CI reference runner and at most 3 s on a mid-range laptop (NFR-P02 allows 5 s total load). The build yields to the event loop between batches (await nextFrame()) and drives a progress bar on the title screen. A budget test in E2E records the atlas build time (perf().atlasMs) and fails above the ceiling. If the budget is exceeded, the fallback is lazy generation of far-away animations (death, hit) on first use.
  6. Memory: pages stay alive for the session (about 4 pages x 16 MB); no per-frame canvas allocation; floors' ground layer chunks are pooled and dropped on floor change (NFR-P05).
  7. Accessibility in art: rarity is encoded by colour and border pattern/label prefix (NFR-A03); health vs mana by shape and fill. The palette of each style is checked against deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulations in test/palette.test.js (pure colour math, no canvas).
  8. UI text is drawn with the system font stack through canvas fillText and DOM text; no webfont, no network. Minimum 14 px at 1080p, size option (NFR-A04). All strings come from core/content/strings.js (NFR-A06).
  9. Review loop: ?test=1&style=<id> plus e2e/art-sheet.mjs renders a contact sheet (all sprites by key prefix) and a set of in-game screenshots per style for the independent visual reviewer. The art-direction variants (A/B/C) are implemented as render/styles/<id>/ against this contract; the selected one becomes the default and the others are dropped from the build (build.mjs --style=).

Audio

  1. WebAudio synthesis, no files. src/audio/synth.js is pure: renderSfx(id, sampleRate) -> Float32Array and renderAmbient(zone, seed, seconds, sampleRate) -> Float32Array using oscillators, filtered noise and envelopes written as plain math over arrays, with their own seeded RNG. They run in Node (tests: non-silent, no NaN, peak at most 1.0, expected duration, deterministic per id/seed, spectral sanity checks by simple band energy).
  2. Engine: src/audio/engine.js creates the AudioContext lazily on the first user gesture (autoplay policy), converts synthesised arrays to AudioBuffers once at load (pre-rendered SFX bank; ambient loops rendered for 20-30 s per zone, looped, rendered in chunks to avoid long frames), and plays cues through gain buses master -> {sfx, ambient}. Cue variation (pitch +-5%, gain +-10%) uses the render-side RNG.
  3. Cues from events: audio/cues.js maps bus events (ADR-0002 section 9) to SFX ids (attack swing, hit, miss, monster death, pickup, gold, UI click, level up, potion, stairs, boss phase); town and floor ambience by zone; priority and a per-id rate limit (e.g. at most 4 voices of the same id within 80 ms) to protect against 50 monsters.
  4. Controls: master, effects, ambient sliders and mute in options; persisted with options (R-082). Pause suspends the context (AC-NFR-A02-2). audio.getState() reads real gain values (test hook).
  5. Music beyond generative ambience stays "could" (Q5).

Licences and records

ASSET-LICENCES.md states: no third-party assets; everything generated; list of generators. THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES lists build tools only (ADR-0001). The denylist scan (AC-NFR-L01-1, AC-NFR-L05-1) runs over content.strings, registry names, sprite keys and source file names.

Options considered

OptionVerdict
Pre-drawn PNG/SVG files embedded as data URIsRejected: still third-party-style assets to author and licence, no cheap style swap, inflates the bundle.
Runtime SVG for spritesRejected as primary: rasterisation cost and cross-engine differences; allowed inside a style as a drawing technique if it rasterises into the atlas once.
Tone.js or other audio libraryRejected: runtime dependency for something ~500 lines of plain math cover; pure synthesis is Node-testable.
Sample files / CC0 packsRejected for MVP (NFR-L01 default is code-generated only).

Consequences

  • Style swap is local to render/styles/<id>/; core, input and audio are unaffected.
  • First load does CPU work (atlas + audio bank). It is bounded and visible (progress bar). It is the main schedule risk for the "5 s load" goal.
  • Quality of generated art/sound is the biggest uncertainty; the plan (../50-plan.md) reserves a work package per slice for art polish after the style pick, and a separate visual-review gate.
  • Sample-accurate audio assertions are not attempted in E2E (headless audio devices differ); gain nodes and the cue log are asserted instead.
ADR-0005-classes-and-skill-trees.md

ADR-0005 Classes and skill trees: one data model, a handful of effect archetypes

Date: 2026-10-14. Status: proposed (plan gate for rounds R4-R6). Owner: architect. Implements R-200..R-209, R-231, R-232, R-233, R-234 (area M). Customer answers are binding: circles/circle-02.md (PROXY, 2026-10-14) Q1 (three classes, Clerk retired, refund), Q2 (3 branches, about 10 skills, 3 tiers at levels 1/8/16, 1 point per level, 29 points at cap 30, max skill level 5, capstones single level, one earlier skill plus a level gate, synergies optional), Q3 (free respec in town), Q4 (items shared, class-tagged affixes only). This ADR decides technical shape only; names, numbers and wording that the customer owns are listed under "Questions for the customer" and the design works with either answer. Interacts with: ADR-0002 (pure core, data-driven content, events), ADR-0003 (test hook), ADR-0004 (assets in code), ADR-0006 (slots, save version 2).

Context

Today (read from the code, 2026-10-14):

  • content/classes.js holds one class {id, name, kind, attrs}; newGame builds the player from it; save/format.js validates class against that list.
  • content/skills.js is flat: 1 basic, 4 actives (effect: projectile, burst, heal, crowd-control) and 2 passives (stat, perLevel). Values are functions (lin(base, per)), so they cannot be serialised, listed in a tooltip generically or checked by a data test. systems/skills.js has one if branch per effect; derive.js reads passives through passiveSkills; the skill panel is a flat list (ui/panels.js renderSkills).
  • learnSkill checks only points and max level. There is no tree, no prerequisite, no level gate, no respec, no timed buff, no summon, no trap, no dash, no damage type on skills (the config already has damageTypes: fire, cold, shock, acid for item resist, but monsters have no resist table).
  • muteT is the one monster status; the boss is exempt.

Thirty skills written as thirty if branches would be thirty code paths to test, balance and render. The goal is thirty rows of data over about nine code paths.

Decision

1. Class definition (src/core/content/classes.js)

{
  id: "facilities-manager",            // stable key; saves and slot index store this
  name: "Facilities Manager",          // working name (brand escalation, R-233); display only
  role: "melee",                        // melee | ranged | caster  (tag on the selection card, bot policy default)
  blurbKey: "classFacilitiesBlurb",     // strings table key (UI owns the words)
  figureKey: "hero.facilities-manager", // renderer sprite-set key; also used for the card portrait
  attrs: { grit: 16, agility: 8, stamina: 14, focus: 6 },       // starting attributes (sum 44 for all three; tuning in R6)
  derived: { hpPerLevel: 14, mpPerLevel: 3, hpPerStamina: 3, mpPerFocus: 2, unarmed: { min: 2, max: 4 } }, // optional overrides of config.derived, merged key by key
  basic: "strike",                      // id of the free basic attack: "strike" (melee), "toss" (ranged, paper), "zap" (ranged, mana-free, short)
  startKit: { weapon: "pipe-wrench", healthPotions: 2, manaPotions: 0, extra: [] }, // base ids from content/items.js
  signature: "pallet-slam",             // tier-1 active, granted free at level 1, never refunded
  branches: ["maintenance", "safety", "logistics"],  // ordered tab order; the tree lives in content/skilltrees/<class>.js
  affixTag: "facilities",               // class tag for class-tagged affixes (section 7)
  bot: { stance: "melee", kite: 0, potionHp: 0.4, manaReserve: 0.15,
         priority: ["demolition-day", "floor-buffer", "pallet-slam", "coffee-break"], buildOrder: ["pallet-slam", "dress-code", "floor-buffer", "fire-drill"] }, // policy hints for bot/policy.js
}

Rules: ids are kebab-case and unique; the three attrs sums are equal (parity check in the data test); derived keys are a subset of config.derived; startKit bases exist; signature is in the class's own tree at tier 1; figureKey must exist in the atlas (R-232 atlas test). Exports: classes, classById, defaultClass (first class, used by fixtures and old tests; fixtures keep working with class: "facilities-manager"), retiredClasses = { clerk: { migrateTo: "facilities-manager" } }.

The attribute names stay Grit, Agility, Stamina, Focus (Q4). Classes differ by start values, growth (derived), basic attack, kit, signature and tree. Item requirements are class-independent.

2. Skill tree schema (src/core/content/skilltrees/{facilities,sales,it}.js, merged by content/skills.js)

The tree is plain JSON-able data: no functions. A numeric value that grows with skill level is a curve [base, perLevel] (optionally [base, perLevel, cap]), evaluated by one helper at(curve, level) = min(cap, base + perLevel * (level - 1)). This replaces lin().

{
  id: "floor-buffer", class: "facilities-manager", branch: "maintenance",
  tier: 2, col: 1,                       // tier 1..3 = row in the panel, col 0..2 = column; UI draws edges from `requires`
  name: "Floor Buffer Sweep", textKey: "skillFloorBufferText",
  kind: "active",                        // basic | active | passive | aura
  archetype: "area",                     // projectile | area | self | buff | aura | summon | dash | trap | passive | melee (section 3)
  maxLevel: 5,                           // 1 for capstones; never above config.skillMaxLevel
  reqLevel: 8,                           // character level gate; tiers default to config.skillTiers = [1, 8, 16]
  requires: [{ id: "pallet-slam", level: 1 }],   // all must be learned at least to this level; same branch only
  tags: ["physical", "area", "heavy"],  // free tags; used by class-tagged affixes ("+x% heavy skill damage") and the UI filter
  cost: { mana: [8, 2], cooldown: 0, reservePct: 0 },   // cooldown in ticks (0 = none, QF-06-5); reservePct only for aura
  delivery: { ... },                     // archetype specific, section 3
  effects: [ ... ],                      // ordered list of ops, section 4
  synergy: [{ from: "pallet-slam", stat: "damagePct", perLevel: 6 }],  // optional (R-208, could): bonus per level of another skill
  fx: { cast: "fx:slam", hit: "fx:dust", icon: "floor-buffer" },       // render keys, section 6
}

Checks that the data test enforces (R-202..R-204, R-233): 3 branches per class; 10 skills per class (the exact count is a test constant so a later tweak is deliberate); skill ids unique across all classes; every requires exists in the same branch with lower tier (hence no cycles); reqLevel is not below the tier default; every branch has at least one active; maxLevel in 1..5; every textKey exists in strings; every fx.icon has an icon body; legal scan over names and texts (denylist). Point sanity: sum of maxLevel of a class tree is at least 1.3 times the 29 usable points, so a character cannot max everything and must choose a build.

Player state. player.skills = { [skillId]: level } stays (save-compatible shape). Unspent points stay in player.skillPoints. Learning rules (learnSkill, extended in systems/progression.js): the skill must belong to the player's class; reqLevel <= player.level; every prerequisite met; points at least 1; level below maxLevel; the signature is already at level 1 and costs nothing. Rejected learns spend nothing and return {ok:false, error} with a stable code (wrong-class, level-gate, prereq, no-points, max-level). Points: config.skillPointsPerLevel = 1, so a level-30 character has earned 29; the signature is free. Accounting invariant (R-205): sum(levels) - 1 + skillPoints === levelsGained, where the minus one is the signature.

Effective level. effLevel = learned > 0 ? learned + bonus : 0, where bonus comes from gear (section 7). The bonus is not capped by maxLevel (curves are linear with an optional cap); the panel shows 3 (+2).

3. Archetypes: the delivery side

Each archetype is a function in systems/skillfx.js (the new runner; systems/skills.js keeps castSkill as the entry and calls the runner). The runner replaces the current if (effect === ...) chain.

ArchetypeDelivery fieldsWhat the runner doesToday's skills it covers
projectilekind (FX key), speed, range, count (1), spreadDeg, pierce (0), chain (0 jumps, falloff)Fires count shots through fireProjectile; each carries the skill's effects as an on-hit list (pr.hit = {skill, level})Stapler Throw
areashape: burst/cone/ring, radius curve, at: self/target, los: true, linger: {ticks, every}Applies on-hit effects to every monster in range and line of sight; a linger leaves a ground zone (section 5)Reply-All, Mute
selfnoneApplies effects to the caster (heal, instant restore)Coffee Break
buffticks curveAdds a timed player.buffs[] entry (stat mods, absorb)new
auraradiusToggle (toggleAura): reserves reservePct of mpMax; while on, its stat mods apply to the hero and allies in radius; one aura at a timenew
summonunit (id in content/allies.js), count, max, ticksSpawns allies into state.allies (cap config.maxAllies = 4); allies follow, attack, expirenew
dashdistance curve, ticksMoves the hero along the line (walkable, in LOS) over a few ticks; applies effects to monsters crossed and at the endnew
traparmTicks, ttl, radius, maxPlaces a ground zone that triggers on the first monster insidenew
passivenoneNo cast; effects are stat mods or triggers, folded in by deriveStatsDress Code, Hustle
meleerange, coneOnly for basic attacks of other classes if needed; resolves through the existing swing pathStrike

Basic attacks stay kind: "basic", free, outside the 10: strike (melee, existing), toss (projectile, low damage, range about 7) and zap (projectile, short range). The click-to-attack path asks the class's basic archetype: melee walks adjacent; projectile stops in range and in line of sight and fires. The skill bar primary is the class basic.

4. Effects: the "what happens" side

An effect is { op, ...fields }, processed by one applyEffect(state, ctx, effect, level, target) switch. All numbers are curves. Ops:

opFieldsNotes
damagetype (physical, fire, cold, shock, acid), min, max, weaponShareTyped damage. Monster resist: {fire: 0.25} (optional table in content/monsters.js, default 0, cap 0.75; bosses at most 0.5) reduces it. Physical keeps the current hit chance and defense path; non-physical skips the hit roll (spells always land)
dottype, perTick, ticks, everyBurn and poison: m.burnT, m.burnDmg (one stack per monster, the stronger refreshes)
heal / hotamount, ticks, everyhot ticks through player.buffs
statuskind: stun / mute / slow / freeze / weaken, ticks, magstun, mute and freeze all set the existing muteT ("disabled"; m.statusKind tells the renderer which effect to show). slow sets slowT/slowMag (movement and attack pace). weaken sets weakenT/weakenMag (damage taken up, defense down). Bosses resist stun, mute and freeze (event resisted, as today) and take half duration of slow and weaken
knockbacktilesReuses knockBack
absorbamount, ticks, reflectPctplayer.absorb = {amount, t, reflect}; hostile damage drains it first
statModstat, value, ticks (timed buff) or none (passive)Stats: defense, attackRating, hpMax, mpMax, damagePct, critChance, critDamage, moveSpeedPct, resist.<type>, regenHp, regenMp
executebelow, multDamage multiplier against targets below a health fraction (finishers)
triggeron: kill / hit / hurt, then: [effects]Passive triggers (mana or gold on kill)
summonunit, count, hp, damage, ticksThrough the summon archetype

New rolls: critChance / critDamage join deriveStats; rollSwing multiplies on a crit (the combat stream is used for the crit roll, one extra draw per hit, so replay hashes change once in R4 and are re-pinned there). deriveStats replaces the passiveSkills loop with a fold over learned passives (and active auras and buffs) of statMod effects; it stays a pure function of (player, equipment) plus player.skills, player.buffs, player.aura.

Event additions (R4 contract): cast (existing, now carries archetype, fx), skillLearned, respec, buffStart/buffEnd, aura, summon, allyDied, zoneStart/zoneTrigger/zoneEnd, dash, status (target, kind, ticks), crit, absorb, dotTick.

5. New state (all JSON-able, in newGame)

player.buffs: [], player.absorb: null, player.aura: null, player.dash: null, state.allies: [], state.zones: [] (traps and lingering fields share one structure {id, kind, skill, level, tile, radius, armT, ttl, effects}), monster fields burnT, burnDmg, slowT, slowMag, weakenT, weakenMag, statusKind. None of these is saved (mid-floor, as the save format says); on load they are empty. Allies and zones clear on floor change and on respec. Monster melee may pick a living ally in reach instead of the hero; a decoy summon (taunt: true) wins that choice.

6. Rendering contract in one paragraph

Render and UI get the skill tree as data (content.skillTrees[classId]) and never import effect code. Icons are looked up by skill id (skillIcon(id); the six existing ids keep their bodies, 24 new ones are drawn in code). Effects are drawn by FX archetype keys, not by skill: fx.cast and fx.hit come from a small closed set (the full list is in docs/reviews/R4-contract.md, render_needs), so thirty skills need about fourteen effect drawings, tinted by damage type. Class figures are selected by figureKey from the same rig as today's hero, with per-class palettes and one accessory per class.

7. Class-tagged affixes and shared items (Q4 option A)

Affix definitions get two optional fields: class: "<affixTag>" and a stat key from a closed set: skillLevel.all (+n to all skills of the class), skillLevel.branch.<branchId>, skillDamagePct.<tag>, manaCostPct. The item roller takes the current character's class when rolling loot, vendor stock and gifts: a class-tagged affix can only be rolled for a character whose affixTag matches, which is deterministic (same seed and class, same loot). Because the stash is per character (ADR-0006) and there is no trade, a tagged item never reaches another class; an imported slot keeps its own class. Tagged affixes use group names that do not collide with the generic groups (an item still carries at most one affix per group) and the item name reads in the same office humour ("of the Corner Office"). Item requirements (level, attributes) are class-independent (R-231). Planned set for R4: per class 2 affixes on weapon, ring and amulet (skillLevel.all, skillLevel.branch.<one of its branches>), plus skillDamagePct.projectile, .area, .summon where fitting; tooltip shows the class tag in the accent colour of that class.

8. Respec (Q3 default A, flip-able)

config.respec = { mode: "free", townOnly: true, goldBase: 0, goldPerLevel: 0 }; modes free, gold (cost = goldBase + goldPerLevel * level), once (one free respec per character, then off), off. The core command respec is valid only in the Lobby (state.scene === "town") and with the hero alive. Effect: every skill except the signature goes to 0 (signature stays at 1); skillPoints becomes levelsGained - 0 (all earned points back); hotkeys holding removed actives become empty (the signature keeps its slot if it had one); buffs, aura, allies and zones clear; attribute points are not touched (attributes are never respecced, LATER). Event respec {refunded}. Under once, player.respecsUsed counts. Changing the customer's answer costs one config edit and one test constant.

9. Migration of the retired Clerk (save version 1 to 2; the slot side is in ADR-0006)

Registered as MIGRATIONS[1] in save/migrate.js, pure and idempotent on a v2 input (it is only called for version === 1):

  1. class: "clerk" becomes "facilities-manager" (via retiredClasses). Any other unknown class id is a schema failure, not a silent mapping.
  2. Refund: skillPoints = skillPoints + sum(levels of every old skill). skills becomes { "pallet-slam": 1 } (the signature, free), and the refund does not count the signature (the player never paid for it). The skill bar becomes primary: "strike", hotkeys: ["pallet-slam", null, null, null], selected: 0.
  3. Attributes are kept exactly as the player left them (a Clerk started with 10 each plus spent points); derived stats now use the class overrides. No attribute refund (attributes are not respecced).
  4. Items, stash, belt, gold, level, xp, depth, boss flags, explored maps and random streams are kept untouched. New fields: name (default "Employee"), version: 2, stats.playTicks: 0.
  5. The old Clerk skill ids that survive (stapler-throw, reply-all, coffee-break, mute, dress-code, hustle) live on in the new trees under new owners (see the lists below), so the icon bodies and strings carry over; but because the class changes owner for most of them, a refund (not a remap) is the rule the customer agreed.
  6. The migration returns a note { migrated: { from: 1, refundedPoints: n } } the shell shows once ("Your Clerk became a Facilities Manager; N skill points are ready to spend").

Test (R-225): a synthetic v1 fixture with 3 skill levels spent migrates to a v2 save whose skillPoints equals the old unspent plus 3 plus the old extras, the class is facilities-manager, validate passes, migrating the output again is a no-op, and a corrupt v1 returns schema without throwing.

Archetype shorthand: PRJ projectile, ARE area, SLF self, BUF buff, AUR aura, SUM summon, DSH dash, TRP trap, PAS passive. Tier gates are levels 1 / 8 / 16 (config). Max level 5, capstones (tier 3 "cap") 1. * = id and icon body inherited from the retired Clerk.
