Counts: 10 per class; Facilities 3 + 4 + 3, Sales 4 + 3 + 3, IT 4 + 3 + 3 (the circle asked about 3 + 3 + 4; the split is free). Active per branch: yes (every branch has at least one active). Spread: 5 PAS in total, 6 projectile, 9 area, 2 self, 3 buff or aura, 3 summon, 1 dash, 1 trap. Names to run through ip-denylist*.txt in the R4 legal test; "Firewall" and "Fire Drill" are ordinary words but sit near a genre skill called Fire Wall, so they carry a legal-scan note with the fallbacks "Packet Filter" and "Evacuation Drill" (id unchanged; the name is a string).

Options considered

  1. Per-skill code (status quo scaled to 30): fastest to write the first skill, but 30 branches to test and per-skill UI exceptions. Rejected.
  2. Full scripting language or expression strings for effects: flexible, but needs an interpreter, a sandbox rule and error handling; overkill for a closed set. Rejected.
  3. Archetype plus op list as data (chosen): about nine delivery archetypes and about twelve effect ops cover all 30 skills; new skills later are rows. The cost is a generic tooltip builder and a runner with a larger switch, both unit-testable once.
  4. Tree as one file with all classes vs. per-class files: per-class files chosen (diff size, parallel work); content/skills.js merges them and exports skills (id lookup, as today) so existing imports keep working.

Consequences

  • Save version 2 (with ADR-0006). save/format.js validates skills against the merged table and the class against classById; unknown skill ids in a v2 save are a schema failure.
  • ui/panels.js renderSkills is replaced by a tree panel (tabs per branch, node graph from tier/col/requires, tooltip from effects); d.mana(level) call sites change to manaCost(def, level).
  • deriveStats signature stays; passiveSkills export is replaced by a helper; castSkill keeps its public name and result shape.
  • Replay hashes change once in R4 (crit draws, new state fields); fixtures pin the new hashes in the same WP.
  • Balance numbers (curves, attribute starts, mana) are placeholders in data, tuned in R6 by per-class bot runs against the parity band in R-230; no code change is needed to tune.
  • Dependency licences: none added.

Questions for the customer (L-05: not decided here; the design fits either answer)

  1. Final class names and the game title are brand questions (R-233, QF-06-1): working names stay Facilities Manager, Sales Rep, IT Wizard. Names are strings; ids are internal.
  2. The respec rule (circle-02 Q3, PROXY with low confidence) can be switched to gold, once or off by one config value.
  3. Whether the starting hero should be auto-given its signature skill (assumed yes to keep the 29-point rule and a playable first minute) or start with one open point; the data supports both.
  4. Whether skill synergies (R-208, could) are wanted in this round; the schema reserves synergy and R6 implements it only if there is room.

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R6-1: skills scale from the class's power attribute)

Problem. deriveStats added max(0, grit - gritFree) * damagePerGrit to the hero's damage range for every class, and every damaging skill adds floor(mean(p.damage) * weaponShare) on top of its own curve (weaponBonus in systems/skillfx.js). A caster (IT Wizard: grit 6, focus 20) therefore had no attribute bonus at all (grit below gritFree), and a bot that followed the generic point weights put its points into Grit, a stat that does nothing for a caster's spells. A Sales Rep (grit 8, agility 16) was in the same position. The "caster attribute" was only feeding mana (mpPerFocus) and the ranged class's agility only fed attack rating and defence. The R5 bot runs showed the cost: Sales Rep 2/3 wins and 6 deaths, IT Wizard slowest after it (docs/reviews/R5-adversarial.md, R6-balance.md baseline).

Decision. Each class names one power attribute in content/classes.js derived.powerAttr: grit (Facilities Manager, melee), agility (Sales Rep, ranged), focus (IT Wizard, caster). Default when absent: config.derived.powerAttr = "grit" (plain player objects and old fixtures behave as before). The formula in items/derive.js becomes

powerBonus   = max(0, attrs[powerAttr] - derived.gritFree)          // attrs = own points + gear, as before
damage.min   = floor(unarmed.min + powerBonus * damagePerGrit.min) + gear.damageMin
damage.max   = floor(unarmed.max + powerBonus * damagePerGrit.max) + gear.damageMax
skill hit    = round((rng(skill.min, skill.max) + floor(mean(damage) * weaponShare)) * mult)  // unchanged; mean(damage) now carries the power attribute

gritFree and damagePerGrit keep their names (no field renamed, no save or snapshot change; the constants are read per class through the existing derived override). Class values: Facilities Manager grit, 0.5 per point; Sales Rep agility, 0.8 per point; IT Wizard focus, 0.6 per point; free points 8 for all.

Why this and not a separate spell-power stat. It reuses one formula and one data key (the contract of R6 forbids new shared fields), it keeps the skill curves and weaponShare meaning intact (a skill still "grows with gear" through the weapon term, and now also through the attribute the class invests in), and it makes the attribute panel honest: the point that raises Focus for a caster raises spell damage and mana, as the class card says. The basic attacks (strike, toss, zap) scale the same way, so the free attack does not fall behind the skills.

Bot side. The class bot.attrWeights follow the power attribute (IT Wizard: stamina, focus, agility; no Grit). Saves are unaffected: attrs already hold all four attributes; a loaded character is re-derived by applyDerived.

Numbers tuned with it (all in data, listed with old and new values in docs/reviews/R6-balance.md): class growth and power rates, skill curves of a few skills, config.scaling, config.xpCurve.

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R6 fix round: respec with nothing to refund, refused casts)

Source: docs/reviews/R6-adversarial.md ADV-R6-02, docs/reviews/R6-code-review.md CR6-07.

  • Respec with nothing to refund (section 8). In the modes gold and once a respec that would return 0 points is refused with { ok: false, error: "nothing-to-respec", reason: "nothing-to-respec" }: no gold is charged and the single respec of mode once stays available. respecCheck returns the same code so a UI can disable the button. Mode free is unchanged (a respec of an empty tree is allowed and harmless). Order of the checks: respec-off, dead, not-in-town, respec-used, nothing-to-respec, no-gold.
  • Refused casts say why. castSkill emits { type: "castRefused", t: "castRefused", skill, reason } (t mirrors type for readers that follow the command naming) for the refusals the player can act on: no-direction (a projectile or dash aimed at the hero's own tile or at nothing usable), no-target (no target tile given) and no-mana (together with the existing noMana event). cooldown and silenced do not exist in the core (there are no cooldowns, QF-06-5, and the hero cannot be silenced), busy casting is not reported (it would fire on every double click) and out of range / no line of sight are not reported yet. The audio table lists the event as silent (the UI shows a toast).
ADR-0006-save-slots.md

ADR-0006 Five save slots: key layout, index, migration, quotas, atomicity

Date: 2026-10-14. Status: proposed (plan gate for rounds R4-R6). Owner: architect. Implements R-220..R-227, NFR-D05, NFR-D06; supersedes the single-slot parts of R-090..R-092 and QF-09-1/-4. Customer answers are binding: circles/circle-02.md Q6 (PROXY): 5 slots, "Save slots" section in Options plus the same list on title and pause, overwrite and delete name the character, rename, options global, stash per character, autosave to the active slot only, Continue opens the last used slot, old save to slot 1 with the old key kept, per-slot export/import, 400 KB per slot. The customer's own words ("a save with 5 slots to the options menu", Third briefing) fix the number and the Options entry. Interacts with ADR-0005 (save version 2, class and skill migration), ADR-0002 (core stays pure: no storage, no wall clock).

Context

Read from the code, 2026-10-14: save/storage.js createSaveStore(adapter) has one slot (config.saveKey = "office-crawler.save"), a rotating three-deep backup of damaged or replaced saves under office-crawler.save.corrupt[.1/.2], and options under office-crawler.options. Adapters (localStorage or memory) never throw; setItem quota errors are caught. save/format.js writes canonical JSON with a checksum, version 1, cap config.saveMaxBytes = 1000000. The stash is already inside the save text (stash), so it is per character as soon as there are several saves. main.js listens for the core autosave event and calls store.autosave(core, ev). The save text contains no wall-clock time (NFR-D01-1).

New needs: five independent characters; a slot list that renders on the title screen without parsing five full saves; per-slot corruption must not hurt the others (R-227); a migration of the existing save and its backups; a storage budget.

Decision

1. Key layout (all under the existing prefix, localStorage, same origin)

KeyContentWritten when
office-crawler.slot.1 .. office-crawler.slot.5Full save text of one character (canonical JSON, save format version 2, checksum), at most 400 000 charactersautosave of the active slot, explicit save, import, create
office-crawler.slotsThe index: small JSON (below), about 1.5 KBafter each slot write or slot operation
office-crawler.slot.N.badRaw text of a slot that failed validation, kept for export (one per slot)on load failure, before the slot is cleared
office-crawler.optionsOptions, unchanged, global (language-free; volume, keys, text size, reduced motion). Not part of any sloton option change
office-crawler.save, office-crawler.save.corrupt, .corrupt.1, .corrupt.2Legacy single-slot keys, read only by the migration (section 5), never written againnever

Nothing else is stored. There is no cross-slot shared stash, no account, no user id. Settings the player expects to survive deleting a character stay in office-crawler.options (QF-09-4).

2. Index shape (readable without parsing any save)

{ "v": 2, "active": 2, "last": 2,
  "slots": [
    { "n": 1, "state": "ok", "name": "Dana", "class": "sales-rep", "level": 17, "depth": 5, "deepest": 6, "playSec": 5421,
      "lastPlayed": 1791964800000, "bytes": 83211, "sum": 2870131233, "boss": false },
    { "n": 2, "state": "empty" },
    { "n": 3, "state": "bad", "reason": "checksum", "lastPlayed": 1791960000000, "bytes": 51022 },
    { "n": 4, "state": "ok", ... }, { "n": 5, "state": "empty" } ] }

Fields: state is ok | empty | bad | newer (newer: written by a newer build, never overwritten, R-227); name is plain text (rules in the contract: 1-16 characters, letters, digits, space, hyphen, apostrophe, trimmed); class is a class id; level; depth is the floor the character is on, deepest the deepest reached; playSec is play time; lastPlayed is epoch milliseconds set by the shell (the only place a clock is read); bytes is the length of the slot text; sum is hash32 over the slot text (cheap, 400 KB hashes in a few ms) used to detect that index and slot disagree; boss is bossDefeated. active is the slot the running game writes to (null on the title); last is what Continue opens. Wall-clock time and play time live only in the index and in a stats.playTicks counter inside the save (ticks, not time), never as a timestamp inside the save text, so NFR-D01-1 holds and the core stays pure.

Reading the list = one getItem on office-crawler.slots plus one JSON.parse of 1.5 KB. No slot text is read. A selection card needs nothing else (R-222).

Repair. The index can be lost or stale because a slot write and the index write are two separate setItem calls (section 6). Rules: (a) when the index is missing or unparsable, the store rebuilds it by scanning the five slot keys (parse, validate, derive metadata) and stores the result; (b) when a slot is opened and its bytes/sum differ from the index, the index entry is rebuilt from the slot (silently) before use; (c) a slot key that exists but has no index entry (crash between the two writes in the order below cannot produce this, but a manual import can) is adopted by (a). Rebuild cost (five parses) is paid once.

3. Per-character data and what is global

Per slot (inside the slot text): everything the v1 save had (character, name, class, skills, items, equipment, belt, stash, gold, depth, boss flags, explored maps, random streams, stats) plus name and stats.playTicks. The stash is per character (Q4/Q6 default; no shared stash, so class-tagged affixes in ADR-0005 cannot cross classes). Global: office-crawler.options and the index. Options are never overwritten by an import or by deleting a slot.

4. Operations and who may do them

The store (save/slots.js, new) exposes: list(), read(n), write(n, state, {now}), create(n, state, {now}), remove(n), rename(n, name), copy(from, to) (could), exportText(n, which), importText(n, text, {now}), setActive(n), lastUsed(), migrateLegacy(), usage(). Every call returns plain data and never throws (as today). Rules:

  • Autosave writes only the active slot (R-224). The autosave handler passes store.activeSlot; with no active slot (not possible while a game runs) it does nothing and tells the player. A test writes 100 saves to slot 2 and asserts slots 1, 3, 4, 5 and their index entries are byte-identical.
  • Create / overwrite / delete / rename / import are session commands (shell level), each confirmed in the UI by a dialog that names the character; the store itself does not ask. Overwrite, delete and import first move the old text to the single undo copy office-crawler.slot.N.prev, which is kept until the next write to that slot and deleted on delete-confirmation ("Delete forever") when space is short. This gives the one-step safety net the old rotating backups gave, but bounded to one copy per slot.
  • Rename edits name in the slot text (a normal save of that slot with new name) and the index.
  • In-game load or overwrite from the pause menu: confirmation naming the character; the running game is saved first to its own slot (unless the player cancels).
  • Continue opens index.last; if that slot is not ok it opens the most recently played ok slot; if none, Continue is hidden (as today).

5. Migration of the existing single save and its backups into slot 1 (R-225)

migrateLegacy() runs once at boot, before the title is shown, and only when office-crawler.slots is absent:

  1. If office-crawler.save exists: parse and deserialize it with the v1 to v2 migration (ADR-0005: Clerk to Facilities Manager, points refunded, name "Employee"). On success write the migrated text to slot.1, then the index (state: ok, last: 1, plus migrated: {from: 1, refunded: n} shown once as a notice). On a newer version: leave the legacy key untouched, slot 1 stays newer-marked via a stub {state: "newer"} entry, notice saveTooNew. On corrupt input: copy the raw text to slot.1.bad (so the player can export it), slot 1 state: bad, the other slots empty (never a crash, R-225).
  2. The legacy keys are kept in place as the backup (the old key is never written again). office-crawler.save.corrupt, .1, .2 stay too; they are only deleted by the space-recovery order in section 7.
  3. The index is written last. A crash before it leaves the legacy keys intact and slot.1 possibly written; the next boot sees no index, rewrites slot.1 from the legacy key (same result, idempotent). Running the migration twice, or with the index present, changes nothing.
  4. If no legacy key exists, the index is created empty (active: null, last: null, five empty entries).

Save format version 2 is the first version with name; the in-save migration (v1 to v2) is the same function that deserialize uses for any v1 text, so import of an old exported file also works (it lands in the chosen slot).

6. Atomicity

localStorage.setItem on one key is atomic: a quota error throws before the old value changes. Two keys (slot and index) cannot be atomic together, so the order is chosen so every crash point is repairable:

  1. serialise to text; check text.length <= config.slotMaxBytes (400000) else fail with too-large and change nothing;
  2. if the slot is occupied and this is a first write after load, copy the current text to slot.N.prev (skipped on routine autosaves; the undo copy is made at overwrite/delete/import moments only);
  3. setItem(slot.N, text); on failure return the error, nothing else was touched (the previous slot text is still there);
  4. setItem(slots, newIndex); on failure the slot is new and the index old: the next list sees bytes/sum mismatch and repairs (rule b);
  5. only then clear lastError and emit success.

A tab closed between 3 and 4 is covered by repair; a tab closed in the middle of 3 cannot corrupt (single-key write). Two tabs: the running game stamps its random tab id into the index field owner when it becomes active, and re-reads the index before each write; if the owner is another tab, it shows "open in another tab" and does not write. This is best effort, not a guarantee (storage events are the next step, LATER).

7. Quotas

  • config.slotMaxBytes = 400000 characters per slot text (NFR-D05); config.saveMaxBytes (1 MB) remains only as the cap on legacy and import input.
  • Budget: 5 slots x 400 KB = 2 MB characters worst case, plus one prev and one bad per slot in the worst case; browsers allow about 5 million characters (5 MB) per origin, so a soft ceiling of 4.0 million characters of own keys is enforced by usage() (sum of lengths of all office-crawler.* keys). Typical saves are 30-100 KB (explored maps are run-length coded), so the ceiling is not expected to bite; the test uses a synthetic oversize slot.
  • Over the ceiling or on QuotaExceededError, space is recovered in this fixed order, each step followed by a retry: (1) legacy .corrupt* keys, (2) slot.N.bad of slots that are not bad in the index, (3) slot.N.prev of non-active slots, (4) the legacy office-crawler.save only if slot 1 reads back ok. If still failing: error quota, notice "Could not save: storage is full. Export a slot or delete a character", nothing deleted without a step above and never a slot with state: ok.
  • The save cannot exceed the cap by growth alone: explored maps are coded as before; if a character legitimately reaches 400 KB, the write is refused with too-large and the previous save stays (R-227).

8. Failure handling (R-227)

A slot that fails validation (parse, checksum, schema, size) becomes state: bad, its text moves to slot.N.bad, the slot key is cleared, and a notice names the slot. The title still loads; the other four slots work. newer slots are never touched. Export of a bad slot returns the .bad text. The adapter fallback (memory when localStorage is blocked) keeps the same API: slots work for the session and a banner says nothing persists.

9. Export and import (R-226)

exportText(n) returns the slot text (the file name is office-crawler-slot-N-<name>.json, name sanitised to [a-z0-9-]). importText(n, text) runs the full validation (including v1 to v2 migration), requires the target slot to be chosen by the player (confirmation if occupied; the old text goes to .prev), stores the text in canonical form and updates the index. The imported character keeps its name; a name collision across slots is allowed (Q5).

Options considered

  1. One key holding all five slots (a single JSON): one atomic write, but every autosave rewrites up to 2 MB and one corrupt character poisons the lot. Rejected.
  2. Per-slot metadata key next to each save (slot.N.meta): five reads for the list, no single place for active/last. Rejected for the single index (one read, one place for pointers); the index is small enough that rewriting it on every autosave is cheap.
  3. IndexedDB: async, more complex tests, no benefit at these sizes; file:// and offline are already served by localStorage. Rejected (ADR-0002 prefers boring).
  4. Metadata inside the save only: forces parsing of up to 5 x 400 KB for the title screen. Rejected.
  5. Keep the rotating 3-deep backup per slot: up to 15 extra copies, too much of the budget. Replaced by one prev per slot plus bad.

Consequences

  • save/storage.js is reworked into save/slots.js (slot store) over the same adapters; config.saveKey/saveBackupKey become legacy constants used only by the migration; config.slotMaxBytes and config.slotCount = 5 are added.
  • Save format becomes version 2: name, stats.playTicks, class validated against the new class table, skills against the merged tree; the in-save migration MIGRATIONS[1] lives in save/migrate.js.
  • The shell (game.js, main.js) gains an active-slot concept and session commands (see docs/reviews/R4-contract.md); the core never learns about slots.
  • Playwright tests that wrote to office-crawler.save are updated by the R4 WP; the memory adapter's keys() is used by the quota tests.
  • The storage ceiling and the repair rules are the main residual risks; both have unit tests with an adapter that can fail writes (failWrites exists).

Questions for the customer (L-05)

None block the design. Two UX defaults are stated for the customer to overrule: (1) the soft one-tab lock shows a read-only message in the second tab; (2) Delete keeps one undo copy of the slot until the next write there ("Delete forever" in the dialog clears it). Both are UI wording and flow, owned by the customer or the proxy.

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R5 fix round: owner lock, migration, schema)

Source: code review CR-01..CR-13 and adversarial findings ADV-R5-01..10 (docs/reviews/R4-R5-G-code-review.md, docs/reviews/R5-adversarial.md). Where this section differs from the text above, this section wins.

  1. Owner lock with a heartbeat (replaces the permanent tab lock of section 6). The index field owner is { id, beat } (beat = epoch ms from the injected clock), no longer a bare tab id. The playing tab refreshes beat on every write of its active slot and from a timer every config.ownerBeatMs (5 s) while a game runs (store.heartbeat(), main.js). An owner whose beat is older than config.ownerStaleMs (15 s, i.e. three missed beats) is stale. Decision table for a write by tab T: no owner or T owns it, write; a live owner that is not T, refuse with another-tab; a stale owner, write (and take over) only if T started after the stale beat, otherwise another-tab. takeOverSaves makes T the owner on the player's explicit confirmation. A bare string owner left by an older build reads as { id, beat: 0 }, i.e. stale. The tab id is a fresh crypto.randomUUID() per page load and is never kept in sessionStorage (a duplicated tab copies sessionStorage and would share the id); pagehide still releases the owner, so a reload does not need to keep it. status.owner is none | self | other | stale. Residual risk: a background tab whose timers are throttled beyond 15 s looks stale; a tab that started later may then take over and the first tab's next write is refused (another-tab), never interleaved.
  2. Ids that reach markup are restricted in the schema. Item, affix and unique ids, item slot/effect/restores, requirement keys and uniquesFound entries must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/; a save with any other value is rejected on load and import (CR-02). Escaping at the UI sinks stays the UI's job; this is defence in depth.
  3. Skills are validated against the rules (CR-03, ADV-R5-04). Every learned skill is of the class, at level 1 or more, within reqLevel and its prerequisites; points spent (the signature's first level is free) plus skillPoints may not exceed (level - 1) * skillPointsPerLevel; primary must be the class's basic attack, hotkeys and secondary are null or a learned active/aura skill of the class; secondary is re-derived from hotkeys[selected] on load.
  4. Options are not part of a slot (CR-04). toSave writes options: {}; on import and load any stored options are dropped (the checksum is verified first, callers re-seal).
  5. Switching characters never loses progress silently (CR-05, CR-06). The running game is saved before loadSlot / createCharacter replaces it, also when it is the slot being loaded. If that save fails the switch is aborted (save-failed-before-switch, reason = the store error) and status.notice = "pre-switch-save-failed".
  6. Persistent status for the UI. slotsView carries status { storage: ok | memory | full, owner, notice }. Notices: no-active-slot (autosave with no active slot, also toasted once, CR-07), pre-switch-save-failed, migration-failed; any successful write clears the first two, dismissSaveNotice clears all. storage: "memory" means localStorage is blocked and nothing persists (ADV-R5-06). Slot summaries gain deepest, savedAt (ISO UTC) and hasPrev.
  7. Migration (replaces section 5 step 1 to 3 where they differ; CR-08, ADV-R5-01). A missing or invalid index is rebuilt from the slot keys before any decision. The legacy save fills slot 1 only when slot 1 is empty; a played slot 1 is never replaced (the legacy keys remain the backup). If the slot write fails the index is still stored with pendingMigration: true (slots 2 to 5 stay visible), status.notice = "migration-failed", and the next boot retries; the flag is removed on success. A later delete of slot 1 does not resurrect the legacy save (it runs only without an index or with the flag).
  8. Smaller rules. rename honours the owner lock (CR-09). Creating over or importing over a damaged slot keeps its text in .bad (exportable) instead of deleting it. restorePrev refuses newer slots and any non-empty slot (ADV-R5-03). The core accepts setName while paused or dead (whitelisted before the paused/live gates), so the shell no longer flips paused (CR-10). Names may contain combining marks \p{M} but not start with one (ADV-R5-10). A new character's xpNext is xpTable[1] (ADV-R5-05). The old single-slot createSaveStore is removed; its acceptance tests run against the slot store (CR-11). The storage total is a running sum, rescanned when the number of own keys changes, on a failed write and on usage({ exact: true }) (CR-13).

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R6 fix round: save version 3, attribute and affix invariants)

Source: docs/reviews/R6-adversarial.md ADV-R6-01 and ADV-R6-05, docs/reviews/R6-code-review.md CR6-02 and CR6-15. Where this section differs from the text above, this section wins.

  1. saveVersion is 3. Version 2 is the R5 format (character name, stats.playTicks, class trees). Version 3 has the same keys; what changes is a migration and two validation rules. Chain: 0 to 1 to 2 to 3, each step pure; a version 3 input passes MIGRATIONS[2] unchanged.
  2. Migration 2 to 3 (ADV-R6-05). Until R5, Grit was the only attribute that added damage, for every class; since R6 a class names its own power attribute (derived.powerAttr: Facilities Manager Grit, Sales Rep Agility, IT Wizard Focus; ADR-0005 amendment of R6-1). For a class whose power attribute is not Grit, every attribute point beyond the class's start values goes back to player.attrPoints (all four attributes return to the start values; a refund is never partial per attribute) so the player can re-spend them where they now count. The Facilities Manager and the Clerk migration (which ends as a Facilities Manager) get nothing. A malformed attribute table is left as it is and fails the schema check. Level, xp, skills, gear, stash, gold and the rest are untouched. migrate() reports { from: 2, attributePointsRefunded: n } in notes (only when n > 0).
  3. Notice. When a load, an import or the boot migration of the legacy save returns that note, the slot store sets status.notice = "attributes-refunded" (a new entry of the notice list in slots.js; shown with a Dismiss button; text key notices["attributes-refunded"] in ui/text.js). It is shown once per load of a version 2 text; once the game saves the slot as version 3 the note is gone. Reloading an unsaved version 2 slot repeats the refund and the notice, which is harmless (the refund is a pure function of the stored text).
  4. Attribute invariant (ADV-R6-01, CR6-02). schemaProblem requires sum(attrs) + attrPoints <= sum(class start attrs) + (level - 1) * config.attrPointsPerLevel, the same kind of rule as the skill-point invariant (section 3 of the R5 amendment). A hero played by the rules sits exactly on the bound; no other source grants attribute points (allocate spends, gainXp and the setLevel cheat grant attrPointsPerLevel per level).
  5. Rollable gear only (ADV-R6-01b). A gear item must be something the generator can produce: every affix has an id of the affix table and its stat, kind, group, tier and range equal the table's, the value is an integer inside that range, the tier is unlocked at the item's ilvl (minIlvl <= ilvl), the group may roll on the base's slot, groups are unique per item, prefixes and suffixes stay within config.maxPrefixes / maxSuffixes, and the number of affixes fits the rarity (normal 0, magic at most magicAffixes[1], rare at most rareAffixes[1]). A unique carries exactly the fixed affixes of its definition (same order, ids, stats, values) on its own base. damage and defense, when present, equal the base's. Class tags are not checked (the values are bounded by the table anyway). A top-tier affix needs ilvl 20, so a forged ilvl buys nothing beyond what depth 7 drops.
  6. Affix ids may contain a dot. Affix id and group use /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,40}$/ (section 2 of the R5 amendment keeps the stricter pattern for every other id): the fixed affixes of four uniques are named after the stat key (unique-resist.fire), and before this fix a save holding one of them could not be loaded back. Found by the generator sweep of test/save-v3.test.js.
  7. Tests. test/save-v3.test.js with real R5-shaped fixtures (test/fixtures/save-v2-r5-{it,sales,fm}.json: version 2, sealed, level 14, generated magic and rare gear), test/adv-r6-core.test.js (ADV-R6-01, 01b, 05).

Addition (orchestrator request): status also carries noticeAttr: the class's power attribute key ("agility", "focus") while notice is "attributes-refunded", else null; the migration note is { from: 2, attributePointsRefunded, attr }.

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R7 quests: save version 4, quest state per slot, pouch, slot card fields)

Source: ADR-0007-quests.md (state shape, rules), ../30-spec/12-quests-journal.md (AC-R-251-1..3, AC-R-252-1, AC-R-253-1..2), ../circles/circle-03.md Q6. Where this section differs from the text above, this section wins. Owner of the implementation: CORE-R7Q (docs/reviews/R7-contract.md).

  1. saveVersion is 4. Chain: 0 to 1 to 2 to 3 to 4, each step pure; a version 4 input passes MIGRATIONS[3] unchanged. A text with a version above 4 reports newer (the existing rule: the slot is never overwritten). An older build reading a v4 slot sees newer for the same reason; the slot index stays at v: 2 (entries only gain optional fields, point 6), so an older build still reads the list.
  2. One new top-level save key, quests (added to SAVE_KEYS; PLAYER_KEYS and the four rng streams are unchanged). Shape (every value is a plain integer, boolean or short id; no text is stored, so a content rename never invalidates a save): `` quests: { main: { m: { memo: bool, depth: 0..9, unlocked: bool, defeated: bool, verdict: bool } }, sq1: { s: "available"|"active"|"ready"|"completed", p: int }, sq2: {...}, sq3: {...}, pinned: "main" | "sq1" | "sq2" | "sq3", pouch: [ { id: "qi-sq2", quest: "sq2" } ] } ` toSave writes {...state.quests, pouch: state.player.pouch}; loadSave splits it again and **sets it before the resume enterFloor**, so the placement hook of ADR-0007 section 7 re-creates the quest item and the elite of a character saved on floor 3 or 4. Loading never emits a quest cue (events are cleared after load and the first floorEnter` finds the milestones already set).
  3. Schema rules (schemaProblem, forged data stays inside what play can produce). quests has exactly the keys main, the ids of content.questIds that are side quests, pinned, pouch; m has exactly its five keys with depth an integer in 0..config.bossDepth; m.depth <= deepestDepth, m.unlocked implies bossUnlocked || bossDefeated, m.defeated implies bossDefeated, m.verdict implies m.defeated; each side s is one of the four states, p an integer in 0..goal with available implying p = 0, active implying p < goal, ready and completed implying p = goal; pinned is main or a side id that is not completed; pouch holds at most one entry per item quest, each {id, quest} with id matching SAFE_ID and equal to the content item id of quest, and an entry exists if and only if its quest is ready. Any other key or value is schema. config.slotMaxBytes is unaffected (the block is under 400 characters).
  4. Migration MIGRATIONS[3] (v3 to v4), pure, idempotent, no retroactive reward. Input: any v3 data (after v2 to v3 if needed). Output: quests derived from fields every v3 save has:
    • m.depth = deepestDepth if deepestDepth >= 2; else 1 if the character has ever left the Lobby, which is read from the save as explored[1] present or resume.depth >= 1 or stats.kills > 0; else 0. (deepestDepth alone cannot say "never descended": it is 1 from the first tick. The v3 schema forces deepestDepth >= 1, so the spec's "deepestDepth 0" case is the fixture with deepestDepth 1 and none of those three signs.)
    • m.unlocked = bossUnlocked || bossDefeated, m.defeated = bossDefeated, m.memo = m.depth >= 1, m.verdict = false.
    • sq1..sq3 = { s: "available", p: 0 }, pinned = "main", pouch = []. Nothing else in the save is read or changed: gold, xp, items, equipment, belt, stash, skills, skillPoints, attrs, stats, rng are byte-identical (asserted by deep-equal). The quest item and the elite are not created (they appear only after an accept, on the next floor entry).
    • Derived main step (ADR-0007 section 2) for the five legal fixtures: never descended: step 1; floor 1 reached (explored[1], deepestDepth 1): step 3; deepestDepth 4: step 4; deepestDepth 8 with bossUnlocked: step 5; bossDefeated: step 6 ("Read the verdict", the journal action of ADR-0007 section 5).
    • migrate() reports no note for 3 to 4 (no dialog is shown; the journal itself is the notice). A corrupt v3 text still ends as corrupt or schema without an exception.
  5. Fixtures are legal v3 saves (L-038). test/fixtures/save-v3-*.json are produced by a helper that takes toSave(state) of the pre-R7 shape: delete quests, set version: 3, re-seal with checksumOf. They are never hand-typed, so every field the v3 schema checks is real. Five fixtures: save-v3-lobby.json (step 1), save-v3-floor1.json (3), save-v3-floor4.json (4), save-v3-boss-unlocked.json (5), save-v3-boss-defeated.json (6); the e2e fixture of AC-R-251-3 is save-v3-floor4.json placed in slot 2 beside a valid slot 1. Existing save-v2-r5-*.json run through 2 to 3 to 4.
  6. Slot index entries gain three optional fields (index v stays 2; no breaking change): mainStep (1..6), mainDone (boolean, all six steps done), sidesDone (0..sideCount, the number of side quests completed). entryFromState and entryFromText fill them (for a migrated text from the migration output, so a v3 slot shows its derived step with 0 side quests, AC-R-252-1). The slot card shows the step title from content.quests.main.steps[mainStep - 1].title and "N/sideCount" (the title is looked up, never stored, so a customer rename needs no save change). An ok entry without mainStep (written by an R5 or R6 build) is stale: store.upgradeIndex() (new, called once at boot right after migrateLegacy) runs rebuild(readIndex()) when any ok entry lacks mainStep, which keeps active, last and owner and re-derives every entry (cost: five parses, once). slotsView().list[i] carries the three fields; an empty, bad or newer entry has none and shows no quest text.
  7. Per-character isolation (AC-R-253-2). Quest state is inside the slot text only; createCharacter builds a fresh newGame, so a new slot starts at step 1 with all side quests available; nothing about quests is global or in office-crawler.options. Delete, overwrite, rename, import and copy move the whole text as before.
  8. Tests and owners. test/save-v4.test.js (round trip AC-R-251-1, 20 mutated copies never throw, version above 4 newer, schema invariants one by one, 500-character cap on the block), test/save-v4-migrate.test.js (the five fixtures, idempotence, no retroactive reward, v2 and v1 chains, corrupt input), test/save-slots.test.js additions (index fields, upgradeIndex keeps active/last/owner, a v3 slot lists with its derived step), all owned by CORE-R7Q. Existing assertions that pin version 3 (test/save-v3.test.js lines 38, 43, 55; test/adv-r6-fix.test.js line 191; e2e/adv-r6.mjs line 686) become config.saveVersion-relative; the contract names the one-line edit and who makes it.
ADR-0007-quests.md

ADR-0007 Quests: data model, step machine, quest stream, generator hooks, pouch, rewards, golden hash

Date: 2026-10-14. Status: proposed (plan gate for R7-0). Owner: architect. Implements R-240..R-256 (../30-spec/12-quests-journal.md, 39 ACs) with the customer-proxy answers of ../circles/circle-03.md (Q1 to Q7, provisional; titles and text escalated). Closes QF-12-1..5; QF-12-6 stays with the customer. Interacts with ADR-0002 (pure core, replay), ADR-0003 (test hook), ADR-0006 (slots; save v4 is the amendment dated 2026-10-14 "R7 quests" in that file).

Context (read from the code, 2026-10-14)

  • state.js newGame builds one plain JSON state; state.rng has four named streams (world, combat, ai, loot); the save schema demands exactly those four (save/format.js schemaProblem). hashState covers the whole canonical state, including events and eventLog (last 256 events); only ui.tooltip, ui.hud, perf are excluded (hash.js).
  • step() clears state.events first, applies inputs, then runs the systems unless the game is paused or not in the Lobby/floor. Events emitted outside step (test cheats such as teleportFloor, the slot loader) sit in state.events and are cleared by the next step: a per-tick scan of state.events would lose them. Every core event goes through emit(state, ev) (events.js, 6 lines), the one choke point.
  • Existing events already carry what the main quest needs: floorEnter {depth} (end of enterFloor, after state.depth changed), stairsUnlocked (floor 8 cleared), bossDefeated, kill {source, target, xp} (emitted after m.ai = "dead", the monster is still in state.monsters for config.deathTicks), keepPlaying (leaving the victory screen).
  • deepestDepth is 1 from the first tick, also in the Lobby (Math.max(1, floor.depth)), and the save schema forces deepestDepth >= 1. "Never left the Lobby" cannot be read from it.
  • The memo (story.start) is shown by the shell (game.ui.story = "start", dismissStory); the core has no memo event. The victory screen is the scene victory (set in boss.js finishVictory, autosave reason victory), left by keepPlaying (screen button, {t: "keepPlaying"} input); the bot sends the same input.
  • NPCs (content/npcs.js): vendor, healer, potions (the potion seller), stash; dialogue is state.ui.dialog = {npc, kind, nameKey, lines}; heal and moveStash already require the matching open dialog. Town stairs lead to townTarget = deepestDepth (config.townStairsTarget); every floor has a way up (enterFloor(..., {at: "exit"})). A floor regenerates from hash32(seed, depth) on every entry; what persists in a session is the list of killed spawn indexes and the ground items (parkFloor); after a reload only the explored map survives.
  • Ground entries (state.groundItems) are drawn by the renderer from the entry's own rarity/mark/border/color/label, gold has no item; keep: true protects an entry from the ground cap. Potions are 1x1 items; the bag is a 10x4 grid (autoplace, findSpot).
  • test/fixtures/run-a.hash and run-class.json (three class hashes) are frozen goldens; AI-R7 re-records them (new standT field) before this work starts.

Decision

1. Quests are data: src/core/content/quests.js plus config.quests

content.quests (exported through content): an object keyed by quest id, plus questIds, sideIds. Structure and text live in the content file; every number a balance pass may touch lives in config.quests (the ACs assert relations to these constants).

quests.main = { id: "main", kind: "main", title, steps: [ {id, title, line}, ... 6 ] }      // the six steps and lines of AC-R-241-1
quests.sqN  = { id, kind: "side", title, giver: <npc id>, salt: <1..9>,
                objective: { type: "kill" | "item" | "elite", ... },
                text: { offer, progress, ready, done },                 // dialogue lines (plain text, original)
                next: { available, active, ready },                      // next-step lines; "{giver}" is replaced by the NPC's name string
                reward: { refDepth, gold, xp, potions?, gear? } }       // numbers read from config.quests.<id>

Working ids as in the spec: sq1 (giver vendor, kill), sq2 (giver healer, item), sq3 (giver potions, elite). The stash keeper gives nothing and no NPC is added. Titles, step lines, dialogue, the item name, the elite name and the reward names are working text (escalated, R-255); test/ip-denylist.test.js already scans all of src, and a new content-walking test (AC-R-255-1) iterates every string of content.quests.

config.quests (new, defaults): sideCount 3, kill {monster "zombie-intern", count 8, depths [1, 2]}, item {floors [3, 4], pickupRange 1}, elite {type "middle-manager", depth 4, hpMult 1.6, level 4}, gearFloor 4, per-quest reward numbers (sq1 {gold {base 30, perDepth 15}, xp {base 40, perDepth 25}, potions 3}, sq2 {slots ["body","head","hands","feet"]}, sq3 {slots ["weapon"], potions 2}, all with refDepth), rewardRerolls 8, genBudgetFactor 1.05, toastMs 4000. Going to 6 side quests is content plus sideCount.

2. State shape

Runtime (state.quests, created by newGame, plain JSON, hashed):

state.quests = {
  main: { m: { memo: false, depth: 0, unlocked: false, defeated: false, verdict: false } },   // milestones, monotone
  sq1:  { s: "available", p: 0 },  sq2: { s: "available", p: 0 },  sq3: { s: "available", p: 0 },   // s: available | active | ready | completed
  pinned: "main",
}
state.player.pouch = []          // [{ id: "qi-sq2", quest: "sq2" }]
  • The main quest stores milestones, not a step number. step is derived: step 1 is done when memo || depth >= 1, 2 when depth >= 1, 3 when depth >= 4, 4 when unlocked || defeated, 5 when defeated, 6 when verdict; the current step is the first one not done (1..6), completed when all six are. Milestones only grow, so a step never goes backwards, an event out of order catches up (cheat.teleportFloor(4) from step 1 sets depth = 4 and steps 1 to 3 are done), and death or leaving a floor changes nothing (AC-R-241-2, AC-R-253-1). newGame always starts with m.depth = 0, also for the legacy start: "floor" fixtures and gameOn test floors (AC-R-240-1 wants step 1 for newGame(seed, {class}), which begins on floor 1): the first floorEnter completes steps 1 and 2 by catch-up. The real game starts in the Lobby.
  • s/p of a side quest: available (p 0), active (0 <= p < goal), ready (p = goal), completed (p = goal). Goal: kill.count, 1 for item and elite. There is no failed and no abandon.
  • pinned: "main" or a side id whose state is not completed.
  • The snapshot (snapshot(state)) adds derived data, never stored: per quest {id, state, step, stepCount, progress, goal, nextStep, title, giver} under quests[id] (the stored fields stay under quests[id] too, so quests.pinned is the stored string), plus npcs: [{id, tile, marker}] and map: {markers: [...]} (section 10). ready is a state of its own; the requirement's four states are unavailable (never produced this round: every side quest is offered from the start), available, active (+ready), completed.

3. The event-driven step machine

src/core/systems/quests.js (new). Every quest change is (questState, event) -> questState in a pure reducer; the system applies it and emits the cue events. Two entry points, both deterministic:

  1. A tap on emit(). events.js emit(state, ev) calls questEvent(state, ev) after pushing the event (an ES-module import cycle events.js <-> systems/quests.js; both sides only call each other inside functions, so it is safe; test/layering.test.js only checks that core files import core files). questEvent returns at once if state.quests is missing (hand-built fixture states) and ignores every event type that starts with quest. (no re-entrancy). Because it runs inside emit, cheats, loaders and input commands feed the machine exactly like the simulation does, paused or not, and no event can be lost. Events it reacts to:
EventEffect
floorEnter {depth}main.m.depth = max(m.depth, depth); if the Lobby is entered with a ready or active item/elite quest nothing changes
stairsUnlockedmain.m.unlocked = true
bossDefeatedm.defeated = true, m.unlocked = true
keepPlayingm.verdict = true if m.defeated (leaving the victory screen = the verdict was read)
storyRead {id}id: "start" sets m.memo; id: "victory" sets m.verdict if m.defeated (section 5)
kill {target}look the monster up in state.monsters (type, summoned, quest); for each active side quest with a kill objective whose monster type and depth range match and the kill is not summoned: p += 1, ready at the goal; for an elite objective whose id equals m.quest: ready

After the reducer, the tap compares the derived main step before and after: a change emits one quest.step {id: "main", step, title, next} (a catch-up over several steps is one event, for the new step), or quest.completed {id: "main", title} when step 6 was the last. A side quest that becomes ready emits quest.step {id, title, next} (its next line now says "Return to <giver>"). Repeated or no-op events emit nothing (AC-R-254-1).

  1. Commands (inputs, applied in applyInput through one default: hook in itemCommand, so the table of intent.js gains one line): {t: "questAccept", id}, {t: "questHandIn", id}, {t: "questPin", id}, {t: "storyRead", id}. Accept and hand-in need the dialogue of the giver NPC to be open (state.ui.dialog.npc === def.giver, in the Lobby, hero within interactRange, the same gate as heal and moveStash): a hand-in to another NPC is refused ({ok: false, error: "wrong npc"}). Decline is closeDialog: no state change. questPin works anywhere in a running game; storyRead is whitelisted before the paused and not-live gates like setName (the memo and the victory screen are not live scenes) and validates its id. All commands return {ok, error?}, and emit quest.accepted {id, title, next}, quest.pinned {id}, quest.handInRefused {id, reason} or the hand-in events of section 8. The inputs are part of recorded input lists, so replays with quest actions are deterministic (AC-R-240-2).

There is no quests.talk command: talking is the existing interact input; the hook's quests.talk(npc) forwards to it. quests.abandon does not exist (AC-R-253-1).

4. nextStep and views (pure, in the core)

src/core/systems/questview.js: questView(state) (the snapshot data), nextStep(state, id), npcMarker(state, npcId), mapMarkers(state). nextStep: main active, the current step's line; side available, next.available ("Talk to the {giver} ..."); active, next.active; ready, next.ready ("Return to {giver} ..."); completed, no text. {giver} is the NPC name string of the giver. After every event the text equals the current step's line because it is computed, not stored (AC-R-242-1). The renderer and the UI call these functions on the live state; the snapshot embeds their results.

5. Step 1 event (QF-12-1) and the verdict event (QF-12-5)

  • Step 1 completes when the memo is read or on the first descent, whichever comes first. The memo is a shell overlay, so the shell reports it with the new core input {t: "storyRead", id: "start"} (sent by dismissStory when the dismissed overlay is the start story; recorded like any input). The first floorEnter with depth >= 1 completes the step too: this covers ?test=1 runs and the bot, which never show the story, and a player who skips it. The step line "Take the lift down." therefore disappears at the first of the two.
  • The verdict. The screen exists as an event source: leaving it fires keepPlaying, which the tap treats as "verdict read". Two gaps are closed: (a) a player who quits to the title from the victory screen is saved with step 6 open; (b) a migrated v3 save with the boss defeated starts at step 6 (AC-R-251-2). Both land in the Lobby with no victory screen. Decision: the journal shows a "Read the verdict" action on step 6 whenever the scene is not victory; it opens the existing story overlay with the victory text (content.story.victory, game.ui.story = "victory"), and dismissing it sends {t: "storyRead", id: "victory"}. storyRead victory is refused unless m.defeated. No new screen.

6. The quest random stream: derived and stateless, not a fifth state stream (separate, QF-12 determinism)

The quest content needs random choices in three places only: which of floors 3 or 4 holds the item, where the item and the elite stand, and which gear the rewards roll. Decision: none of them touches state.rng. Each draws from a generator seeded by a hash of fixed inputs:

questRng(seed, quest.salt, purpose, depth) = createRng(hash32(seed, 0x51535400 + salt, purpose, depth)), purpose: 1 item floor, 2 item tile, 3 elite tile, 4 reward gear, 5 reward potions.

Why not rng.quest in the state:

  • A fifth key in state.rng would change every state and every save for every run and break the strict "exactly four streams" schema check; it would also need a stored cursor that depends on the order of accepts.
  • A derived stream has no cursor: a floor regenerates identically on every entry (the existing rule), so the item and the elite stand on the same tile on every visit and after a reload; accepting sq3 before sq2 changes nothing about sq2.
  • Gameplay of a run that never accepts a quest is bit-identical: nothing draws, spawns or drops without an accepted quest (AC-R-240-2, AC-R-256-3). generateFloor itself is not touched: the hooks run after it, so generateFloor(seed, depth) is byte-identical with and without quests (the 50-seed layout comparison of AC-R-240-2 holds trivially for tiles, stairs and the spawn list).
  • Two characters on the same seed get the same reward gear. Accepted (the rolled item still depends on class tag and hero level through the reroll rule below).

The elite's drops are rolled by the normal loot stream when it dies, which is part of a run that accepted sq3; that is allowed to differ.

7. Generator hooks: the quest item and the named elite

placeQuestObjects(state) (in systems/quests.js) is called once, from enterFloor, after initFloorMap(state) and before emit(floorEnter). It is idempotent per entry and does nothing unless a quest is active.

  • Item (sq2). Conditions: sq2.s === "active", p === 0, the pouch has no qi-sq2, state.depth equals itemFloor = config.quests.item.floors[questRng(purpose 1).int(0, 1)], no ground entry with quest: "sq2" is already there (a parked floor keeps its ground list). The tile comes from the pure function questSpot(floor, rng, avoid): candidate rooms are the floor's rooms without the entry room and the exit room; a room and a tile inside it are drawn (up to 30 tries) until the tile is walkable (getCtx(state).grid.walkable, which already excludes blocking props and NPCs), is not a spawn start tile, not the entry or exit, and farther than config.safeRadius from the entry; then a scan of the same rooms in order, then any walkable tile that passes the same tests. Every walkable tile of a generated floor is reachable from the stairs (validateFloor, R-042), so any returned tile satisfies "reachable". The entry is a normal ground entry without item: {id: "qi-sq2", quest: "sq2", label, rarity: "normal", mark: "!", border: "none", color, keep: true, tile}. It is placed directly on the tile (no freeGroundTile, no mint, so nextItemId is untouched).
  • Elite (sq3). Conditions: sq3.s === "active", state.depth === config.quests.elite.depth, and no living monster with quest === "sq3". A tile from questSpot (purpose 3, the monster start tiles and the player's tile are avoided; if spawnMonster refuses the tile, the next candidate is tried). spawnMonster(state, type, tile, null, {tier: "champion", mods: [], level: elite.level, name, hpMult, quest: "sq3"}); makeMonster gains three optional options (name, hpMult, quest, about 4 lines; the champion tier gives xp x3, hp x1.5 and the champion nameplate and loot floor "at least magic"). Total hp is round(round(base x 1.5) x hpMult), at least hpMult x monsterStats(type, 4).hp (AC-R-246-4). The elite has no entry in floor.spawns, so parkFloor never counts it as killed: if the hero leaves or dies, the next entry creates exactly one again while sq3 is active; once ready or completed, never (AC-R-246-5). It is not part of the population budget (floor.spawns is unchanged).
  • Validity (AC-R-250-1). No new level, no change to generateFloor, no extra work at generation time beyond two random draws and a short scan per accepted quest; the budget assertion (genBudgetFactor) is measured by generateFloor + placeQuestObjects against generateFloor alone.

8. The pouch, the pickup and the rewards (QF-12-2)

  • Pouch = state.player.pouch, an array of {id, quest}; the quest item's name and description come from content. It is separate from inventory, stash, cursorItem, belt and equipment, so it cannot be sold (sell only finds bag items), dropped (dropCommand only finds the bag or the cursor), stashed, or lost on death, and a full bag never blocks a pickup. Invariant (checked by the save schema): an entry exists if and only if its quest is ready.
  • Pickup. takeGround (loot.js) handles entry.quest before the item path: remove the entry, push {id, quest} to the pouch, set sq.p = 1, s = "ready", emit quest.item {id, quest, name} and quest.step. Both pickup routes (click/pickup input and the walk-over order in pickups) call takeGround, and the bot's nextLoot already issues pickup for every ground entry, so no bot change is needed for the pickup. The eviction code evictOne reads e.item?.rarity (safe) and never evicts keep entries.
  • Hand-in questHandIn(state, id) is atomic: (1) checks dialogue/giver, s === "ready", the pouch entry for item quests; (2) builds the reward list: gold, xp, gear (0 or 1 item), potions (n items); (3) dry-runs the placement on a structuredClone of the bag grid with the same autoplace order the real placement uses (gear first, then potions): if anything does not fit, return {ok: false, error: "bagFull"}, emit quest.handInRefused {id, reason: "bagFull"}, and change nothing (QF-12-2: the quest stays ready, nothing is dropped on the floor, nothing is granted); (4) otherwise grant gold (giveGold), xp (gainXp, may level up), place the items (mint ids, autoplace), drop the pouch entry, set s = "completed", move pinned to main if it pointed at this quest (or to the first active/ready side quest when main is completed, else keep main), emit quest.completed {id, title, rewards: {gold, xp, items: [names]}}. A second hand-in finds s === "completed" and is refused with no effect. Potions go to the bag only (no belt logic): fewer cases, the player or the bot moves them to the belt as with any pickup.
  • Gear. Drawn from questRng(seed, salt, 4, 0), rolled by the normal generator: rollItem(rng, {depth: config.quests.gearFloor, ilvl: gearFloor * config.ilvlPerDepth, minRarity: "magic", maxRarity: "rare", slot: rng.pick(reward.gear.slots), affixTag: affixTagOf(state)}). maxRarity: "rare" keeps uniques out (no unique, uniquesFound untouched). The roll is repeated up to config.quests.rewardRerolls (8) times with the same stream until checkReqs(player, item) passes at hand-in time (a reward the hero cannot wear is a bad reward; after 8 tries the last roll stands). For the same seed, class and hero level the result is identical. sq2 slots are armour (body, head, hands, feet), sq3 is weapon. No skill or attribute point is granted by any hand-in (the reward code has no such branch).
  • Gold and xp scale with the quest's refDepth (sq1 2, sq2 and sq3 4): base + perDepth x refDepth.

9. The revisit of floors 3 and 4 for migrated v3 saves (QF-12-3)

Floors are revisitable today: every floor has a way up, enterFloor regenerates it from the seed and the placement hooks of section 7 run on every entry. Decision: no special rule. A migrated character (or a player who skipped ahead) may accept sq2 and sq3 in the Lobby and walk up the stairs to floor 3 or 4 (a long way from floor 8, but it is the same way a player returns today); the item and the elite are created on entry. The Lobby elevator is not changed (townStairsTarget stays deepest): redirecting it to a quest floor would change existing behaviour for every player. Consequences, stated rather than fixed: after a reload the floors come back with all monsters alive (existing rule), and the reward gear is level-4 gear and may be below what a deep character already wears (no retroactive power, by the customer's answer to Q6). The journal's next-step text for an open sq2 or sq3 names the floor, so the player knows where to walk. A UI fast-travel is a LATER idea, not part of this round.

10. Markers and map targets (derived, never stored)

  • npcMarker(state, npcId): "handin" if any quest of that giver is ready, else "available" if any is available, else "none". The stash keeper is always "none". The renderer calls it for the Lobby NPCs; the snapshot adds npcs[].marker.
  • mapMarkers(state): for the pinned quest only, the target of its next step if it is on the current floor and already known: the giver NPC in the Lobby (state.depth === 0, exploredAt is true for the whole Lobby), the stairs down or up of the current floor when exploredAt(exit) or exploredAt(entry) is true, the elevator in the Lobby for steps 1 and 2. Item and elite positions never appear before they have been seen (they are not "known targets"); a freshly entered floor yields []. Each marker is {quest, kind: "stairs-down" | "stairs-up" | "npc", tile, label} with a text label. Step targets are data in the step (target: {kind: "elevator" | "stairs-down" | "npc"}), so a rename or a new quest changes content only.

11. The golden hash (QF-12-4): re-pin once, with a proof

Decision: the state gains quests and player.pouch and stays hashed; the goldens (run-a.hash, the three hashes of run-class.json) are re-pinned exactly once, in package CORE-R7Q step 1, with a proof that gameplay is unchanged. Exclusion from hashState is rejected:

  • Quest state is saved state (save v4) and part of cross-engine parity (NFR-Q01, e2e/replay.mjs compares the browser hash to the Node golden); excluding it makes replay checks blind to the step machine, the pouch and the rewards, which are exactly the new things that can drift between engines.
  • ui.hud and perf are excluded because they are not simulation state; quest progress is.
  • The proof is cheap and strong: hash.js gains hashStateWithout(state, {paths, eventPrefixes}) (the existing canonical takes an optional exclusion set and an event filter). The test replays run-a.json and the per-class run, strips quests, player.pouch and any events/eventLog entry whose type starts with quest., and asserts equality with the pre-quest values, kept as test/fixtures/run-a.pre-quests.hash and run-class.pre-quests.json (copies of the goldens as AI-R7 leaves them; the proof baseline is the golden at the moment CORE-R7Q starts, not an older one). Equality holds only if the tap, the commands and the hooks change nothing for a run that never accepts a quest, which is the property the spec asks for. The same helper backs AC-R-240-2.
  • The re-pinned values go to run-a.hash and run-class.json; the reason and old/new hashes to docs/reviews/R7-core-q-notes.md. Nobody else touches them.

12. Bot

bot/quests.js (new, pure like the policy) decides quest actions from snapshot data and the public input API; bot/policy.js gets two small call sites. Path: in the Lobby before the first descent, talk to the three givers (interact) and send questAccept for each available quest; on a cleared floor 4 (all three ready, or a ready subset after floor 4) climb with useStairs up to the Lobby (floors 1 to 3 are parked with their monsters dead, so the walk is quick), interact with each giver and questHandIn, then take the elevator (townStairsTarget = deepest = 4). The kill task needs no code (the bot hunts everything), the elite is a living champion on floor 4 (the bot clears floors), the item is a ground entry (the bot's nextLoot). Hand-in refused with bagFull: the bot sells spare gear with the existing vendor logic and retries. Expected cost: about 3 to 5 minutes of game time (three floors of walking); AC-R-256-2 keeps the 20 to 40 minute window.

Options considered

  1. Per-tick scan of state.events for the step machine: no edit of events.js, but loses events emitted outside step() (cheats, loaders; step clears events first) and runs while paused never. Rejected.
  2. Call quest hooks from each producer (damage.js, boss.js, world.js, ...): four to six small edits in files other work is changing (AI-R7 in ai.js, intent.js), easy to forget on a new producer. Rejected for the single tap in emit.
  3. A stored step number instead of milestones: needs explicit catch-up code in every handler and can drift from the world; migration has to compute it anyway. Milestones are the migration's output and the step is a function of them. Chosen.
  4. A fifth stream in state.rng (rng.quest): see section 6. Rejected.
  5. Pouch as a flag on the quest (sq2.p) without an item list: the journal must list "quest items" and AC-R-246-3 names player.pouch; a list keeps the model open for a second item quest. Chosen: list.
  6. Quest item as a real bag item (kind: "quest"): full-bag problem returns, and every item validator (ITEM_KEYS, rollableOk) must learn a new kind. Rejected.
  7. Re-pin vs exclude the golden: section 11.
  8. Hand-in refusal vs drop on the floor / partial grant (QF-12-2): atomic refusal is the simplest to test and cannot lose an item. Chosen.
  9. Elevator choice or quest-floor redirect for QF-12-3: scope and behaviour change. Rejected for this round.

Consequences

  • New files: src/core/content/quests.js, src/core/systems/quests.js, src/core/systems/questview.js, bot/quests.js; new test files named in docs/reviews/R7-contract.md.
  • Edited core files: events.js (tap, 3 lines), state.js (quests, player.pouch, makeMonster options), config.js (saveVersion 4, quests), systems/world.js (one call in enterFloor), systems/loot.js (takeGround quest branch), systems/intent.js (command hook in itemCommand default, the storyRead whitelist), cheats.js (setQuestStep, completeQuest), hash.js (hashStateWithout), index.js (exports, snapshot additions). generateFloor and every file under gen/ stay as they are.
  • Save v4 and the slot index: ADR-0006 amendment "R7 quests".
  • Test goldens change once (section 11). New core events: quest.accepted, quest.step, quest.completed, quest.item, quest.pinned, quest.progress, quest.handInRefused; every consumer table is in the contract (audio, text keys, snapshot, hook list, key table, ground-entry consumers).
  • Residual risks: (1) the new champion on floor 4 must be beatable by the bot classes (balance gate); (2) the bot's walk up to the Lobby adds game time; (3) the ground entry without item meets code written for item entries (the contract lists every reader); (4) the cycle events.js <-> quests.js is benign but a future bundler change that evaluates module bodies eagerly would matter (nothing in the cycle runs at import time); (5) a deep migrated character gets level-4 gear (accepted).

Feasibility check (owning package, L-026)

Read and confirmed on 2026-10-14; the owning package re-confirms by test before relying on each line:

  • Tap in emit: emit is the only writer of state.events (grep "events.push" finds only events.js); killMonster sets m.ai = "dead" before emit(kill); enterFloor sets state.depth before emit(floorEnter). CORE-R7Q checks by a test that a cheat.teleportFloor made while paused moves the main step.
  • placeQuestObjects needs getCtx(state).grid, state.floor.rooms, floor.spawns, floor.entry/exit: all present on generated, fallback and arena floors (arena has no rooms list use: hook returns early for depth >= config.bossDepth and for floor.custom).
  • spawnMonster forwards opts to makeMonster; the three new options are read there. A prepared test floor (floor.custom) gets no quest objects.
  • Reward placement: autoplace/findSpot are pure on a grid copy; potions and gear use mint so ids are fresh (nextItemId).
  • storyRead before the live gate: applyInput has the same pattern for setName (R5 fix, CR-10).
  • Stairs up exist on every floor 1 to 8 and takeStairs(up) calls enterFloor(d - 1, {at: "exit"}).
  • Save: check()/schemaProblem strictness and migrate chain are detailed in the ADR-0006 amendment; feasibility owner CORE-R7Q (save part).
  • Render and UI readers of ground entries: see the consumer table in the contract; owners WORLD-R7Q (render/fx.js, render/world.js) and UI-R7Q (game.js hover) confirm they tolerate an entry without item.

Questions for the customer (L-05)

None block the design; all are content or scope and escalated by the spec already: (1) three side quests or more, (2) the working titles and the six step lines, (3) whether quests should hand out gear (the pacing tool for the floor 5 step) or only gold and experience. The design fits each answer: more quests are content plus sideCount, new text is content/quests.js only, gold-only rewards are reward.gear removed.

Amendment 2026-10-14 (R7-4: three main quests and five side quests)

Source: customer decision 8 (../00-brief.md, "Customer decisions (user, 2026-10-14)": "do 3 quests and 5 sidequests"), item 7 (keep the working names and texts), item 6 (spread the difficulty over the floors; the numbers are a later balance package, R7-3). Spec addendum: ../30-spec/12-quests-journal.md section "Addendum R7-4" (15 ACs, AC-R-257-1..259-5). Packages: ../50-plan.md R7-4.1 and R7-4.2. Owner: architect. Where this section differs from the text above, this section wins. It is written against the code of 2026-10-14 and the fix round FIX-R7-CORE / FIX-R7-UI that runs now; R7-4 starts on top of both (overlaps at the end).

A1. The three main quests are derived, not stored

Decision: no stored state is added for the main quests. state.quests.main.m keeps the five milestones (memo, depth, unlocked, defeated, verdict); all three arcs read the same milestones. The key stays main and now means "the story milestones"; main2 and main3 have no stored entry.

  • Content: content.quests.main, main2, main3 (kind: "main", arc: 1..3, title, blurb, unlock line, steps[]). Each step gains when, a data predicate: {milestone: "memo" | "unlocked" | "defeated" | "verdict"} or {depth: N}. New exports: content.mainIds = ["main","main2","main3"], content.mainSteps (the three step lists concatenated, each with arc and a global index 1..10), questIds = [...mainIds, ...sideIds].
  • mainDone(m) becomes generic: raw[i] = predicate(step i), done[i] = OR(raw[i..end]) (a later step implies the earlier ones: this is the existing catch-up rule, now over ten steps). mainStep(m) is the global step 1..10, 11 when all are done; MAIN_STEPS is 10. Arc state is a function of it: arc k is completed when all its steps are done, active when it holds the first undone step, unavailable otherwise (this is the first time unavailable is produced; the journal shows it as locked). Because done is a suffix-OR, an arc can only be active when every earlier arc is completed: the next arc unlocks exactly when the previous completes, and a catch-up (cheat, migration, an old save) can never leave an arc open behind a finished one.
  • Step table (the six existing lines are kept word for word, customer item 7; four steps are new working text, ../30-spec/12-quests-journal.md addendum table):
ArcStepCompletesLine
1 main "Why the Lights Went Out"1 memomemo (or first descent)Take the lift down.
2 dark-floordepth 1Reach floor 1 and look for what cut the power.
3 cables (new)depth 3Follow the power cables down to floor 3.
2 main2 "The Paper Trail"1 go-deeperdepth 4Reach floor 4. Visit the Lobby first: the staff may pay in gear.
2 records (new)depth 5Reach floor 5 and look for where the paperwork goes.
