Arc boundaries are data (when and the grouping): moving a boundary, for example arc 2 ending on floor 5, is a content edit.

  • Cues. changeMain (the tap) compares the global step before and after. For every arc that became complete it emits quest.completed {id, title, rewards} in arc order; then, if some arc is still open, one quest.step {id: <active arc>, step: <step within the arc>, title: <arc title>, next, unlocked: true|undefined} (unlocked: true when the active arc changed, so the toast can say "new assignment"). A catch-up over several arcs is therefore one completed per finished arc plus one step; a repeated event emits nothing. No new event type: test/audio.test.js (which fails on unmapped events) and the cue table stay valid; quest.step gains the optional field unlocked.
  • Pinning. pinned may be an active arc id, or a side quest that is not completed; when everything is done main3 stays pinned (it keeps the journal valid). questPin {id: "main"} is kept as an alias for "the active main arc" and is stored resolved (old tests, e2e and the journal's pin control keep working). Pinning a locked or completed arc is refused (locked, already done). When the pinned arc completes, the tap moves pinned to the next active arc (or, after the last arc, to the first open side quest, else main3) and emits quest.pinned. handInQuest uses the same helper (replacing its stateOf(state, "main") === "active" test).
  • Arc rewards (customer goal: pacing on floors 5 to 8). Arcs 1 and 2 pay gold and experience only, automatically, once, in the tap at the moment the arc completes (config.quests.arc.main, .main2: refDepth, gold {base, perDepth}, xp {base, perDepth}; same formula as the side quests). Arc 3 pays nothing (the victory is the reward). No item, so there is no bag problem and no hand-in trip; skill and attribute points are never granted. Because the grant is the effect of the transition, a load, a migration or a snapshot never pays (no retroactive reward), a catch-up pays each finished arc once, and a milestone only grows so it cannot pay twice. questEvent runs inside emit; gainXp may emit levelup, which the tap ignores (it only reacts to the listed types), so there is no re-entrancy.

A2. Five side quests: the objective kinds are generalised, no new kind

Today the objective numbers are global (config.quests.kill, .item, .elite) and sq2 and sq3 are special-cased by id (qi-sq2, itemFloorOf). Decision: every side quest names its own objective config; the three kinds kill, item, elite stay the only kinds, so no new system is needed.

  • objCfg(id) = config.quests[id][type] ?? config.quests[type]: sq1..sq3 keep reading the global blocks (their numbers and tests do not move), sq4 and sq5 carry their own block. reduceSide, goalOf, itemFloorOf(seed, id), placeQuestObjects (a loop over all active item and elite quests), the pouch entry id (qi-<id>), rewardOf and the save schema's goal and world-flag checks read it. placeQuestObjects stays idempotent, draws only from questRng(seed, salt, purpose, depth) and never from state.rng; salts 4 and 5 are new, so sq1..sq3 draw the same numbers as before.
  • sq4 "The Misfiled Ledger" (item, giver stash, the Storage Locker, which was the only Lobby NPC without a quest): one ledger on floor 5 or 6 (config.quests.sq4.item.floors [5, 6], chosen by questRng(seed, 4, 1, 0)), into the pouch. It can sit in the pouch together with the sq2 badge (the pouch already allows one entry per quest; the schema bound is sideIds.length).
  • sq5 "Slide Deck Surplus" (kill, giver vendor): defeat 6 Consultants on floors 5 and 6 (config.quests.sq5.kill {monster "consultant", count 6, depths [5, 6]}; the Consultant is the new ranged type of floor 5, minDepth 5). Satisfiability: the kill task inherits the FIX-R7-CORE rule for CR7-01 (an accepted kill quest must be completable after the floors were already cleared in this session); R7-4.1 applies it per quest through objCfg. A new validity test asserts that floors 5 and 6 of 100 seeds together spawn at least count Consultants; if the generator budget makes that false for some seeds, lower count (config), never the rule.
  • Givers. The Lobby has four NPCs and three already give a quest, so "the remaining Lobby NPCs" is one: stash. The fifth quest therefore goes to a second quest from an existing giver (vendor, whose first quest is over by floor 2). npcMarker already loops over all quests of a giver; the dialogue lists every non-completed quest of the giver (UI, R7-4.2). giver is data, so a customer wish for a sixth Lobby character (question 1) changes giver plus the NPC work below, nothing in the machine. Cost of a new NPC, for the decision: npcs.js entry and two strings.js keys, a spot in gen/town.js (changes the Lobby layout and therefore the golden once more), a sprite and portrait (WORLD), hit and interact tests, the town tests; about 250 lines plus art, its own package R7-4.3.
  • Why no new kind. Candidates and their cost, if the customer wants more variety: "clear a floor" needs a new floorCleared core event (all spawns of the floor dead; about 40 lines plus tests, and a definition of cleared on a parked floor), "collect N items" needs N ground entries and a counted pouch (about 80 lines; the pouch entry becomes {id, quest, n} and the schema changes), "reach a floor" is the main quests' job. Each also changes the save schema, so it would be a v6 matter.
  • Rewards (config, all tunable by R7-3):
QuestGold / xp (base + perDepth x refDepth)GearPotions
main arc 120+10x3 = 50 / 20+15x3 = 65nonenone
main2 arc 220+10x6 = 80 / 20+15x6 = 110nonenone
sq430+15x5 = 105 / 30+15x5 = 105none2 (ilvl of floor 5)
sq530+15x6 = 120 / 30+15x6 = 120one piece, minRarity = maxRarity = "magic", slot in ["ring","amulet","belt"], ilvl = 6 x ilvlPerDepthnone

reward.gearFloor becomes per quest (config.quests.sqN.gearFloor, default config.quests.gearFloor 4; sq4 5, sq5 6) and rarity {min, max} per quest (default magic to rare), both read by rewardOf; rewardSummary(id) (FIX-R7-CORE, CR7-05) must return {gold, xp, potions, gear: {slots, minRarity, maxRarity}|null} and R7-4.1 extends it for the arcs and the new quests, so the UI never recomputes. The gear roll follows FIX-R7-CORE CR7-06 (candidate rolls are seed-pure; checkReqs only picks among them).

  • How the rewards keep the classes inside the band (R6: clear-time and mean-deaths band of 25 % between the class medians, test/balance-gate.test.js, bot/parity.mjs): (1) gold, experience and potions are the same numbers for every class; (2) the only new gear is one magic jewellery or belt piece, which carries no weapon damage and no armour base, has fewer affixes than the rare floor-4 armour and weapon of sq2 and sq3 (the existing gear quests are not touched), and is rolled by the same affixTagOf(state) class rule as every drop, so each class gets the same count of affixes useful to it; (3) a relation test caps the new experience: sum(new xp) <= config.quests.newXpShare x xpTable[config.quests.balanceLevel - 1] (defaults 0.10 and 12, today 400 of 4356 = 9.2 %, so adding quests cannot silently become a levelling shortcut); (4) the parity run (24 seeds x 3 classes, quests on) must keep every class inside the existing band, and the shift of each class median caused by the quests (quests on minus quests off) may differ between classes by at most 5 points, so no class gains more than another. Power per floor: the new gear is magic at ilvl 18 against rare at ilvl 12 for the old pieces; the new gold, experience and potions are small steps spread over floors 3, 6 and 6 to 8 instead of one block at floor 4.
  • Where the help lands (floors 5 to 8). Floor 3: arc 1 pays (65 xp). Floor 4 and the Lobby trip T1: sq1..sq3 pay as before (the existing floor-5 gear). Floors 5 and 6: the ledger and the Consultants give a reason to explore both floors fully (the loot and xp of those floors are the main pacing resource) and arc 2 pays on reaching floor 6 (110 xp). Trip T2 (below) pays sq4 and sq5 before floor 7. The boundary of arc 2 (floor 6) and the objective floors are config and content, so the balance package can move the help toward floor 5 (for example the ledger on floor 5 only, arc 2 ending on floor 5) without touching the machine.

A3. State shape and migration: save version 5 (decision)

State after R7-4: state.quests = { main: {m}, sq1..sq5: {s, p}, pinned } plus state.player.pouch (entries {id: "qi-sq2"|"qi-sq4", quest}). Changes against v4: two new keys sq4 and sq5; the domain of pinned; nothing else.

Decision: bump to saveVersion 5 with MIGRATIONS[4], instead of loading v4 with defaults. Reasons: (1) schemaProblem demands exactly the quest keys; accepting a block with or without sq4/sq5 inside one version weakens the one strictness the save layer has (ADV-R7 relied on it); (2) an older build (v4) reading a v5 slot reports newer and never overwrites it, whereas a v5 save under the version number 4 would be judged corrupt and could be replaced; (3) pinned needs a real transform (below); (4) the v3 to v4 step is unchanged and the chain stays pure and idempotent. The cost is one migration and the fixtures.

MIGRATIONS[4](d): pure; d.version >= 5 returns d; otherwise quests = {...d.quests, sq4: {s: "available", p: 0}, sq5: {s: "available", p: 0}}, pinned = canonical(d.quests.pinned, m) where a "main" pin becomes the active arc derived from m (main while arc 1 is open, main2, main3, and main3 when everything is done), a side id is kept, anything malformed is left for the schema check. pouch, m and every other field are untouched, no reward is paid, and the new quests start available (they are offered at the next Lobby visit; a deep character may accept sq4/sq5 and walk up to floor 5 or 6 by the rule of section 9). A migrated character's arcs are simply derived: depth 4 shows arc 1 completed and arc 2 at step 2 (floor 5), a boss-defeated save shows arcs 1 and 2 completed and arc 3 at "Read the verdict"; none of the arc rewards is paid.

Schema (format.js, extends ADV-R7-01's fix): quests has exactly main, sq1..sq5, pinned, pouch; pinned is the id of the active arc (or main3 when all are done) or a side quest that is not completed; sq4 ready/completed implies deepestDepth >= min(config.quests.sq4.item.floors) and, for the pouch rule, the entry exists iff ready; sq5 ready/completed implies stats.kills >= count and deepestDepth >= min(depths); the pouch bound stays sideIds.length; the block stays well below 400 characters. loadSave sets quests before the resume enterFloor as before. The slot card reads the milestones through the same functions.

Slot index (ADR-0006 amendment point 6): mainStep becomes the global step 1..10 (the card shows the step title from content.mainSteps and, as before, "N/sideCount" with N 0..5), mainDone means all three arcs are done, sidesDone is 0..5. Entries written by a v4 build carry mainStep on the old 1..6 scale: they get a new optional field qv: 5, and upgradeIndex (already called on load) treats an ok entry without qv: 5 as stale and rebuilds it from its text through the migration; a failed rebuild keeps the old entry (card without quest text, no crash). Index v stays 2.

A4. Golden hash: re-pinned once more, proof unchanged

The state gains quests.sq4 and quests.sq5 for every run, so run-a.hash and the three hashes of run-class.json change, once, in R7-4.1 step 1, with the reason and old and new values in docs/reviews/R7-4-core-notes.md. The proof is the existing one (section 11): hashStateWithout strips quests, player.pouch and quest.* events, and the result must equal the pre-quest baselines run-a.pre-quests.hash and run-class.pre-quests.json, which stay as they are (the stripped subtree is the only thing R7-4 adds). Two guards: (1) the proof test asserts that the recorded runs never reach floor 3 (m.depth < 3, no arc completed), because from floor 3 on an arc pays gold and experience and the stripped hash would legitimately differ; if a golden run ever reaches floor 3 the test fails with a message that the arc rewards must be zeroed by config in the proof (config.quests.arc.* set to 0 in the test copy of the config); (2) CR7-02 (FIX-R7-CORE) asks for a second recorded run that changes floors and picks up loot; R7-4.1 uses that second golden too and the zeroed-arc-reward variant of the proof for it, since it does reach floor 3 or deeper. Nobody else touches the goldens.

A5. The bot's route

bot/quests.js stays pure; the changes are small:

  1. Lobby, before the first descent: storyRead start, then talk to all four NPCs and accept all five quests (the vendor twice: after the first accept the dialogue stays open and pending() yields the second quest; the existing at = todo.find(...) already handles two quests of one giver). The stash keeper is now a stop.
  2. Floors 1 to 4: as today (interns, badge, Toner Tyrant). Main arc 1 completes on entering floor 3.
  3. Trip T1 from floor 4 (cleared, any of sq1..sq3 ready): climb, hand in at vendor, healer, potion seller (the vendor's sq5 is not ready yet), elevator to floor 4.
  4. Floors 5 and 6: the ledger is a ground entry (nextLoot), the Consultants die in the normal loop. Arc 2 completes on entering floor 6.
  5. Trip T2 from floor 6 (cleared and sq4 or sq5 ready; also any quest still ready from T1, which makes ADV-R7-03's missed badge recoverable): climb to the Lobby, hand in at the stash keeper and the vendor, elevator to floor 6 (townStairsTarget is the deepest floor), continue on 7 and 8.
  6. QBOT.climbDepth (4) becomes QBOT.trips = [{depth: 4, ids: ["sq1","sq2","sq3"]}, {depth: 6, ids: ["sq4","sq5"]}] with a per-stage counter in the memory; questTrip picks the stage whose floor is the current one and whose ids (plus any other ready quest) are ready; QBOT.climbDepth is removed (R7-4.1 greps for it). A trip is skipped when the run's profile.depth ends at or above that floor, as now.
  7. Arc 3's "Read the verdict" is the keepPlaying input of run-headless (unchanged). bot/report.js counts arc events per arc id (today it filters id === "main"), and reports trips and trip ticks per stage.

Cost: T2 climbs six parked floors and descends by the elevator: expected +2 to +4 minutes of game time (measured in R7-4.1; T1 climbs four floors and costs about 3 to 5 by ADR-0007 section 12's estimate). The run must stay in the R-006 window of 20 to 40 minutes (median today 26 to 27). Fallbacks, in this order: both sq4 and sq5 objectives on floor 5 only (trip T2 from floor 5), or T2 only when quest rewards are worth it for the bot's profile; a fast-travel option for the player is a LATER customer item.

A6. Options considered (R7-4)

  1. Separate stored milestones per arc (main2: {m}): duplicates the same facts three times and needs its own catch-up; rejected for derived arcs over one milestone block.
  2. One main quest with three chapters: the customer asked for three quests (journal shows three, each completes and unlocks the next, each can pay); rejected.
  3. Arc rewards by hand-in to an NPC: adds one more Lobby trip for the bot and the player, and bag-full cases; rejected for automatic gold and experience (no item).
  4. Rewarding arcs with gear: would double the pacing items before floor 5 and open the class-band question for the weapon slot; rejected, gold and experience only.
  5. v4 with defaults: see A3, rejected. 6. New NPC for sq5 vs a second quest on the vendor: see A2; the second quest is the default, the new NPC is open for the customer. 7. A new objective kind: see A2, not needed.

A7. Consequences and overlaps

  • Edited files (R7-4.1): content/quests.js (three arcs, sq4, sq5, when, mainIds, mainSteps), questview.js (generic mainDone, arc state, questView for arcs, nextStep, mapMarkers for any active arc), systems/quests.js (changeMain with arcs and rewards, reduceSide and placeQuestObjects per quest, questPin alias, hand-in pin helper), cheats.js (setQuestStep(id, n) takes an arc id and a step within the arc; completeQuest("main3") completes everything; the duplicated changeMain copy there calls the shared function), config.js (sideCount 5, arc, sq4, sq5, newXpShare, balanceLevel, saveVersion 5), core/index.js (exports), save/format.js, save/migrate.js, save/slots.js (qv, upgradeIndex), bot/quests.js, bot/policy.js (two call sites), bot/report.js, goldens. Not touched: gen/**, events.js, state.js (except newQuestState's two keys through content), audio.
  • Overlaps with the packages running now (R7-4 starts after both hand back): FIX-R7-CORE owns the same files src/core/systems/quests.js (CR7-01 kill satisfiability, CR7-06 gear candidate rolls), src/core/content/quests.js (none expected), src/core/config.js, src/save/format.js (ADV-R7-01 forged states: the new schema rules extend its comparison table), bot/quests.js and bot/policy.js (ADV-R7-03 badge and trip), test/fixtures/** (CR7-02 second golden), rewardSummary (CR7-05). FIX-R7-UI owns src/ui/journal.js, questdialog.js, game.js toast queue, e2e/r7quest.mjs and the reward text switch to rewardSummary. R7-4.1 and R7-4.2 rebase on their results and re-read the contract names; R7-contract.md gets an addendum row per file only if a name changes. R7-3 (pace) follows R7-4 on the finished content.
  • Residual risks: (1) bot time with trip T2 (A5); (2) Consultant count on floors 5 and 6 (validity test, count is config); (3) the vendor with two quests is new in the dialogue UI (R7-4.2); (4) arc rewards add xp on the way to the golden runs of CR7-02's second golden (zeroed in the proof); (5) a quest reward that pays inside emit is new (the tap already mutated state, it now also pays; reviewed by test: pay-once, catch-up, no pay on load); (6) text is working text, escalated again for the four new step lines, two new quests and two arc titles.
